message.content:
Context: I'm helping Marcel revise a document at /Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/Zimmermann_Frontend_Lead_Playbook.md. He's an Angular/Nx engineer at Accenture stepping up as Frontend Lead on a Salesforce PWA Kit commerce migration for Zimmermann (a luxury fashion brand), working out of the repo at /Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa. The playbook was distilled from a generic AI-engineering training week (Claude.ai + Claude Code methodology, taught on a throwaway Next.js/Tailwind/Contentful practice project called "TelcoNow") and its closing section (§16, "Bridge to Zimmermann") speculatively maps that generic methodology onto the real Zimmermann project — but it explicitly flags that mapping as "a starting hypothesis... from separate context (the solution deck), not from the training... to confirm against your actual repo," because whoever wrote it hadn't actually read this codebase. My job now is to read the actual repo and find where each generic concept really lands, so the playbook can cite real files/skills/paths instead of speculation.

I already have full text of these files loaded from earlier reading — do NOT re-read or re-summarize them in detail, just reference them by name/path where relevant to a mapping: AGENTS.md (root), .claude/rules/conventions.md, .claude/rules/testing.md, .claude/rules/protectedFiles.md, .claude/rules/frozenFiles.md. I also already know the top-level directory listing and the 14 skill folder names under .claude/skills/ (audit-tier, code-quality, contentful-drift-check, contentful-register-component, feature-spec, generate-changelog, new-component, onboarding, pr-checklist, project-init, qa-generate, scope-check, session-start, upstream-sync-review) and the .docs/ file listing, but have NOT read their contents yet.

Please read, in full, and report back on:

1. **Two-squad structure**: `.claude/rules/squadA.md` and `.claude/rules/squadB.md` in full — what's the real RACI/ownership split? (protectedFiles.md already shows some "Owner: Squad A/B" tags — connect those.)
2. **All 14 skill definitions**: read every `.claude/skills/*/SKILL.md`. For each, give a one-line "what it actually does" — I need to know which ones are real, working operationalizations of playbook concepts like: the "planning layer"/gap-hunting (compare against feature-spec), the "story skill" for scaffolding a component+story (compare against new-component — and separately, note that qa-generate turns Jira stories into Gherkin/Playwright, which is a DIFFERENT sense of "story" than a component-build story; flag that terminology collision explicitly), the "hardening checklist" (compare against code-quality, pr-checklist), "build-log.md" memory-at-session-start (compare against session-start), scaffolding discipline / one-time setup (compare against project-init, onboarding), the tier system (compare against audit-tier, scope-check), and anything with no playbook equivalent at all (generate-changelog, upstream-sync-review, contentful-register-component, contentful-drift-check) — describe those too, since the Lead should know they exist even if the playbook never mentioned them.
3. **Living memory files**: read all of `.docs/memory/*.md` (projectState.md, feedback.md, sprintScope.md, references.md, upstreamBaseline.md). Does anything here function as the playbook's imagined "build-log.md"? Does `feedback.md` already implement the playbook's §9.6 "push corrections into the rules layer" loop?
4. **`.docs/planning/sharedAiBrainBrief.md`** — read this in full; it sounds like it may be the actual project-specific "planning layer" design doc. High priority.
5. **Is there a real component registry?** Search for anything registry-like (a markdown file listing built components, or does Storybook + the Contentful component definitions serve that function instead via contentful-register-component/contentful-drift-check). Be honest if no direct §9.4 "component-registry.md" equivalent exists.
6. **Real prompt templates**: read `.docs/prompts/omsIntClaudeCodePrompt.md`, `.docs/prompts/claudeCodeSitPrompt.md`, `.docs/prompts/qaClaudeCodeSetup.md` — are these concrete instances of the playbook's §9.5 "build prompt pattern"?
7. **Open items**: read `.docs/temp/openItems.md` — does this match the playbook's "keep an open-items list visible" suggestion?
8. **Integrations reality check**: skim `.docs/vendor/*.md` and `.docs/temp/integration/*.md` (numbered 01-18) — the playbook claims "14 integrations and four connector patterns routing through MuleSoft." Count what's actually there and note if that number is accurate, stale, or unverifiable from these docs.
9. **`.docs/agents-proposals/README.md`** — read it; likely describes planned/future AI-agent work relevant to a "multiply the team" angle.
10. Skim `.docs/architecture.md`, `.docs/releaseBranchesRules.md`, `.docs/upstreamPolicy.md`, `.docs/temp/tsd-architecture.md`, and root `CODEOWNERS` — just enough to describe the real branch/release/CI-CD workflow in a sentence or two, to check against the playbook's generic "CI-CD gates; Digital SIT; NewStore SIT" claims.

This is read-only research — do not edit any files. Output a dense, structured report: for each playbook concept above, state (a) confirmed real equivalent with exact path, (b) a partial/different equivalent with the gap explained, or (c) no equivalent found (still aspirational). Separately list any concrete facts that contradict specific playbook claims (integration count, squad names, tool names, etc.) so they can be corrected, and flag any real repo capabilities the playbook doesn't mention at all but a Frontend Lead should know about. Prioritize precision on file paths and skill/file names over prose — this feeds directly into rewriting a leadership document.

Triggers on phrases like 'implement this Figma design in SwiftUI', 'build this screen in Swift', 'push this SwiftUI view to Figma', 'mirror my Swift code in a Figma file', or whenever a Figma URL appears alongside `.swift` files / an `.xcodeproj`. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- verify: Verify that a code change actually does what it's supposed to by exercising it end-to-end and observing behavior — drive the affected flow, not just tests or typecheck. Run before committing nontrivial changes; bootstraps this repo's project verify skill if none exists yet. Don't invoke it on a diff that only touches tests, docs, or other code with no runtime surface to drive (a change to product source always has one) — there's nothing to observe.
- code-review: Review the current diff for correctness bugs and reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings). Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review.
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- audit-tier: Identify the protection tier, owner, and import blast radius of a file or directory under overrides/. Use before editing anything you're unsure about. (from zimmermann-pwa/.claude/skills — applies when working on files under zimmermann-pwa/)
- code-quality: Audit recently changed or specified files for code quality issues — naming, circular imports, TypeScript coverage, test/story existence, and structural debt. Read-only. Use after implementing a feature or before opening a PR. (from zimmermann-pwa/.claude/skills — applies when working on files under zimmermann-pwa/)
- contentful-drift-check: Check for drift between React component props and their Contentful Studio component definitions. Use when a developer wants to verify definitions are still in sync after props have changed, or to audit all registered components at once. (from zimmermann-pwa/.claude/skills — applies when working on files under zimmermann-pwa/)
- contentful-register-component: Register a Zimmermann React component with Contentful Studio Experiences. Use when a developer asks to register, add, or expose a React component to Contentful, or when they need to create a Contentful component definition for an existing component. (from zimmermann-pwa/.claude/skills — applies when working on files under zimmermann-pwa/)
- feature-spec: Turn a plain-English feature request into a scoped implementation plan before any code is written. Asks one clarifying question at a time, then produces a spec Claude Code can execute safely. Use this before starting any non-trivial implementation session. Minor residual points to confirm with Tryzens: `channel.type` values for online orders (sample data only shows in-store); whether the returns endpoint supports `offset`/`count` pagination; the `shop.id` inconsistency between list (`"storefront-catalog-eu"`) and detail (`"ZIMMERMANN_LONDON_STORE"`) responses; the full set of `psp` values for online payment methods (sample shows `"cash"` and `"store_credit"` only).
4. **CAI-023 — warehouse + boutique stock aggregation for browse-level availability.** Confirm whether MuleSoft can deliver a pre-aggregated available-to-promise figure combining warehouse and eligible boutique stock, to drive the Add to Bag / Back Soon / Out of Stock states on PDP and PLP. If MuleSoft cannot pre-aggregate, the storefront must decide whether to request both sources separately and aggregate client-side (extra round-trip) or fall back to SFCC-only inventory. This is distinct from the cart → checkout entry stock check (CAI-034) and the Find in Boutique flyout (CAI-038), both of which have their own endpoints. **Owner:** Integration team (Tryzens / MuleSoft).

## 4. Omneo

No Omneo-issued identifiers, hosts, or credentials are currently in Accenture's possession. All three items below are needed before implementation can begin against a real Omneo tenant; all three are hard blockers.

Omneo documents embedding the Profile Portal as an iframe dialog — so the embed itself is a supported Omneo capability. However, Omneo's documented embed is a Shopify theme extension that authenticates via the Omneo CX Shopify app proxy, which a PWA does not have. Confirm, for the non-Shopify embed on Zimmermann's plan: the Profile Portal embed URL, how the Communication Preferences and region/country selection views are scoped within it, and the auth handshake outside Shopify (a customer-scoped signed-URL / HMAC approach, or a server-minted customer-scoped token). If no embed path is available, the fallback is a redirect to the hosted portal or a native rebuild against Omneo's API.
2. **Omneo identifiers and embed URL.** Provide the values needed to construct the iFrame `src` for production and each non-production environment:

3. **HMAC signing secret (or token mechanism).** Provide the per-environment secret/credential Omneo issues for the customer-scoped embed auth. Without it the Omneo ID proxy authentication cannot be exercised end-to-end; until it is provided, the integration can only be developed against a mock.

Without this contract the storefront cannot implement the call against a real MuleSoft instance. **Owner:** MuleSoft — GiveX supplies the underlying failure-code list; Zimmermann owns the final customer-facing message copy.
2. **Per-environment MuleSoft endpoint, API token, and rate-limit thresholds.** MuleSoft to supply, per environment: MuleSoft host, balance-check endpoint path, MuleSoft API token, and the agreed per-IP / per-session rate-limit thresholds and the bot-management vendor in front of the MRT route. **Owner:** MuleSoft (host / token / thresholds); the MRT-edge WAF / bot / rate-limit config is ours.
3. **Whether the balance-check route uses a CAPTCHA.** Confirm whether the MRT balance-check route should present a CAPTCHA challenge when the bot manager elevates a request — this is not yet decided. If a CAPTCHA is used, the simplest option is Google reCAPTCHA v3, reusing the site key already provisioned for register / login (no new provisioning). **Owner:** Zimmermann.

## 6. Booxi

Boutique appointment history is a PWA-direct read (PWA → MRT → Booxi); scope and timeline are TBC.

1. **Storefront scope and timeline (CRM-165 – CRM-167).** Confirm whether the My Account appointments surface is read-only history (current assumption) or whether in-storefront booking / rescheduling / cancellation is also in scope, and confirm the target sprint. Until confirmed, the section is built read-only and structured to slot in without redesign.

3. **Customer-identification mechanism (PWA-direct path).** Confirm how the storefront proves customer identity to Booxi without allowing the browser to retrieve an arbitrary customer's appointments — whether a Booxi customer ID is stored on the SFCC / Omneo profile (and how it is populated), or whether MRT must look the customer up in Booxi at request time. The mechanism must prevent impersonation.
4. **Per-environment Booxi credentials.** Booxi to supply, per environment: Booxi API host, API credential, and the credential rotation cadence and named owner. Note the API host is region-specific (e.g. a North America vs EU base URL), so confirm which regional host serves Zimmermann.

## 7. Adyen

1. **Apple Pay and Google Pay merchant IDs.** Provide the Apple Pay and Google Pay merchant IDs per domain. Needed before the wallet buttons can be switched on. **Owner:** Zimmermann.
2. **Per-environment Adyen credentials.** Provide, for each environment (Dev / SIT / Stage / UAT / Prod): client key, API key, HMAC key, merchant account ID per region, and whether it's a test or live Adyen account. Without these, checkout can't be tested against a real Adyen account.
## 8. Global-e

Neither can be guessed; both are needed before the iframe can be built.

2. **Order fields for international orders.** Confirm what order fields the PWA will receive for a Global-e order, to decide between rendering full order detail or a "View on tracking page" fallback. Full detail needs: line items, totals in both shopper and base currency, shipping address, and fulfilment status.

## 9. Google Maps

1. **Google Cloud Platform (GCP) project and per-environment API keys.** Zimmermann to provision one Places API key per environment (Dev / SIT / Stage / UAT / Prod). Without the keys the integration cannot be exercised against a real Google account.

## 10. reCAPTCHA

1. **Per-environment reCAPTCHA site key and secret key.** Zimmermann to provision a Google Cloud project (or use an existing one) and register reCAPTCHA v3 keys for each environment's domain. Supply `RECAPTCHA_SITE_KEY` (public) and `RECAPTCHA_SECRET_KEY` (server-only, for MRT token verification) per environment (Dev / SIT / Stage / UAT / Prod). Without these, bot protection cannot be exercised against a real Google account.

2. **Didomi consent category and vendor / feature ID (EU and UK storefronts only).** reCAPTCHA is consent-gated in EU and UK. Zimmermann Privacy to confirm which Didomi consent category covers reCAPTCHA (no obvious prior — the purpose is bot protection, not analytics or marketing). Tell No Lies to then provide the corresponding Didomi vendor or feature ID so the consent-gated script loader can be wired correctly. **Owner:** Zimmermann Privacy / Tell No Lies.

## 11. Narvar

1. **Per-environment Narvar retailer ID and CONVERT API key.** Provide one set per environment (Dev / SIT / Stage / UAT / Prod). Without these the widget cannot be exercised against a real Narvar account.

2. **Didomi consent category for Narvar Promise.** Confirm which Didomi category the CONVERT widget falls under (Performance?). This determines whether the widget loads for EU and UK users who accept Performance cookies but decline Analytics or Marketing.

## 12. Didomi

1. **Didomi purpose / vendor IDs.** Provide the Didomi purpose IDs backing the storefront's consent categories (Performance, Analytics, Marketing — REG-051). Also provide Didomi vendor IDs if applicable.
2. **Notice IDs per environment.** Zimmermann to provision the Didomi Notices per environment (Dev / SIT / Stage / UAT / Prod) and supply the Notice IDs so they can be wired into the per-environment configuration. Without these IDs the SDK cannot be exercised end-to-end against a real Didomi configuration.

## 13. GTM (with Tell No Lies/Zimm)

1. **Addingwell tagging-server URL (per environment).** The production first-party subdomain is confirmed as `ruffles.zimmermann.com` (2026-06-09). Zimmermann/Accenture to provision the equivalent first-party host for each non-production environment (each must be first-party to that environment's storefront domain). The PWA points the loader at this URL.
2. **Data layer schema confirmation.** The data layer is a single shared artifact. Tell No Lies to confirm the storefront's proposed event and attribute schema (page views, product impressions, add-to-cart, begin-checkout, purchase and related ecommerce events, plus consent state and user identifiers) satisfies both GTM's own tags (GA4, Meta) and the frontend-direct data-layer consumers (Optimizely, Crazy Egg — not GTM tags). Any additional attributes Optimizely needs for segmentation (AAB-004) or Crazy Egg needs for filtering (AAB-005) must be raised at this point.

## 14. Inside Chat

No open items — PWA has zero Inside-Chat work.

## 15. Optimizely (with Zimm/TNL)

Optimizely Web is a frontend-direct script (not in GTM), gated on Didomi consent.

1. **Didomi consent category and vendor / feature ID.** Zimmermann Privacy to confirm which Didomi consent category covers Optimizely (expected: Analytics). Tell No Lies to then provide the corresponding Didomi vendor or feature ID so the consent-gated loader can be wired correctly.

## 16. Crazy Egg (with Zimm/TNL)

Crazy Egg (heatmaps / session recording) is a frontend-direct script (not in GTM), gated on Didomi consent (category TBC — Zimmermann Privacy to confirm).

1. **Crazy Egg account / site ID per environment.** Zimmermann to provide the account / site ID (script), confirming whether a single account serves all environments or one per tier.
2. **Masking configuration ownership.** Confirm that Tell No Lies owns and applies the session-recording masking configuration (payment and PII fields suppressed) inside the Crazy Egg application. The storefront-side scope is confirmed (AAB-005): the PWA populates the data layer and renders maskable fields with stable selectors; masking itself is outside the PWA.
3. **Didomi consent category and vendor / feature ID.** Zimmermann Privacy to confirm which Didomi consent category covers Crazy Egg (expected: Analytics). Tell No Lies to then provide the corresponding Didomi vendor or feature ID so the consent-gated loader can be wired correctly.

## 17. Measmerize

1. **Consent approach.** Zimmermann privacy / legal to confirm which of two approaches applies: (a) load the script freely and call `window.measmerize.tracking.disableAnalytics()` / `disableCustom()` / `cookies.disableFunctional()` when consent is denied (Essential cookies always run), or (b) gate the entire script load behind a Didomi consent category. This is a **blocking** decision. If approach (b) is chosen, Zimmermann Privacy to also confirm the Didomi consent category and Tell No Lies to supply the corresponding Didomi vendor / feature ID. **Owner:** Zimmermann.
2. **Brand code UUIDs.** Script URL (`https://client.measmerize.com/script.js`) and product identifier (SFCC SKU, `data-product-code`) are confirmed from vendor docs. Measmerize issues exactly two brand codes per retailer: one for production and one shared across all non-production environments (Dev / SIT / Stage / UAT). Measmerize to supply both values to be set as MRT environment variables. **Owner:** Zimmermann / Measmerize.

## 18. Vimeo

Vimeo is used for product video (PDP) and editorial video (content pages via Contentful CMS). The embed loads client-side as a facade-loaded iframe.

1. **Consent approach.** Zimmermann privacy / legal to confirm: (a) always append `dnt=1` to the embed URL — suppresses Vimeo's tracking cookies, no Didomi gate needed; or (b) load the standard embed gated behind a Didomi consent category. 2. **Vimeo platform confirmation (PRD-067).** The Third Party Integrations sheet lists Vimeo as the video platform, but PRD-067 is explicitly open: "Vimeo has not been 100% confirmed — open action to confirm best solution for smoothest FE experience." 1	# Shared AI Brain — Implementation Brief
2	## Zimmermann SFCC Replatform — Sprint 0 Deliverable
3	
4	**Prepared by:** Tim Lavelle, Accenture Song  
5	**Audience:** Lead Architect + Claude Code CLI  
6	**Date:** May 2026  
7	**Status:** Ready for implementation  
8	**Owner post-build:** Lead Architect  
9	
10	---
11	
12	## 1. What We Are Building and Why
13	
14	### The problem
15	
16	Claude Code CLI and Claude.ai both start every session with zero memory. A BA writes a critical regional checkout rule in Confluence on Monday. A developer asks Claude Code about checkout behaviour on Wednesday. Claude Code has no awareness of that decision and either answers from general knowledge or asks the developer to provide context manually.
17	
18	Multiply this across a team of BAs, PMs, QAs, and developers across a 12-month engagement and the result is: decisions made by one person are invisible to everyone else's AI sessions, context gets reconstructed from scratch in every conversation, and conflicting information accumulates silently until it surfaces as a defect or a rework in build.
19	
20	### What we are building
21	
22	A team-wide shared AI knowledge layer — referred to throughout this document as the **Shared Brain** — that:
23	
24	- Automatically ingests structured knowledge from Confluence (the team's single source of truth)
25	- Embeds and stores that knowledge in a vector database for semantic retrieval
26	- Detects conflicts between knowledge items automatically and surfaces them for human triage
27	- Exposes a RAG query API that both Claude Code (via MCP server) and Claude.ai (via project knowledge sync) can consume
28	- Requires no manual sync from any team member — ingestion is event-driven on Confluence page changes
29	
30	### Who it serves
31	
32	| Role | How they interact with it |
33	|---|---|
34	| Developers | Claude Code `/knowledge` skill queries the RAG API via MCP server |
35	| BAs / PMs / QAs | Claude.ai project knowledge is auto-updated from the same source — no Git access required |
36	| Lead Architect | Owns the system, monitors ingestion health, triages conflict flags in Confluence |
37	
38	### What it is not
39	
40	This is not a general-purpose enterprise knowledge platform. It is a sprint-scoped, engagement-specific tool built to solve one problem: keeping every team member's AI sessions working from the same shared context. It should be lean, low-cost, and maintainable by one person.
41	
42	---
43	
44	## 2. Key Decisions (Made, Not Open)
45	
46	These decisions were made during the planning phase. Claude Code should implement against them, not re-evaluate them.
47	
48	### Decision 1 — Confluence is the only authoritative source
49	
50	All team knowledge flows into the Shared Brain from Confluence. No other source. Decisions made in Claude.ai sessions, Slack, or email do not enter the Shared Brain until a human writes them into a properly templated Confluence page.
51	
52	**Rationale:** Confluence is the tool every team role — including non-technical members — can write to without friction. Having a single authoritative source prevents the "which version is correct" problem that kills RAG quality.
53	
54	**Implication for build:** The ingestion pipeline reads from Confluence only. No Git-to-Confluence sync, no Slack integration, no direct Claude Code writes to the knowledge base.
55	
56	---
57	
58	### Decision 2 — pgvector on managed Postgres as the vector store
59	
60	**Chosen:** pgvector extension on a managed Postgres instance (Railway, Supabase, or Neon — Lead Architect selects based on cloud availability).
61	
62	**Rejected alternatives:**
63	- Pinecone — predictable cost but adds a vendor dependency and a separate service to manage
64	- Weaviate — self-hosted complexity is unnecessary at this engagement's knowledge volume
65	- Chroma — good for local dev, not suitable for a multi-user team deployment
66	
67	**Rationale:** Zimmermann's knowledge base will be in the hundreds of Confluence pages, not millions of documents. pgvector on a small managed Postgres instance is sufficient, cheap (~$20-50/month), and gives the Lead Architect a familiar operational model. One service, one connection string, no separate vector DB infrastructure.
68	
69	**Schema to implement:**
70	
71	```sql
72	CREATE EXTENSION IF NOT EXISTS vector;
73	
74	CREATE TABLE knowledge_chunks (
75	  id            UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
76	  page_id       TEXT NOT NULL,
77	  page_title    TEXT NOT NULL,
78	  page_type     TEXT NOT NULL,          -- 'architecture-decision' | 'scope-boundary' | 'regional-rule' | 'open-item' | 'meeting-outcome'
79	  space_key     TEXT NOT NULL,
80	  chunk_index   INTEGER NOT NULL,
81	  content       TEXT NOT NULL,
82	  embedding     vector(1536),           -- OpenAI text-embedding-3-small dimensions
83	  source_url    TEXT,
84	  last_updated  TIMESTAMPTZ DEFAULT now(),
85	  checksum      TEXT                    -- MD5 of content, used to skip unchanged chunks on re-ingestion
86	);
87	
88	CREATE INDEX ON knowledge_chunks USING ivfflat (embedding vector_cosine_ops) WITH (lists = 100);
89	
90	CREATE TABLE conflict_flags (
91	  id              UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
92	  chunk_a_id      UUID REFERENCES knowledge_chunks(id),
93	  chunk_b_id      UUID REFERENCES knowledge_chunks(id),
94	  similarity      FLOAT,
95	  conflict_summary TEXT,
96	  status          TEXT DEFAULT 'open',  -- 'open' | 'resolved' | 'dismissed'
97	  flagged_at      TIMESTAMPTZ DEFAULT now(),
98	  resolved_by     TEXT,
99	  resolved_at     TIMESTAMPTZ
100	);
101	
102	CREATE TABLE ingestion_log (
103	  id            UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
104	  page_id       TEXT NOT NULL,
105	  page_title    TEXT NOT NULL,
106	  event_type    TEXT NOT NULL,          -- 'created' | 'updated' | 'deleted'
107	  status        TEXT NOT NULL,          -- 'success' | 'failed' | 'skipped'
108	  chunks_written INTEGER,
109	  error_message TEXT,
110	  processed_at  TIMESTAMPTZ DEFAULT now()
111	);
112	```
113	
114	---
115	
116	### Decision 3 — Embeddings via OpenAI text-embedding-3-small
117	
118	**Chosen:** `text-embedding-3-small` (1536 dimensions, $0.02 per million tokens).
119	
120	**Rationale:** At Zimmermann's knowledge volume (hundreds of pages, re-ingested weekly), the cost will be under $5/month. Claude does not currently expose an embeddings API. Using the same embedding model for ingestion and query ensures consistency. `text-embedding-3-small` outperforms `ada-002` at lower cost.
121	
122	**Note:** If Anthropic releases a native embeddings API during the engagement, the Lead Architect should evaluate migration — the schema is model-agnostic as long as the dimension column is updated.
123	
124	---
125	
126	### Decision 4 — Node.js for the ingestion service and RAG API
127	
128	The existing project infrastructure is Node.js (PWA Kit, pptxgenjs, CI/CD scripts). The Lead Architect and development team are already working in this stack. Building the Shared Brain in Node.js means one language across the entire engagement infrastructure.
129	
130	**Stack:**
131	- Runtime: Node.js 18+ (matches PWA Kit requirement)
132	- Framework: Express.js for the RAG API (already used in pwa-kit-runtime)
133	- Confluence client: Atlassian REST API v2 via `axios`
134	- Postgres client: `pg` with `pgvector` extension support
135	- Embeddings: `openai` SDK
136	- Deployment: Railway, Render, or Fly.io (Lead Architect selects — must support always-on Node.js service and Postgres add-on)
137	
138	---
139	
140	### Decision 5 — Claude Code connects via MCP server
141	
142	The MCP server wraps the RAG API and exposes it as a Claude Code tool. Developers add one line to their Claude Code MCP config. No per-session setup required after initial onboarding.
143	
144	A `/knowledge` skill is added to the existing `.claude/skills/` directory alongside the existing 13 skills. It calls the MCP server's query endpoint and returns retrieved chunks with source page links.
145	
146	---
147	
148	### Decision 6 — Claude.ai sync via auto-generated summary document
149	
150	Claude.ai does not currently support programmatic injection into project knowledge via API. The practical solution for non-developer team members is a daily auto-generated `TEAM-KNOWLEDGE-SUMMARY.md` written to the Claude.ai project by the ingestion service.
151	
152	This document is structured, not a raw dump — it contains current decisions by category, open conflicts requiring triage, recently updated pages, and a staleness timestamp. It gives BA, PM, and QA sessions grounded context without requiring Git access or technical configuration.
153	
154	**Limitation to communicate to the team:** Claude.ai sessions for non-developers will have summarised context, not full RAG retrieval. Full RAG is available in Claude Code sessions via MCP. This is a current Claude.ai platform constraint, not a design choice.
155	
156	---
157	
158	### Decision 7 — Conflict detection is AI-flagged, human-resolved
159	
160	The ingestion pipeline runs conflict detection on every new or updated chunk. Detection uses cosine similarity — chunks from different pages on the same topic with similarity > 0.92 but divergent conclusions are flagged.
161	
162	Conflicts are written to a dedicated Confluence page: `Shared Brain / Conflict Review`. The Lead Architect reviews this page weekly. Conflicts are never auto-resolved.
163	
164	**Why not auto-resolve:** Auto-resolution requires understanding business intent, not just semantic similarity. Two pages can say different things about EU checkout for valid reasons — one describes the current state, one describes the target state. Only a human with engagement context can make that call.
165	
166	---
167	
168	## 3. Confluence Space Structure (Required Before Pipeline Build)
169	
170	The ingestion pipeline's quality depends entirely on consistent Confluence structure. The pipeline uses page type labels to route chunks into the correct knowledge categories. Pages without a recognised type label are logged as `skipped` and not ingested.
171	
172	### Required page types (Confluence labels)
173	
174	Every page that should be ingested must have exactly one of these labels applied in Confluence:
175	
176	| Label | Used for | Examples |
177	|---|---|---|
178	| `architecture-decision` | Technical and solution decisions with rationale | Storefront baseline, APM tool selection, checkout split |
179	| `scope-boundary` | What is in scope, out of scope, and explicitly deferred | ME RTL out of scope, Contentful editorial only |
180	| `regional-rule` | Rules that vary by storefront or region | Avalara covers AU+NZ, VAT EU domestic only |
181	| `open-item` | Unresolved decisions requiring follow-up | Global-e Retail Rewards redemption pending call |
182	| `meeting-outcome` | Key decisions and actions from sessions | Merchandising deep dive outcomes, workshop decisions |
183	
184	### Required page template fields
185	
186	Every ingested page must have these fields in the page body. The ingestion service looks for these as H2 headings and extracts the content beneath them:
187	
188	```
189	## Summary
190	One paragraph. What this page is about.
191	
192	## Decision / Rule / Outcome
193	The actual content. What was decided, what the rule is, what happened.
194	
195	## Rationale
196	Why this decision was made. What alternatives were considered and rejected.
197	
198	## Owner
199	Who is accountable for this knowledge item.
200	
201	## Last Reviewed
202	Date. Updated whenever the content is verified as current.
203	
204	## Related Pages
205	Links to related Confluence pages.
206	```
207	
208	Pages missing `## Summary` or `## Decision / Rule / Outcome` are logged as malformed and not ingested. The Lead Architect is notified via the ingestion log.
209	
210	### Seed content — what gets loaded in Sprint 0
211	
212	The following existing project outputs must be converted into properly templated Confluence pages before the pipeline runs. This is a one-time task, not an ongoing requirement.
213	
214	| Existing artefact | Target page type | Owner to create |
215	|---|---|---|
216	| Scope Framework — 11 functional groups | `scope-boundary` (one page per group) | BA Lead |
217	| RADAR — Out of Scope items | `scope-boundary` | BA Lead |
218	| RADAR — Assumptions | `architecture-decision` | Lead Architect |
219	| RADAR — Risks | `open-item` | PM |
220	| Integration register — 34 integrations | `architecture-decision` | Lead Architect |
221	| Regional checkout model (domestic vs Global-e) | `regional-rule` | Lead Architect |
222	| APM / New Relic recommendation | `architecture-decision` | Lead Architect |
223	| Avalara regional scope | `regional-rule` | BA Lead |
224	| VAT EU domestic only | `regional-rule` | BA Lead |
225	| ME English-only, RTL out of scope | `scope-boundary` | BA Lead |
226	| PIM recommendation (Akeneo Growth) | `architecture-decision` | Lead Architect |
227	| Correlation ID strategy | `architecture-decision` | Lead Architect |
228	| Merchandising deep dive outcomes | `meeting-outcome` | BA Lead |
229	| Global-e Retail Rewards — open item | `open-item` | PM |
230	
231	---
232	
233	## 4. System Architecture
234	
235	```
236	┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
237	│                    CONFLUENCE                           │
238	│  Pages with labels: architecture-decision,             │
239	│  scope-boundary, regional-rule, open-item,             │
240	│  meeting-outcome                                        │
241	└────────────────────┬────────────────────────────────────┘
242	                     │ Webhook (page created/updated)
243	                     ▼
244	┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
245	│              INGESTION SERVICE (Node.js)                │
246	│                                                         │
247	│  1. Receive webhook payload                             │
248	│  2. Fetch full page content via Confluence REST API v2  │
249	│  3. Validate page has required label and template fields│
250	│  4. Chunk content by H2 section                         │

257	│  11. On conflict: update Confluence conflict review page│

259	└────────────────────┬────────────────────────────────────┘
260	                     │
261	                     ▼
262	┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
263	│         POSTGRES + pgvector (managed instance)          │
264	│  Tables: knowledge_chunks, conflict_flags,              │
265	│  ingestion_log                                          │
266	└────────────────────┬────────────────────────────────────┘
267	                     │
268	          ┌──────────┴──────────┐
269	          ▼                     ▼
270	┌──────────────────┐  ┌────────────────────────────────┐
271	│   RAG API        │  │  DAILY SUMMARY WRITER           │
272	│   (Express.js)   │  │                                 │
273	│                  │  │  Reads knowledge_chunks and     │
274	│  POST /query     │  │  conflict_flags, generates      │
275	│  POST /health    │  │  TEAM-KNOWLEDGE-SUMMARY.md,     │
276	│  GET  /conflicts │  │  written to Claude.ai project   │

541	## 11. Build Sequence for Claude Code
542	
543	Work through these phases in order. Do not start the next phase until the current one is verified.
544	
545	### Phase 1 — Database (Day 1)
546	1. Create `shared-brain/db/schema.sql` from the schema in Decision 2
547	2. Create `shared-brain/db/migrate.js` — runs schema against the Postgres instance
548	3. Create `shared-brain/db/client.js` — pg connection pool singleton with health check
549	4. Run migration against a dev Postgres instance

551	
552	### Phase 2 — Ingestion service (Days 2-3)
553	1. Build `confluence-client.js` — wraps Confluence REST API v2, handles pagination
554	2. Build `validator.js` — checks page label and required H2 fields
555	3. Build `chunker.js` — splits page content by H2 section, returns array of chunks
556	4. Build `embedder.js` — calls OpenAI embeddings API, returns vector per chunk
557	5. Build `conflict-detector.js` — runs cosine similarity query against existing chunks, returns conflicts above threshold
558	6. Build `confluence-writer.js` — appends conflict summary to the Conflict Review page
559	7. Wire together in `ingestion/index.js` as an Express POST /webhook endpoint
560	8. Test with a single manually crafted Confluence webhook payload
561	9. Verify: chunk written to DB, embedding stored, ingestion_log entry created
562	
563	### Phase 3 — RAG API (Day 4)
564	1. Build `api/query.js` — embeds incoming question, runs cosine similarity query, returns ranked chunks
565	2. Build `api/conflicts.js`, `api/log.js`, `api/health.js`
566	3. Wire in `api/index.js` with bearer token auth middleware
567	4. Test all endpoints manually with `scripts/test-query.js`
568	5. Verify: `/query` returns relevant chunks for a known question, `/health` shows correct chunk count
569	
570	### Phase 4 — MCP server (Day 5)
571	1. Build `mcp/index.js` and `mcp/tools.js` from the tool definition in Section 8
572	2. Write `mcp/README.md` — exact developer config instructions including the one-line MCP config entry
573	3. Test locally: configure Claude Code to use the MCP server, run `/knowledge` skill, verify retrieval
574	4. Verify: Claude Code session returns knowledge base results when queried
575	
576	### Phase 5 — Summary writer and /knowledge skill (Day 6)
577	1. Build `summary-writer.js` — generates TEAM-KNOWLEDGE-SUMMARY.md from DB
578	2. Add daily schedule to ingestion service (node-cron or equivalent)
579	3. Create `.claude/skills/knowledge.md` from Section 9
580	4. Manually upload generated summary to Claude.ai project knowledge
581	5. Verify: Claude.ai session references correct project decisions from summary
582	
583	### Phase 6 — Seed verification and go-live check (Day 7)
584	1. Confirm all seed content from Section 3 has been loaded into Confluence with correct labels and templates
585	2. Run `scripts/seed-check.js` — queries for each expected seed page, reports missing
586	3. Run `scripts/health-check.js` — verifies DB connection, API response, MCP connectivity
587	4. Share `/health` endpoint output with Lead Architect for sign-off
588	5. Document Confluence webhook URL and deployment URL in `shared-brain/README.md`
589	
590	---
591	
592	## 12. Maintenance Responsibilities (Lead Architect)
593	
594	### Weekly (15 minutes)
595	- Review Confluence Conflict Review page — triage open flags as resolved or dismissed
596	- Check ingestion log via `GET /log` — investigate any `failed` or `skipped` entries
597	- Verify `GET /health` shows expected chunk count growth
598	
599	### Per sprint
600	- Review TEAM-KNOWLEDGE-SUMMARY.md for accuracy — spot-check 3-5 chunks against source pages
601	- Update `CONFLICT_SIMILARITY_THRESHOLD` if conflict detection is too noisy or missing real conflicts
602	- Notify team if any page type is being underused (e.g. no new `open-item` pages when there are clearly unresolved decisions)
603	
604	### When a new team member joins
605	- Add them to Confluence space with correct permissions
606	- Walk them through the Confluence page template and labelling requirements (15-minute onboarding)
607	- For developers: configure MCP server in their Claude Code setup (one config line — see `mcp/README.md`)
608	- For non-developers: confirm they have access to the Claude.ai project and can see the knowledge summary
609	
610	---
611	
612	## 13. What This Does Not Do (Scope Boundaries)
613	
614	Be explicit with Claude Code about what is out of scope to prevent scope creep:
615	
616	- **No Slack integration.** Decisions made in Slack do not enter the Shared Brain until written to Confluence.
617	- **No automatic write-back from Claude sessions to Confluence.** Knowledge flows one way: Confluence → Shared Brain → Claude. Claude never writes to Confluence directly.
618	- **No multi-engagement generalisation in Sprint 0.** Build for Zimmermann. Reusable patterns can be extracted after the engagement proves the model.
619	- **No fine-tuning or model training.** This is retrieval augmentation only. No model training, no fine-tuning, no embeddings retraining.
620	- **No real-time conflict resolution.** Conflicts are flagged and triaged by humans. Auto-resolution is explicitly out of scope.
621	- **No Jira integration in Sprint 0.** Jira tickets are not ingested. If a ticket contains a key decision, the BA or PM writes it to a Confluence page.
622	
623	---
624	
625	## 14. Cost Model
626	
627	| Item | Estimate | Notes |
628	|---|---|---|
629	| Managed Postgres + pgvector | $20–50/month | Railway Pro, Supabase Pro, or Neon Launch |
630	| OpenAI embeddings | < $5/month | ~2,500 page chunks × re-ingestion cadence |
631	| Hosting for ingestion service + RAG API | $7–20/month | Railway Starter or Render Free/Starter |
632	| Confluence webhooks | Free | Built into Atlassian |
633	| MCP server | $0 | Runs locally on each developer's machine |
634	| **Total** | **~$30–75/month** | Well within delivery infrastructure budget |
635	
636	---
637	
638	## 15. Success Criteria for Sprint 0 Sign-Off
639	
640	The Lead Architect signs off the Shared Brain as Sprint 0 complete when all of the following are true:
641	
642	- [ ] Confluence space has all seed content loaded with correct labels and templates
643	- [ ] Ingestion pipeline receives Confluence webhooks and writes chunks to DB
644	- [ ] Conflict detection flags a known test conflict correctly
645	- [ ] RAG API returns relevant results for 5 test questions covering different page types
646	- [ ] MCP server configured on at least 2 developer machines, `/knowledge` skill functional
647	- [ ] TEAM-KNOWLEDGE-SUMMARY.md uploaded to Claude.ai project and verified by a BA
648	- [ ] `GET /health` shows > 200 chunks indexed from seed content
649	- [ ] `shared-brain/README.md` complete with setup, config, and maintenance guide
650	- [ ] Lead Architect has reviewed first week of ingestion logs with no unresolved failures
651	
652	---
653	
654	*Brief prepared by Tim Lavelle, Accenture Song, May 2026.*  
655	*This document is the implementation contract for Claude Code. Every decision in Section 2 is final. If Claude Code identifies a technical blocker against any decision, it should flag it explicitly before proceeding — not work around it silently.*

# Shared AI Brain — Implementation Brief
## Zimmermann SFCC Replatform — Sprint 0 Deliverable

**Prepared by:** Tim Lavelle, Accenture Song  
**Audience:** Lead Architect + Claude Code CLI  
**Date:** May 2026  
**Status:** Ready for implementation  
**Owner post-build:** Lead Architect  

---

## 1. What We Are Building and Why

### The problem

Claude Code CLI and Claude.ai both start every session with zero memory. A BA writes a critical regional checkout rule in Confluence on Monday. A developer asks Claude Code about checkout behaviour on Wednesday. Claude Code has no awareness of that decision and either answers from general knowledge or asks the developer to provide context manually.

Multiply this across a team of BAs, PMs, QAs, and developers across a 12-month engagement and the result is: decisions made by one person are invisible to everyone else's AI sessions, context gets reconstructed from scratch in every conversation, and conflicting information accumulates silently until it surfaces as a defect or a rework in build.

### What we are building

A team-wide shared AI knowledge layer — referred to throughout this document as the **Shared Brain** — that:

- Automatically ingests structured knowledge from Confluence (the team's single source of truth)
- Embeds and stores that knowledge in a vector database for semantic retrieval
- Detects conflicts between knowledge items automatically and surfaces them for human triage
- Exposes a RAG query API that both Claude Code (via MCP server) and Claude.ai (via project knowledge sync) can consume
- Requires no manual sync from any team member — ingestion is event-driven on Confluence page changes

### Who it serves

| Role | How they interact with it |
|---|---|
| Developers | Claude Code `/knowledge` skill queries the RAG API via MCP server |
| BAs / PMs / QAs | Claude.ai project knowledge is auto-updated from the same source — no Git access required |
| Lead Architect | Owns the system, monitors ingestion health, triages conflict flags in Confluence |

### What it is not

This is not a general-purpose enterprise knowledge platform. It is a sprint-scoped, engagement-specific tool built to solve one problem: keeping every team member's AI sessions working from the same shared context. It should be lean, low-cost, and maintainable by one person.

---

## 2. Key Decisions (Made, Not Open)

These decisions were made during the planning phase. Claude Code should implement against them, not re-evaluate them.

### Decision 1 — Confluence is the only authoritative source

All team knowledge flows into the Shared Brain from Confluence. No other source. Decisions made in Claude.ai sessions, Slack, or email do not enter the Shared Brain until a human writes them into a properly templated Confluence page.

**Rationale:** Confluence is the tool every team role — including non-technical members — can write to without friction. Having a single authoritative source prevents the "which version is correct" problem that kills RAG quality.

**Implication for build:** The ingestion pipeline reads from Confluence only. No Git-to-Confluence sync, no Slack integration, no direct Claude Code writes to the knowledge base.

---

### Decision 2 — pgvector on managed Postgres as the vector store

**Chosen:** pgvector extension on a managed Postgres instance (Railway, Supabase, or Neon — Lead Architect selects based on cloud availability).

**Rejected alternatives:**
- Pinecone — predictable cost but adds a vendor dependency and a separate service to manage
- Weaviate — self-hosted complexity is unnecessary at this engagement's knowledge volume
- Chroma — good for local dev, not suitable for a multi-user team deployment

**Rationale:** Zimmermann's knowledge base will be in the hundreds of Confluence pages, not millions of documents. pgvector on a small managed Postgres instance is sufficient, cheap (~$20-50/month), and gives the Lead Architect a familiar operational model. One service, one connection string, no separate vector DB infrastructure.

**Schema to implement:**

```sql
CREATE EXTENSION IF NOT EXISTS vector;

CREATE TABLE knowledge_chunks (
  id            UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  page_id       TEXT NOT NULL,
  page_title    TEXT NOT NULL,
  page_type     TEXT NOT NULL,          -- 'architecture-decision' | 'scope-boundary' | 'regional-rule' | 'open-item' | 'meeting-outcome'
  space_key     TEXT NOT NULL,
  chunk_index   INTEGER NOT NULL,
  content       TEXT NOT NULL,
  embedding     vector(1536),           -- OpenAI text-embedding-3-small dimensions
  source_url    TEXT,
  last_updated  TIMESTAMPTZ DEFAULT now(),
  checksum      TEXT                    -- MD5 of content, used to skip unchanged chunks on re-ingestion
);

CREATE INDEX ON knowledge_chunks USING ivfflat (embedding vector_cosine_ops) WITH (lists = 100);

CREATE TABLE conflict_flags (
  id              UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  chunk_a_id      UUID REFERENCES knowledge_chunks(id),
  chunk_b_id      UUID REFERENCES knowledge_chunks(id),
  similarity      FLOAT,
  conflict_summary TEXT,
  status          TEXT DEFAULT 'open',  -- 'open' | 'resolved' | 'dismissed'
  flagged_at      TIMESTAMPTZ DEFAULT now(),
  resolved_by     TEXT,
  resolved_at     TIMESTAMPTZ
);

CREATE TABLE ingestion_log (
  id            UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  page_id       TEXT NOT NULL,
  page_title    TEXT NOT NULL,
  event_type    TEXT NOT NULL,          -- 'created' | 'updated' | 'deleted'
  status        TEXT NOT NULL,          -- 'success' | 'failed' | 'skipped'
  chunks_written INTEGER,
  error_message TEXT,
  processed_at  TIMESTAMPTZ DEFAULT now()
);
```

---

### Decision 3 — Embeddings via OpenAI text-embedding-3-small

**Chosen:** `text-embedding-3-small` (1536 dimensions, $0.02 per million tokens).

**Rationale:** At Zimmermann's knowledge volume (hundreds of pages, re-ingested weekly), the cost will be under $5/month. Claude does not currently expose an embeddings API. Using the same embedding model for ingestion and query ensures consistency. `text-embedding-3-small` outperforms `ada-002` at lower cost.

**Note:** If Anthropic releases a native embeddings API during the engagement, the Lead Architect should evaluate migration — the schema is model-agnostic as long as the dimension column is updated.

---

### Decision 4 — Node.js for the ingestion service and RAG API

The existing project infrastructure is Node.js (PWA Kit, pptxgenjs, CI/CD scripts). The Lead Architect and development team are already working in this stack. Building the Shared Brain in Node.js means one language across the entire engagement infrastructure.

**Stack:**
- Runtime: Node.js 18+ (matches PWA Kit requirement)
- Framework: Express.js for the RAG API (already used in pwa-kit-runtime)
- Confluence client: Atlassian REST API v2 via `axios`
- Postgres client: `pg` with `pgvector` extension support
- Embeddings: `openai` SDK
- Deployment: Railway, Render, or Fly.io (Lead Architect selects — must support always-on Node.js service and Postgres add-on)

---

### Decision 5 — Claude Code connects via MCP server

The MCP server wraps the RAG API and exposes it as a Claude Code tool. Developers add one line to their Claude Code MCP config. No per-session setup required after initial onboarding.

A `/knowledge` skill is added to the existing `.claude/skills/` directory alongside the existing 13 skills. It calls the MCP server's query endpoint and returns retrieved chunks with source page links.

---

### Decision 6 — Claude.ai sync via auto-generated summary document

Claude.ai does not currently support programmatic injection into project knowledge via API. The practical solution for non-developer team members is a daily auto-generated `TEAM-KNOWLEDGE-SUMMARY.md` written to the Claude.ai project by the ingestion service.

This document is structured, not a raw dump — it contains current decisions by category, open conflicts requiring triage, recently updated pages, and a staleness timestamp. It gives BA, PM, and QA sessions grounded context without requiring Git access or technical configuration.

**Limitation to communicate to the team:** Claude.ai sessions for non-developers will have summarised context, not full RAG retrieval. Full RAG is available in Claude Code sessions via MCP. This is a current Claude.ai platform constraint, not a design choice.

---

### Decision 7 — Conflict detection is AI-flagged, human-resolved

The ingestion pipeline runs conflict detection on every new or updated chunk. Detection uses cosine similarity — chunks from different pages on the same topic with similarity > 0.92 but divergent conclusions are flagged.

Conflicts are written to a dedicated Confluence page: `Shared Brain / Conflict Review`. The Lead Architect reviews this page weekly. Conflicts are never auto-resolved.

**Why not auto-resolve:** Auto-resolution requires understanding business intent, not just semantic similarity. Two pages can say different things about EU checkout for valid reasons — one describes the current state, one describes the target state. Only a human with engagement context can make that call.

---

## 3. Confluence Space Structure (Required Before Pipeline Build)

The ingestion pipeline's quality depends entirely on consistent Confluence structure. The pipeline uses page type labels to route chunks into the correct knowledge categories. Pages without a recognised type label are logged as `skipped` and not ingested.

### Required page types (Confluence labels)

Every page that should be ingested must have exactly one of these labels applied in Confluence:

| Label | Used for | Examples |
|---|---|---|
| `architecture-decision` | Technical and solution decisions with rationale | Storefront baseline, APM tool selection, checkout split |
| `scope-boundary` | What is in scope, out of scope, and explicitly deferred | ME RTL out of scope, Contentful editorial only |
| `regional-rule` | Rules that vary by storefront or region | Avalara covers AU+NZ, VAT EU domestic only |
| `open-item` | Unresolved decisions requiring follow-up | Global-e Retail Rewards redemption pending call |
| `meeting-outcome` | Key decisions and actions from sessions | Merchandising deep dive outcomes, workshop decisions |

### Required page template fields

Every ingested page must have these fields in the page body. The ingestion service looks for these as H2 headings and extracts the content beneath them:

```
## Summary
One paragraph. What this page is about.

## Decision / Rule / Outcome
The actual content. What was decided, what the rule is, what happened.

## Rationale
Why this decision was made. What alternatives were considered and rejected.

## Owner
Who is accountable for this knowledge item.

## Last Reviewed
Date. Updated whenever the content is verified as current.

# /knowledge — Query the shared project knowledge base

## When to use
Run this before answering any question about:

- Scope boundaries (what is in/out/deferred)
- Regional rules (checkout model, tax, payment, fulfilment by region)
- Open items (unresolved decisions, pending calls)

## 11. Build Sequence for Claude Code

Work through these phases in order. Do not start the next phase until the current one is verified.

### Phase 1 — Database (Day 1)
1. Create `shared-brain/db/schema.sql` from the schema in Decision 2
2. Create `shared-brain/db/migrate.js` — runs schema against the Postgres instance
3. Create `shared-brain/db/client.js` — pg connection pool singleton with health check
4. Run migration against a dev Postgres instance
5. Verify: `psql $DATABASE_URL -c "\d knowledge_chunks"` returns correct schema

### Phase 2 — Ingestion service (Days 2-3)
1. Build `confluence-client.js` — wraps Confluence REST API v2, handles pagination
2. Build `validator.js` — checks page label and required H2 fields
3. Build `chunker.js` — splits page content by H2 section, returns array of chunks
4. Build `embedder.js` — calls OpenAI embeddings API, returns vector per chunk
5. Build `conflict-detector.js` — runs cosine similarity query against existing chunks, returns conflicts above threshold
6. Build `confluence-writer.js` — appends conflict summary to the Conflict Review page
7. Wire together in `ingestion/index.js` as an Express POST /webhook endpoint
8. Test with a single manually crafted Confluence webhook payload
9. Verify: chunk written to DB, embedding stored, ingestion_log entry created

### Phase 3 — RAG API (Day 4)
1. Build `api/query.js` — embeds incoming question, runs cosine similarity query, returns ranked chunks
2. Build `api/conflicts.js`, `api/log.js`, `api/health.js`
3. Wire in `api/index.js` with bearer token auth middleware
4. Test all endpoints manually with `scripts/test-query.js`
5. Verify: `/query` returns relevant chunks for a known question, `/health` shows correct chunk count

### Phase 4 — MCP server (Day 5)
1. Build `mcp/index.js` and `mcp/tools.js` from the tool definition in Section 8
2. Write `mcp/README.md` — exact developer config instructions including the one-line MCP config entry
3. Test locally: configure Claude Code to use the MCP server, run `/knowledge` skill, verify retrieval
4. Verify: Claude Code session returns knowledge base results when queried

### Phase 5 — Summary writer and /knowledge skill (Day 6)
1. Build `summary-writer.js` — generates TEAM-KNOWLEDGE-SUMMARY.md from DB
2. Add daily schedule to ingestion service (node-cron or equivalent)
3. Create `.claude/skills/knowledge.md` from Section 9
4. Manually upload generated summary to Claude.ai project knowledge
5. Verify: Claude.ai session references correct project decisions from summary

### Phase 6 — Seed verification and go-live check (Day 7)
1. Confirm all seed content from Section 3 has been loaded into Confluence with correct labels and templates
2. Run `scripts/seed-check.js` — queries for each expected seed page, reports missing
3. Run `scripts/health-check.js` — verifies DB connection, API response, MCP connectivity
4. Share `/health` endpoint output with Lead Architect for sign-off
5. Document Confluence webhook URL and deployment URL in `shared-brain/README.md`

## 12. Maintenance Responsibilities (Lead Architect)

### Weekly (15 minutes)
- Review Confluence Conflict Review page — triage open flags as resolved or dismissed
- Check ingestion log via `GET /log` — investigate any `failed` or `skipped` entries
- Verify `GET /health` shows expected chunk count growth

### Per sprint
- Review TEAM-KNOWLEDGE-SUMMARY.md for accuracy — spot-check 3-5 chunks against source pages
- Update `CONFLICT_SIMILARITY_THRESHOLD` if conflict detection is too noisy or missing real conflicts
- Notify team if any page type is being underused (e.g. no new `open-item` pages when there are clearly unresolved decisions)

### When a new team member joins
- Add them to Confluence space with correct permissions
- Walk them through the Confluence page template and labelling requirements (15-minute onboarding)
- For developers: configure MCP server in their Claude Code setup (one config line — see `mcp/README.md`)
- For non-developers: confirm they have access to the Claude.ai project and can see the knowledge summary

## 13. What This Does Not Do (Scope Boundaries)

Be explicit with Claude Code about what is out of scope to prevent scope creep:

- **No Slack integration.** Decisions made in Slack do not enter the Shared Brain until written to Confluence.
- **No automatic write-back from Claude sessions to Confluence.** Knowledge flows one way: Confluence → Shared Brain → Claude. Claude never writes to Confluence directly.
- **No multi-engagement generalisation in Sprint 0.** Build for Zimmermann. Reusable patterns can be extracted after the engagement proves the model.
- **No fine-tuning or model training.** This is retrieval augmentation only. No model training, no fine-tuning, no embeddings retraining.
- **No real-time conflict resolution.** Conflicts are flagged and triaged by humans. Auto-resolution is explicitly out of scope.
- **No Jira integration in Sprint 0.** Jira tickets are not ingested. If a ticket contains a key decision, the BA or PM writes it to a Confluence page.

# Paste this entire prompt into Claude Code CLI at the root of the PWA Kit repo

You are helping implement the Digital SIT quality gate framework for a Salesforce Commerce Cloud PWA Kit storefront (template-retail-react-app, GitHub Actions CI/CD, trunk-based development).

The goal is to make "Digital SIT green" a concrete, automatically enforced composite gate rather than a manual check. Four signals must all pass before promotion to E2E/Pre-prod is allowed:

1. Playwright P0 journey suite — 100% pass rate across all 6 storefront configurations
2. Lighthouse CI — Performance ≥ 80, Accessibility ≥ 90, Best Practices ≥ 90, score drop > 5 pts vs baseline = blocked
3. MuleSoft contract tests — Experience API schemas validated via Pact or OpenAPI schema assertions
4. Bundle size — main.js < 180 kB, vendor.js < 250 kB, main.css < 50 kB

Please make the following changes across the repo. Read existing files before editing — do not overwrite content that is unrelated to these changes.

---

## 1. GitHub Actions — Digital SIT workflow

File: `.github/workflows/digital-sit.yml`

Create this file if it does not exist. If it exists, extend it rather than replace it.

The workflow should:
- Trigger on push to `develop` and on pull_request targeting `release/**`
- Run on `ubuntu-latest`
- Use Node 18 (match the version in package.json engines field if present)
- Have the following jobs in order, each depending on the previous:

**Job: `install`**
- `actions/checkout@v4`
- `actions/setup-node@v4` with `cache: npm`
- `npm ci`
- Upload `node_modules` as a cache artifact keyed on the lockfile hash

**Job: `playwright-p0`** (depends on `install`)
- Restore node_modules cache
- Install Playwright browsers: `npx playwright install --with-deps chromium`
- Run: `npx playwright test --project=p0 --reporter=html,github`
- Upload the Playwright HTML report as an artifact named `playwright-report` with 30 day retention
- Set `continue-on-error: false` — this job must block promotion on any failure
- The report should be published to GitHub Pages if the triggering branch is `develop`. Use `actions/deploy-pages` for this.

**Job: `lighthouse-ci`** (depends on `install`)
- Restore node_modules cache
- Run: `npx lhci autorun`
- Upload `.lighthouseci/` directory as an artifact named `lighthouse-results` with 30 day retention
- Set `continue-on-error: false`

**Job: `contract-tests`** (depends on `install`)
- Restore node_modules cache
- Run: `npm run test:contracts` — if this script does not exist in package.json, add a placeholder that prints a warning and exits 0, and add a TODO comment noting that MuleSoft OpenAPI spec source must be confirmed before this gate is active
- Set `continue-on-error: false`

**Job: `bundle-size`** (depends on `install`)
- Restore node_modules cache
- Run: `npm run build` then `npx bundlewatch`
- Set `continue-on-error: false`

**Job: `sit-gate`** (depends on all five jobs above)
- This is the required status check that GitHub branch protection will reference
- Run a simple script that prints "Digital SIT gate: all checks passed" and exits 0
- This job name must be exactly: `Digital SIT Gate` (GitHub branch protection references it by name)

9	# Environment Strategy, Branching & SIT Pipeline — Claude Code Briefing
10	
11	## Programme Context
12	
13	Zimmermann is migrating from Magento 2 to Salesforce Commerce Cloud (SFCC) using the PWA Kit
14	(`template-retail-react-app`) as the storefront baseline, deployed on Managed Runtime (MRT).
15	
16	Seven storefronts are in scope: AU, UK, US domestic, US international (Global-e), EU domestic,
17	EU international (Global-e), and ME. The Digital pipeline must support all six active SFCC
18	storefronts simultaneously. NewStore (OMS) runs a parallel SIT cycle on its own cadence and
19	converges with Digital only at the STAGE tier.
20	
21	Zimmermann has 20 SFCC sandboxes available and no MRT environment licence restriction.
22	This enables a clean six-tier topology with no shared-environment contention.
23	
24	---
25	
26	## Environment Topology — Six Tiers
27	
28	```
29	LOCAL  →  DEV  →  SIT (parallel)  →  STAGE  →  UAT  →  PROD
30	```
31	
32	### Tier 1 — LOCAL
33	
34	| Layer | Environment | Purpose |
35	|---|---|---|
36	| SFCC BM | n/a | Not used locally |
37	| MRT / PWA | `npm start` (developer machine only — no MRT deployment) | Feature development and local SSR testing |
38	| 3P systems | All stubs via MSW | No real third-party calls at this tier |
39	| OMS SIT | Not in scope | NewStore not involved at this tier |
40	
41	**Who deploys here:** Individual developers run `npm start` locally. No MRT deployment for `feature/*` branches.
42	
43	**CDN / cache:** n/a — local dev server only.
44	
45	**Logging:** `debug` level. Source maps exposed.
46	
47	---
48	
49	### Tier 2 — DEV (Digital Dev)
50	
51	| Layer | Environment | Purpose |
52	|---|---|---|
53	| SFCC BM | SFCC STG org | Jobs: AP21 feed, OCI sync, Lengow |
54	| MRT / PWA | MRT staging | 7 storefronts, Playwright matrix, Lighthouse CI |
55	| 3P systems | MuleSoft STG only | All other third parties stubbed via MSW |
56	| OMS SIT | Not in scope | NewStore not involved at this tier |
57	
58	**Who deploys here:** CI pipeline on every merge to `develop`. Auto-deployed.
59	
60	**Gate:** `Digital SIT Gate` — composite GitHub Actions required status check. All four signals
61	must be green before promotion to STAGE is permitted:
62	- Playwright P0: 100% pass rate across 6 storefront configs
63	- Lighthouse CI: Performance ≥ 80, Accessibility ≥ 90, Best Practices ≥ 90
64	- MuleSoft contract tests: no schema breach
65	- Bundle size: main.js < 180 kB, vendor.js < 250 kB, main.css < 50 kB
66	
67	Vitest and Storybook interaction + a11y tests run in `qa.yml` (every PR to `develop`) — they gate
68	the PR merge, not the environment deploy.
69	
70	**CDN / cache:** 60s page TTL, 1h asset TTL.
71	
72	---
73	
74	### Tier 3 — SIT (NewStore SIT lane — parallel, never gates Digital)
75	
76	| Layer | Environment | Purpose |
77	|---|---|---|
78	| SFCC BM | Dedicated sandbox | Mirrors STG config — isolated from Digital STG data |
79	| MRT / PWA | MRT sit | Auto-receives every develop merge after Digital SIT gate passes |
80	| 3P systems | NewStore STG, MuleSoft STG, Adyen SBX | Real systems for OMS SIT scope |
81	| 3P stubs | Global-e, Narvar | Not required for OMS SIT |
82	| OMS SIT | SIT | NewStore runs 2–3 month SIT cycles here |
83	
84	**Who deploys here:** CI pipeline auto-push on every `develop` merge. NewStore never deploys
85	here manually — they consume what the pipeline provides.
86	
87	**Critical rules:**
88	- SIT is NOT a Digital gate. Digital promotes independently.
89	- SIT does NOT gate STAGE. STAGE opens only when OMS SIT is complete AND Digital SIT
90	  is green — confirmed via Jira environment booking ticket.
91	- NewStore reports regressions introduced by Digital changes here. Rollback via previous
92	  bundle ID while Digital fix is prepared.
93	
94	**Bundle retention:** 10 bundles.
95	
96	---
97	
98	### Tier 4 — STAGE (Shared convergence — time-boxed, Jira-booked)
99	
100	| Layer | Environment | Purpose |
101	|---|---|---|
102	| SFCC BM | Pre-prod org | Full config, jobs, pricebooks, promotions |
103	| MRT / PWA | MRT pre-prod | Full stack, all 3P real, Perf + a11y, visual regression |
104	| 3P systems | All systems real | NewStore STG, MuleSoft STG, Adyen SBX, Global-e STG, Narvar STG |
105	| OMS SIT | Convergence point | OMS SIT must be COMPLETE before this window opens |
106	
107	**Who deploys here:** Manual trigger only. Requires Jira booking ticket approved by Zimmermann
108	environment owner with both entry criteria confirmed green.
109	
110	**Entry criteria — both must be met before the window opens:**
111	1. Digital SIT Gate green (GitHub Actions required check passed on `release/*` branch)
112	2. NewStore OMS SIT complete (sign-off from NewStore project lead on Jira ticket)
113	
114	**CDN / cache:** 300s page TTL, 24h asset TTL — production-mirrored.
115	
116	**Gate:** `Environment booking confirmed` — first blocking gate in E2E / Pre-prod quality gates.
117	
118	---
119	
120	### Tier 5 — UAT
121	
122	| Layer | Environment | Purpose |
123	|---|---|---|
124	| SFCC BM | UAT org | Merch sign-off, production-mirrored config |
125	| MRT / PWA | MRT UAT | Business acceptance testing, all 6 regions |
126	| 3P systems | All systems real | Same as STAGE |
127	| OMS SIT | Feeds UAT | NewStore validated at STAGE — no further OMS SIT required |
128	
129	**Who deploys here:** Manual trigger. Requires business stakeholder sign-off per region.
130	
131	**Gate:** `UAT ✓` — Zimmermann stakeholder approval required. Cannot be automated.
132	
133	---
134	
135	### Tier 6 — PRODUCTION
136	
137	| Layer | Environment | Purpose |
138	|---|---|---|
139	| SFCC BM | PROD org | Live BM config, AU first then wave rollout |
140	| MRT / PWA | MRT Production | AU canary → all regions via `mrt:activate` |
141	| 3P systems | All PROD systems | Live credentials, live data |
142	| OMS SIT | Feeds PROD | NewStore PROD activated with Digital wave rollout |
143	
144	**Who deploys here:** Release manager only. Manual approval gate in GitHub Environments.
145	
146	**Gate:** `Production ✓` — named release manager activates bundle. Post-canary smoke test
147	must pass (error rate < 0.5% over 2h on AU) before remaining regions are opened.
148	
149	**Rollback:** Single `mrt:activate --target production --bundle-id <PREVIOUS_ID>` command.
150	Retention: 50 bundles (≈30-day rollback window).

153	
154	## Branching Strategy
155	
156	### Branch model overview
157	
158	```
159	main
160	 └── release/v*.*.*       ← release candidates, gates UAT + PROD
161	      └── develop          ← integration baseline, gates Dev + SIT
162	           └── feature/*   ← feature work, runs locally only (no MRT deployment)
163	hotfix/*                   ← branches from main, merges back to main + develop
164	```
165	
166	### Branch definitions and rules
167	
168	#### `main`
169	- Represents production. Always deployable.
170	- Protected: no direct pushes. Merge via PR from `release/v*.*.*` only.
171	- Required status checks: `Digital SIT Gate`, `UAT ✓` (manual), post-canary smoke.
172	- Tag every merge: `v{major}.{minor}.{patch}` — e.g. `v1.3.0`.
173	- Triggers: production deployment pipeline (manual approval gate).
174	
175	#### `release/v*.*.*`
176	- Naming convention: `release/v1.3.0`, `release/v1.3.1` etc.
177	- Branched from `develop` when a release window is scheduled.
178	- No new features merged here — bug fixes and release-prep only.
179	- Required status checks on PR to `main`: `Digital SIT Gate` (run against release branch),
180	  `UAT ✓`.
181	- Triggers: STAGE deployment pipeline (manual trigger after Jira booking approved).
182	- Git tag on branch creation: `release/digital/v1.3.0` — referenced in Jira booking ticket.
183	
184	#### `develop`
185	- Integration baseline. All feature branches merge here.
186	- Protected: no direct pushes. Merge via PR with minimum 1 approval.
187	- Required status checks on PR merge: lint, unit tests, bundle size, security scan.
188	- Triggers on merge:
189	  - Auto-deploy to MRT staging (Dev tier)
190	  - Auto-push to MRT sit (SIT tier) — fires after `sit-gate` passes
191	- Git tag convention on significant milestones: `develop/{sprint}/{date}` — e.g.
192	  `develop/sprint-12/2026-05-09`. Used to anchor SIT bundle reference for NewStore.
193	
194	#### `feature/*`
195	- Naming convention: `feature/JIRA-123_short-description`
196	- Branched from `develop`. Merges back to `develop` via PR.
197	- Runs locally only (`npm start`). No MRT deployment for feature branches.
198	- No required status checks beyond lint and unit tests — this tier is for fast iteration.
199	- Delete branch on merge.
200	
201	#### `hotfix/*`
202	- Naming convention: `hotfix/JIRA-456_short-description`
203	- Branched from `main` only. Never from `develop`.
204	- Merges to `main` first, then back-merged to `develop`.
205	- Abbreviated pipeline: skips load test, keeps smoke test and approval gate.
206	- Do not skip the production approval gate under any circumstances.
207	- Tag: `v{major}.{minor}.{patch+1}` — e.g. `v1.3.1`.

211	## Branch → Environment → Trigger Matrix

213	| Branch | Tier | Trigger | Gate |
214	|---|---|---|---|
215	| `feature/*` | LOCAL (developer machine — no MRT deployment) | `npm start` | None — fast iteration |
216	| `develop` | Dev (MRT staging) | Merge to develop | Lint, unit tests, bundle size, security scan |

221	| `hotfix/*` | PROD (expedited) | Merge to main | Abbreviated pipeline, approval gate retained |

225	## SIT Auto-Push Implementation

229	#### 1. GitHub Actions — SIT auto-push job
230	
231	Add a new job to the existing `develop` push workflow. This job must run on every merge to
232	`develop`, after the standard Digital SIT pipeline jobs complete successfully.

234	**File to modify:** `.github/workflows/digital-sit.yml`
235	
236	Add a new job named `deploy-sit` with the following properties:
237	
238	```yaml
239	deploy-sit:
240	  name: Deploy to SIT
241	  needs: [sit-gate]           # only fires after Digital SIT gate passes
242	  if: github.ref == 'refs/heads/develop'
243	  runs-on: ubuntu-latest
244	  environment: sit            # GitHub Environment — requires reviewer approval
245	  steps:
246	    - uses: actions/checkout@v4
247	
248	    - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
249	      with:
250	        node-version: '18'
251	        cache: 'npm'
252	
253	    - name: Install dependencies
254	      run: npm ci
255	
256	    - name: Build bundle
257	      run: npm run build
258	      env:
259	        COMMERCE_API_CLIENT_ID:       ${{ secrets.COMMERCE_API_CLIENT_ID_SIT }}
260	        COMMERCE_API_ORGANIZATION_ID: ${{ secrets.COMMERCE_API_ORG_ID_SIT }}
261	        COMMERCE_API_SHORT_CODE:      ${{ secrets.COMMERCE_API_SHORT_CODE_SIT }}
262	        COMMERCE_API_SITE_ID:         ${{ secrets.COMMERCE_API_SITE_ID_SIT }}
263	
264	    - name: Push bundle to SIT
265	      id: push
266	      run: |
267	        BUNDLE_ID=$(npm run push:sit --silent 2>&1 | grep -oP 'Bundle ID: \K[0-9]+')
268	        echo "bundle_id=$BUNDLE_ID" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
269	      env:
270	        MOBIFY_USER:    ${{ secrets.MRT_USER }}
271	        MOBIFY_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.MRT_API_KEY }}
272	
273	    - name: Activate bundle on SIT
274	      run: BUNDLE_ID=${{ steps.push.outputs.bundle_id }} npm run activate:sit
275	      env:
276	        MOBIFY_USER:    ${{ secrets.MRT_USER }}
277	        MOBIFY_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.MRT_API_KEY }}
278	
279	    - name: Smoke test SIT
280	      run: npm run test:smoke
281	      env:
282	        SMOKE_TEST_URL: ${{ secrets.SIT_URL }}
283	
284	    - name: Notify NewStore team
285	      run: |
286	        echo "SIT updated: bundle ${{ steps.push.outputs.bundle_id }}"
287	        echo "SHA: ${{ github.sha }}"
288	        echo "Triggered by: ${{ github.actor }}"
289	```
