# Environment Strategy, Branching & SIT Pipeline — Claude Code Briefing

## Programme Context

Zimmermann is migrating from Magento 2 to Salesforce Commerce Cloud (SFCC) using the PWA Kit
(`template-retail-react-app`) as the storefront baseline, deployed on Managed Runtime (MRT).

Seven storefronts are in scope: AU, UK, US domestic, US international (Global-e), EU domestic,
EU international (Global-e), and ME. The Digital pipeline must support all six active SFCC
storefronts simultaneously. NewStore (OMS) runs a parallel SIT cycle on its own cadence and
converges with Digital only at the STAGE tier.

Zimmermann has 20 SFCC sandboxes available and no MRT environment licence restriction.
This enables a clean six-tier topology with no shared-environment contention.

---

## Environment Topology — Six Tiers

```
LOCAL  →  DEV  →  SIT (parallel)  →  STAGE  →  UAT  →  PROD
```

### Tier 1 — LOCAL

| Layer | Environment | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| SFCC BM | n/a | Not used locally |
| MRT / PWA | `npm start` (developer machine only — no MRT deployment) | Feature development and local SSR testing |
| 3P systems | All stubs via MSW | No real third-party calls at this tier |
| OMS SIT | Not in scope | NewStore not involved at this tier |

**Who deploys here:** Individual developers run `npm start` locally. No MRT deployment for `feature/*` branches.

**CDN / cache:** n/a — local dev server only.

**Logging:** `debug` level. Source maps exposed.

---

### Tier 2 — DEV (Digital Dev)

| Layer | Environment | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| SFCC BM | SFCC STG org | Jobs: AP21 feed, OCI sync, Lengow |
| MRT / PWA | MRT staging | 7 storefronts, Playwright matrix, Lighthouse CI |
| 3P systems | MuleSoft STG only | All other third parties stubbed via MSW |
| OMS SIT | Not in scope | NewStore not involved at this tier |

**Who deploys here:** CI pipeline on every merge to `develop`. Auto-deployed.

**Gate:** `Digital SIT Gate` — composite GitHub Actions required status check. All four signals
must be green before promotion to STAGE is permitted:
- Playwright P0: 100% pass rate across 6 storefront configs
- Lighthouse CI: Performance ≥ 80, Accessibility ≥ 90, Best Practices ≥ 90
- MuleSoft contract tests: no schema breach
- Bundle size: main.js < 180 kB, vendor.js < 250 kB, main.css < 50 kB

Vitest and Storybook interaction + a11y tests run in `qa.yml` (every PR to `develop`) — they gate
the PR merge, not the environment deploy.

**CDN / cache:** 60s page TTL, 1h asset TTL.

---

### Tier 3 — SIT (NewStore SIT lane — parallel, never gates Digital)

| Layer | Environment | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| SFCC BM | Dedicated sandbox | Mirrors STG config — isolated from Digital STG data |
| MRT / PWA | MRT sit | Auto-receives every develop merge after Digital SIT gate passes |
| 3P systems | NewStore STG, MuleSoft STG, Adyen SBX | Real systems for OMS SIT scope |
| 3P stubs | Global-e, Narvar | Not required for OMS SIT |
| OMS SIT | SIT | NewStore runs 2–3 month SIT cycles here |

**Who deploys here:** CI pipeline auto-push on every `develop` merge. NewStore never deploys
here manually — they consume what the pipeline provides.

**Critical rules:**
- SIT is NOT a Digital gate. Digital promotes independently.
- SIT does NOT gate STAGE. STAGE opens only when OMS SIT is complete AND Digital SIT
  is green — confirmed via Jira environment booking ticket.
- NewStore reports regressions introduced by Digital changes here. Rollback via previous
  bundle ID while Digital fix is prepared.

**Bundle retention:** 10 bundles.

---

### Tier 4 — STAGE (Shared convergence — time-boxed, Jira-booked)

| Layer | Environment | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| SFCC BM | Pre-prod org | Full config, jobs, pricebooks, promotions |
| MRT / PWA | MRT pre-prod | Full stack, all 3P real, Perf + a11y, visual regression |
| 3P systems | All systems real | NewStore STG, MuleSoft STG, Adyen SBX, Global-e STG, Narvar STG |
| OMS SIT | Convergence point | OMS SIT must be COMPLETE before this window opens |

**Who deploys here:** Manual trigger only. Requires Jira booking ticket approved by Zimmermann
environment owner with both entry criteria confirmed green.

**Entry criteria — both must be met before the window opens:**
1. Digital SIT Gate green (GitHub Actions required check passed on `release/*` branch)
2. NewStore OMS SIT complete (sign-off from NewStore project lead on Jira ticket)

**CDN / cache:** 300s page TTL, 24h asset TTL — production-mirrored.

**Gate:** `Environment booking confirmed` — first blocking gate in E2E / Pre-prod quality gates.

---

### Tier 5 — UAT

| Layer | Environment | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| SFCC BM | UAT org | Merch sign-off, production-mirrored config |
| MRT / PWA | MRT UAT | Business acceptance testing, all 6 regions |
| 3P systems | All systems real | Same as STAGE |
| OMS SIT | Feeds UAT | NewStore validated at STAGE — no further OMS SIT required |

**Who deploys here:** Manual trigger. Requires business stakeholder sign-off per region.

**Gate:** `UAT ✓` — Zimmermann stakeholder approval required. Cannot be automated.

---

### Tier 6 — PRODUCTION

| Layer | Environment | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| SFCC BM | PROD org | Live BM config, AU first then wave rollout |
| MRT / PWA | MRT Production | AU canary → all regions via `mrt:activate` |
| 3P systems | All PROD systems | Live credentials, live data |
| OMS SIT | Feeds PROD | NewStore PROD activated with Digital wave rollout |

**Who deploys here:** Release manager only. Manual approval gate in GitHub Environments.

**Gate:** `Production ✓` — named release manager activates bundle. Post-canary smoke test
must pass (error rate < 0.5% over 2h on AU) before remaining regions are opened.

**Rollback:** Single `mrt:activate --target production --bundle-id <PREVIOUS_ID>` command.
Retention: 50 bundles (≈30-day rollback window).

---

## Branching Strategy

### Branch model overview

```
main
 └── release/v*.*.*       ← release candidates, gates UAT + PROD
      └── develop          ← integration baseline, gates Dev + SIT
           └── feature/*   ← feature work, runs locally only (no MRT deployment)
hotfix/*                   ← branches from main, merges back to main + develop
```

### Branch definitions and rules

#### `main`
- Represents production. Always deployable.
- Protected: no direct pushes. Merge via PR from `release/v*.*.*` only.
- Required status checks: `Digital SIT Gate`, `UAT ✓` (manual), post-canary smoke.
- Tag every merge: `v{major}.{minor}.{patch}` — e.g. `v1.3.0`.
- Triggers: production deployment pipeline (manual approval gate).

#### `release/v*.*.*`
- Naming convention: `release/v1.3.0`, `release/v1.3.1` etc.
- Branched from `develop` when a release window is scheduled.
- No new features merged here — bug fixes and release-prep only.
- Required status checks on PR to `main`: `Digital SIT Gate` (run against release branch),
  `UAT ✓`.
- Triggers: STAGE deployment pipeline (manual trigger after Jira booking approved).
- Git tag on branch creation: `release/digital/v1.3.0` — referenced in Jira booking ticket.

#### `develop`
- Integration baseline. All feature branches merge here.
- Protected: no direct pushes. Merge via PR with minimum 1 approval.
- Required status checks on PR merge: lint, unit tests, bundle size, security scan.
- Triggers on merge:
  - Auto-deploy to MRT staging (Dev tier)
  - Auto-push to MRT sit (SIT tier) — fires after `sit-gate` passes
- Git tag convention on significant milestones: `develop/{sprint}/{date}` — e.g.
  `develop/sprint-12/2026-05-09`. Used to anchor SIT bundle reference for NewStore.

#### `feature/*`
- Naming convention: `feature/JIRA-123_short-description`
- Branched from `develop`. Merges back to `develop` via PR.
- Runs locally only (`npm start`). No MRT deployment for feature branches.
- No required status checks beyond lint and unit tests — this tier is for fast iteration.
- Delete branch on merge.

## SIT Auto-Push Implementation

### What needs to be implemented

#### 1. GitHub Actions — SIT auto-push job

Add a new job to the existing `develop` push workflow. This job must run on every merge to
`develop`, after the standard Digital SIT pipeline jobs complete successfully.

**File to modify:** `.github/workflows/digital-sit.yml`

Add a new job named `deploy-sit` with the following properties:

```yaml
deploy-sit:
  name: Deploy to SIT
  needs: [sit-gate]           # only fires after Digital SIT gate passes
  if: github.ref == 'refs/heads/develop'
  runs-on: ubuntu-latest
  environment: sit            # GitHub Environment — requires reviewer approval
  steps:
    - uses: actions/checkout@v4

    - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
      with:
        node-version: '18'
        cache: 'npm'

    - name: Install dependencies
      run: npm ci

    - name: Build bundle
      run: npm run build
      env:
        COMMERCE_API_CLIENT_ID:       ${{ secrets.COMMERCE_API_CLIENT_ID_SIT }}
        COMMERCE_API_ORGANIZATION_ID: ${{ secrets.COMMERCE_API_ORG_ID_SIT }}
        COMMERCE_API_SHORT_CODE:      ${{ secrets.COMMERCE_API_SHORT_CODE_SIT }}
        COMMERCE_API_SITE_ID:         ${{ secrets.COMMERCE_API_SITE_ID_SIT }}

    - name: Push bundle to SIT
      id: push
      run: |
        BUNDLE_ID=$(npm run push:sit --silent 2>&1 | grep -oP 'Bundle ID: \K[0-9]+')
        echo "bundle_id=$BUNDLE_ID" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
      env:
        MOBIFY_USER:    ${{ secrets.MRT_USER }}
        MOBIFY_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.MRT_API_KEY }}

    - name: Activate bundle on SIT
      run: BUNDLE_ID=${{ steps.push.outputs.bundle_id }} npm run activate:sit
      env:
        MOBIFY_USER:    ${{ secrets.MRT_USER }}
        MOBIFY_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.MRT_API_KEY }}

    - name: Smoke test SIT
      run: npm run test:smoke
      env:
        SMOKE_TEST_URL: ${{ secrets.SIT_URL }}

    - name: Notify NewStore team
      run: |
        echo "SIT updated: bundle ${{ steps.push.outputs.bundle_id }}"
        echo "SHA: ${{ github.sha }}"
        echo "Triggered by: ${{ github.actor }}"
```

#### 2. package.json scripts

Add the following scripts to `package.json`. Read the file first and add only what is missing —
do not remove or rename existing scripts:

```json
"push:sit":     "pwa-kit-dev-tools push --target sit",
"activate:sit": "pwa-kit-dev-tools activate --target sit --bundle-id $BUNDLE_ID"
```

#### 3. MRT environment configuration

Add `sit` as a named environment in `mobify.config.js`:

```js
environments: {

  'sit': {
    target: 'sit',

}

#### 9. Git tagging convention script

```bash
#!/bin/bash
# tagRelease.sh — creates and pushes a release tag
# Usage: ./scripts/tagRelease.sh v1.3.0
# Run from the root of the repo after merging to main

set -e

VERSION=$1

if [ -z "$VERSION" ]; then
  echo "Usage: ./scripts/tagRelease.sh v1.3.0"
  exit 1
fi

if ! [[ "$VERSION" =~ ^v[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+$ ]]; then
  echo "Error: version must be in format v{major}.{minor}.{patch}"
  exit 1
fi

git tag -a "$VERSION" -m "Release $VERSION"
git tag -a "release/digital/$VERSION" -m "Digital release candidate $VERSION"
git push origin "$VERSION"
git push origin "release/digital/$VERSION"

echo "Tagged and pushed: $VERSION and release/digital/$VERSION"
```

# Branching Guide — Developer Onboarding

## The four branch types you will use

### feature/* — your daily branch
Branch from: `develop`
Merge back to: `develop` via PR
Naming: `feature/JIRA-123_short-description`
Runs locally only: `npm start` on developer machine. No MRT deployment for feature branches.

# QA Automation Setup — Claude Code prompt
## Zimmermann PWA Kit

> **Status — done. Kept for traceability.** The QA harness this prompt was designed to scaffold
> is already in place. Resulting artefacts:
> [docs/qa/README.md](../../docs/qa/README.md),
> [playwright.config.js](../../playwright.config.js),
> [e2e/features/](../../e2e/features/),
> [e2e/support/pages/](../../e2e/support/pages/),
> [e2e/support/helpers/](../../e2e/support/helpers/),
> [e2e/tests/zimm/](../../e2e/tests/zimm/),
> [.browserstack.yml](../../.browserstack.yml),
> and the `test:sit` script in [package.json](../../package.json).
> Operational guidance for running the harness lives in [docs/qa/README.md](../../docs/qa/README.md).

> Adapted for this project: slim overrides (no monorepo), **Vitest** for unit tests (not Jest),
> TypeScript Page Objects.

---

## Project Context

Magento → Salesforce Commerce Cloud replatform for Zimmermann luxury fashion.
This project is a **slim overrides** project on `@salesforce/retail-react-app` — not a fork, not
a monorepo. Customisations live under `overrides/app/`.

QA model is human-in-the-lead: you generate tests, a Lead QA validates them in plain English,
and you update them based on QA annotations.

**Never treat test generation as complete until the Lead QA has validated the `.feature` file.**

---

## Test Directory Layout

Zimmermann QA files live in `e2e/` at the repo root.

```
e2e/
├── features/            # Gherkin .feature files (SOURCE OF TRUTH)
│   ├── checkout/
│   ├── search/
│   ├── account/
│   ├── integrations/
│   └── regression/      # Magento baseline parity tests
├── fixtures/            # Test data — multi-region aware
│   ├── site.ts          # Regional site configs
│   ├── customers.ts
│   ├── products.ts
│   └── orders.ts
├── support/             # Shared helpers, page objects
│   ├── pages/           # Page Object Model — one file per SFCC page
│   │   ├── basePage.ts
│   │   ├── checkoutPage.ts
│   │   └── productPage.ts
│   └── helpers/
│       └── auth.ts
└── tests/
    └── zimm/            # Zimmermann Playwright tests
        ├── checkout/
        ├── search/
        ├── account/
        └── integrations/
```

**Important notes:**
- `playwright.config.js` at the project root has `testDir: './e2e'` and is the source of truth.
- Unit tests for `overrides/app/` use **Vitest**, not Jest. Tests live alongside the source
  as `*.test.ts`. See [AGENTS.md](../../AGENTS.md) > Testing.
- `vitest.config.*` and `playwright.config.*` are Tier 1 frozen files — see
  [.claude/rules/frozenFiles.md](../../.claude/rules/frozenFiles.md).

---

## Gherkin Feature File Standard

All `.feature` files must follow this format. This is non-negotiable — QAs read these files.

```gherkin
@SFCC-142 @checkout @p0
Feature: [Feature name matching Jira story title]
  As a [persona]
  I want to [goal]
  So that [value]

  Background:
    Given I am on the Zimmermann storefront
    And the following products are available:
      | SKU     | Name          | Price  | Stock |
      | ITEM-001 | Example Item  | $350   | 10    |

  Scenario: [Happy path — descriptive name]
    Given [precondition]
    When [action]
    Then [expected outcome]

  Scenario: [Edge case or failure path]
    Given [precondition]
    When [action]
    Then [expected outcome]
    And [additional assertion]

  Scenario Outline: [Data-driven scenario]
    Given I am logged in as a "<customer_type>" customer
    When I add "<product>" to cart
    Then I see price "<expected_price>"

    Examples:
      | customer_type | product     | expected_price |
      | guest         | ITEM-001     | $350           |
      | registered    | ITEM-001     | $350           |
```

**Rules:**
- One `.feature` file per Jira story
- File name: `{JIRA-KEY}_{short-description}.feature` e.g. `SFCC-142_guest-checkout.feature`
- Always include at least one happy path and one failure/edge scenario
- Background block for shared preconditions — never repeat setup in every scenario
- Plain English only — no technical implementation detail in `.feature` files
- P0 journeys (Digital SIT gate) must be tagged `@p0` — their spec files use `.p0.spec.ts` naming
- When QA annotates a correction, update the `.feature` file first, then regenerate the Playwright test

---

## Playwright Test Generation Rules

Generate Playwright tests from `.feature` files using the Page Object Model.

```typescript
// e2e/tests/zimm/checkout/SFCC-142_guest-checkout.p0.spec.ts
// P0 tests use .p0.spec.ts — picked up by the Digital SIT gate on every release/** PR

import {test, expect} from '@playwright/test'
import {CheckoutPage} from '../../../support/pages/checkoutPage'
import {ProductPage} from '../../../support/pages/productPage'
import {guestCustomer} from '../../../fixtures/customers'
import {standardProduct} from '../../../fixtures/products'

// Test name must match the Scenario name in the .feature file exactly
test('Guest customer completes checkout with credit card', async ({page}) => {
    const productPage = new ProductPage(page)
    const checkoutPage = new CheckoutPage(page)
    const customer = guestCustomer()
    const product = standardProduct()

    await productPage.goToProduct(product.sku)
    await productPage.addToCart()
    await checkoutPage.proceedAsGuest(customer)
    await checkoutPage.enterShipping(customer)
    await checkoutPage.confirmOrder()

    await expect(checkoutPage.orderConfirmation).toBeVisible()
    await expect(checkoutPage.orderNumber).toBeVisible()
})
```

**Rules:**
- Page Object Model is mandatory — selectors live in `e2e/support/pages/` only
- Test file name mirrors `.feature` file name: same Jira key, same description
- Test descriptions must match Scenario names in the `.feature` file exactly
- No hardcoded selectors, URLs, or data values in test files
- Selector priority: accessible selectors (role + accessible name, label, text) → semantic HTML attributes (alt, title) → `data-testid` (only when no semantics apply)
- Use `waitForResponse` or `waitForSelector` — never `page.waitForTimeout()`
- P0 tests → `.p0.spec.ts` (Playwright p0 project, retries: 0, runs in SIT gate)
- Standard tests → `.spec.ts` (runs in BrowserStack cross-browser, release PRs only)

---

## Page Object Model Pattern

```typescript
// e2e/support/pages/checkoutPage.ts

import type {Page, Locator} from '@playwright/test'
import {BasePage} from './basePage'

type Customer = {email: string; firstName: string; lastName: string}

export class CheckoutPage extends BasePage {
    readonly orderConfirmation: Locator
    readonly orderNumber: Locator
    readonly emailField: Locator
    readonly continueAsGuestButton: Locator

    constructor(page: Page) {
        super(page)
        // Selector priority: accessible (role, label, text) → semantic (alt, title) → data-testid
        this.emailField = page.getByRole('textbox', {name: /email/i})
        this.continueAsGuestButton = page.getByRole('button', {name: /guest checkout/i})
        // data-testid only where the element has no accessible/semantic anchor
        this.orderConfirmation = page.getByTestId('order-confirmation')
        this.orderNumber = page.getByTestId('order-number')
    }

    async proceedAsGuest(customer: Customer) {
        await this.goto('/checkout')
        await this.emailField.fill(customer.email)
        await this.continueAsGuestButton.click()
        await this.page.waitForLoadState()
    }
}
```

---

## Unit Test Pattern (Vitest)

This project uses **Vitest** — not Jest. Do not reference Jest, create `jest.config.*`, or
suggest switching test runners. `vitest.config.*` is a Tier 1 frozen file.

Unit tests live alongside their component or hook in `overrides/app/`:

```typescript
// overrides/app/components/productTile/index.test.ts

import {renderWithProviders} from '../../utils/testUtils'
import {screen} from '@testing-library/react'
import {describe, it, expect} from 'vitest'
import ProductTile from './index'
import {mockProduct, mockSaleProduct} from './testFixtures'

describe('ProductTile', () => {
    it('renders product name and price', () => {
        renderWithProviders(<ProductTile product={mockProduct} />)
        expect(screen.getByText(mockProduct.name)).toBeInTheDocument()
    })

    it('shows sale price when product is on sale', () => {
        renderWithProviders(<ProductTile product={mockSaleProduct} />)
        expect(screen.getByTestId('sale-price')).toBeInTheDocument()
    })
})
```

Component-interaction coverage typically belongs in a Storybook `play` function rather than
a Vitest test — see [AGENTS.md](../../AGENTS.md) > Testing.

---

## Multi-Region Fixtures

Zimmermann serves 6 regions across 7 SFCC sites (US is one site; EU is two — domestic + international). All test data must be
region-aware **from day one**.

```typescript
// e2e/fixtures/site.ts — set SITE_ID env var to switch regions (default: au)
// Site IDs and locale IDs verified against bkzk-002 BM (2026-06-13)
export const SITE_CONFIGS = {
    au:     {locale: 'en',    currency: 'AUD', currencySymbol: 'A$',  siteId: 'ZimmermannAU'},
    us:     {locale: 'en-US', currency: 'USD', currencySymbol: '$',   siteId: 'ZimmermannUS'},
    uk:     {locale: 'en-GB', currency: 'GBP', currencySymbol: '£',   siteId: 'ZimmermannUK'},
    eu:     {locale: 'en-GB', currency: 'EUR', currencySymbol: '€',   siteId: 'ZimmermannEU'},
    euIntl: {locale: 'en-CH', currency: 'EUR', currencySymbol: '€',   siteId: 'ZimmermannEUIntl'},
    hk:     {locale: 'en-HK', currency: 'HKD', currencySymbol: 'HK$', siteId: 'ZimmermannHK'},
    me:     {locale: 'en-AE', currency: 'AED', currencySymbol: 'AED', siteId: 'ZimmermannME'},
} as const
```

```bash
SITE_ID=us npx playwright test e2e/tests/zimm
```

> `config/sites.js` is still the OOTB Salesforce default — customise for the 7-site setup
> before wiring fixtures end-to-end. Track as a separate work item.

---

## BrowserStack Configuration

See [.browserstack.yml](../../.browserstack.yml) at the repo root.

---

## CI/CD — GitHub Actions

`qa.yml` runs unit tests, then BrowserStack on `release/**` PRs only. See
[docs/ciCd/workflowMap.md](../../docs/ciCd/workflowMap.md) and the qa workflow itself.

**Branch naming:** this project uses `feature/*` branches. Integration branch is `develop`.
Never trigger automated workflows that write to `develop` or `main`.

---

## Magento Baseline Regression Tests

These live in `e2e/features/regression/` and document expected Magento 2 behaviour.
Generated during Sprint 1 (Foundation) from the Magento baseline.

Naming convention: `BASELINE-{area}-{behaviour}.feature`

Examples:
- `BASELINE-checkout-guest-flow.feature`
- `BASELINE-search-filters-applied.feature`
- `BASELINE-account-order-history.feature`

**When a regression test fails against SFCC:**
1. Do NOT automatically update the test to pass
2. Add a comment: `# DELTA: SFCC behaviour differs from Magento baseline — [description]`
3. Surface to Lead QA for human decision: bug, intentional change, or SFCC constraint

---

## QA Annotation Workflow

See [docs/qa/README.md](../../docs/qa/README.md) > "QA annotation workflow".

---

## Zephyr Traceability Requirements

Every `.feature` file must include the Jira story key as a tag:

```gherkin
@SFCC-142 @checkout @p0
Feature: Guest Checkout
```

This tag links BrowserStack Test Observability results to the correct Jira story in Zephyr.
Without it, traceability breaks and results cannot be synced.

Confirm the Zephyr integration method (Scale vs Squad) with the QA Lead before activating
Test Observability sync.

---

## Token Budget for Test Generation

- `.feature` file: under 150 lines. Split into multiple files by scenario group if exceeded.
- Playwright test file: under 200 lines. Extract shared logic to `e2e/support/helpers/`.
- Page Object file: under 150 lines. One page = one file. Split by section if needed.

Stop and refactor before continuing if you exceed these limits.

---

## What NOT to Do

- Never write selectors directly in test files — always Page Objects
- Never hardcode test data in test files — always fixtures
- Never update a baseline regression test to pass without Lead QA sign-off
- Never generate a Playwright test before the `.feature` file has been validated by QA
- Never add `@skip` tags without a Jira ticket reference and Lead QA approval
- Never use `page.waitForTimeout()` — use `waitForSelector` or `waitForResponse`
- Never generate tests that only test the happy path
- Never modify `vitest.config.*`, `playwright.config.*`, or any Tier 1 configuration file
- Never operate on `develop` or `main` branches

1	# Architecture
2	
3	*Key technical decisions, stack overview, overrides pattern, component organisation, and key paths. Update this file when the stack changes, a new integration is added, or a structural decision is made.*
4	
5	Production storefront for www.zimmermann.com — multi-locale, multi-currency, seven storefronts across six regions (AU, US, UK, EU, HK, ME), with the EU as two storefronts (domestic + international).
6	
7	## Pre-Build Decisions
8	
9	These decisions affect tooling, CI, and code shape that's hard to retrofit later. Status as of 2026-05-29.
10	
11	| # | Decision | Status |
12	|---|---|---|
13	| 1 | Browser & device matrix | ✅ Confirmed (informal) |
14	| 2 | Accessibility manual testing | 🟡 Partial — vendor info pending |
15	| 3 | Performance budgets | ✅ Confirmed (informal) |
16	| 4 | Client-side error reporting | ⚪ Accepted risk — no tool |
17	| 5 | Feature-flag tool | ⚪ Accepted risk — Optimizely Web only |
18	| 6 | Translation fallback chain | 🟡 Partial — Brand/Legal pending |
19	
20	### #1 — Browser & device matrix ✅
21	**Mobile perf-test floor:** current OS version −2 on iPhone and Android (iOS 17+, Android 14+), verified via BrowserStack Automate. `package.json` browserslist aligned to match.
22	**Desktop matrix** ([.browserstack.yml](../../.browserstack.yml)): Chrome + Safari (macOS Sonoma), Firefox + Edge (Windows 11) — all latest.
23	
24	### #2 — Accessibility 🟡
25	**Target:** WCAG 2.2 AA, at least 2.1 AA. **Automated:** axe-core in Vitest + Playwright; Storybook a11y addon; Lighthouse CI a11y ≥0.90 ([lighthouserc.js](../../lighthouserc.js)). **Manual:** client's existing a11y vendor.
26	**Pending:** vendor name, screen-reader/browser matrix, audit cadence, remediation owner.
27	
28	### #3 — Performance budgets ✅
29	**Client-mandated:** **LCP ≤ 2s** at p75 mobile, plus Lighthouse Performance ≥ 0.80, Accessibility ≥ 0.90, Best Practices ≥ 0.90. These are the only performance numbers in the signed TSD (§9).
30	**Other CWV (internal working defaults, not client-mandated):** INP ≤ 200ms · CLS ≤ 0.1. Lighthouse mobile defaults at p75.
31	**CI gate (SIT gate):** Lighthouse CI (`@lhci/cli`) asserts the Lighthouse score floors above, plus a >5pt trend-drop gate (LHCI server required). SEO intentionally not asserted. Runs on every PR to `develop` ([`digital-sit.yml`](../../.github/workflows/digital-sit.yml)), deploys to the **Dev** tier on merge — treat its numbers as a **regression indicator**, not the contractual measurement.
32	**Contractual measurement:** Client-mandated LCP and Lighthouse numbers are validated on **Stage** — the prod-mimicking tier (same MRT bundle size class, same CDN/edge configuration, same SFCC realm tier as production). The Dev tier is slower and further from the edge, so its absolute numbers will be worse — that is expected and not a sign-off concern. Full environment topology in [tsd-architecture.md §14.1](./temp/tsd-architecture.md).
33	**Bundle ceilings — internal CI policy, NOT client requirements:** `main.js` 180 kB · `vendor.js` 250 kB · `main.css` 50 kB (`bundlesize` in `package.json`). (These were set as aspirational targets early in the project. As of the last measurement the actual sizes are well above these ceilings (`main.js` ~352 kB, `vendor.js` ~2 MB) before any optimisation pass — the ceilings need to be re-baselined against measured size + a growth-only headroom (e.g. current + 10–15%) once a baseline pass is done.) Their purpose is regression detection, not a client-facing commitment.
34	**Third-party script weight:** uncapped — tight LCP is the de-facto constraint. See AGENTS.md > Performance for the deferral rule.
35	
36	### #6 — Translation fallback 🟡
37	[regional.md](./prd/regional.md) REG-046: "English is the site-wide fallback." Doesn't disambiguate `en-eu` vs `en`, nor split by content type.
38	**Pending Brand/Legal decision** on the rule per content type:
39	
40	| Content type | Suggested chain | Why |
41	|---|---|---|
42	| UI strings | `fr-eu` → `en-eu` → `en` | Universal meaning |
43	| Editorial | `fr-eu` → `en-eu` → hide | Avoid half-translated pages |
44	| Product copy | `fr-eu` → `en-eu` → hide | Care/sizing are region-specific (regulatory) |
45	
46	REG-047 (Contentful↔Transperfect↔SFCC workflow) remains separately TBC.
47	
48	### Accepted risks
49	
50	**#4 — No client-side error reporting.** JS errors in customer browsers (e.g. Adyen iframe failure on a specific iOS Safari version) are invisible to the team; detection relies on support tickets. Revisit post-launch if checkout completion dips unexplained.
51	
52	**#5 — No feature-flag tool.** Optimizely Web Experimentation ([analytics.md](./prd/analytics.md) AAB-004) covers analytics A/B. Note (confirmed 09-06): Optimizely is **not** a GTM tag — the PWA loads its script directly in the page head (US storefront only, single snippet across environments, before render to avoid flicker), Didomi-gated. Progressive rollout, social login dark-launch, and August-2026 payment-method gating will be handled via deploy timing and branch merges — no instant kill-switch, no % rollouts.
53	
54	## Frontend Stack
55	
56	### Bundled by PWA Kit
57	| Layer | Library | Notes |
58	|---|---|---|
59	| Base framework | PWA Kit v3+ | Salesforce storefront foundation |
60	| UI framework | React 18 + Chakra UI | Component library + theme system |
61	| Routing | React Router v6 | |
62	| Server/async state | TanStack Query (via `@salesforce/commerce-sdk-react`) | All SFCC data fetching |
63	| i18n | react-intl | Translations in `translations/` |
64	| Build + dev server | Webpack 5 (via `pwa-kit-dev`) | |
65	| Build + test runner (legacy) | Jest (via `pwa-kit-dev test`) | `jest.config.js` — kept for PWA Kit internals; superseded by Vitest for project tests |
66	
67	### Project additions
68	| Layer | Library | Notes |
69	|---|---|---|
70	| Type safety | TypeScript strict mode | `tsconfig.json` |
71	| Component explorer + interaction tests | Storybook 8 | `storybook dev -p 6006`; `play` functions are the primary tool for component-level interaction testing |
72	| Storybook a11y addon | `@storybook/addon-a11y` | Component-level accessibility checks during development and in Storybook test runs |
73	| Unit test runner | Vitest | `vitest.config.ts`; replaces `pwa-kit-dev test` for project tests |
74	| Accessibility testing | axe-core (via `vitest-axe` / `axe-playwright`) | Automated WCAG checks in unit and E2E layers; see Pre-Build Decisions #2 for outstanding items |
75	| E2E tests (planned) | Playwright | Not yet configured |
76	| Forms + validation | react-hook-form + zod | Not yet installed; add when checkout/account work begins |
77	| Global UI state | Zustand | For shared state that outgrows Context (multi-step flows, drawer state, etc.). **SSR note:** initialise store per-request — never as a module singleton — to prevent state leaking across server-rendered requests. |
78	
79	### External services
80	Salesforce Commerce Cloud, Contentful Studio CMS, Global-e (international checkout + server-side pricing/catalogue feed — PRC-34..43 sign-off pending), Didomi (consent), GTM hosted on Addingwell (data layer + downstream tag loading via Tell No Lies). Full integration map below.
81	
82	## Environments
83	
84	Six-tier topology spans **Local → Dev → SIT → Stage → UAT → Prod**. Each tier (other than Local) has its own SFCC realm, Contentful environment, and MuleSoft connections. Ownership splits across three zones — Digital, IT/NewStore, and Shared (Digital + Business).
85	
86	| # | Tier | Owner | Purpose | Third-party availability | Deploy trigger |
87	|---|---|---|---|---|---|
88	| 1 | **Local** | Digital | Feature build on developer machines | All services mocked (MSW stubs) | `npm start` |
89	| 2 | **Dev** | Digital | Integrated digital testing across all 6 storefronts, independent of NewStore | MuleSoft STG · NewStore Dev · Omneo STG · Narvar stub · Adyen sandbox | Merge to `develop` |
90	| 3 | **SIT** | IT / NewStore | NewStore SIT and regression on its own cadence | NewStore STG · MuleSoft STG · Narvar STG · AP21 test | NewStore release cadence (parallel lane, non-blocking for Digital releases) |
91	| 4 | **Stage** (E2E) | Shared | End-to-end testing with all third parties live; time-boxed booked windows | NewStore STG · MuleSoft STG · Omneo STG · Narvar STG · Adyen sandbox | Booked 2-week window |
92	| 5 | **UAT** | Shared | Business acceptance across all 6 regions | NewStore STG · Narvar STG · Omneo STG · Adyen sandbox | Business approval gate |
93	| 6 | **Prod** | Live | Production; AU canary then flag-flip to remaining regions | NewStore PROD · MuleSoft PROD · Omneo PROD · Narvar PROD · Adyen PROD | Release manager + canary gate |
94	
95	**Stage** is the contractual performance-test environment referenced under [Pre-Build Decisions #3](#3--performance-budgets-) — it mirrors production infrastructure (same MRT bundle class, CDN/edge configuration, SFCC realm tier).
96	
97	**QA workflow** ([`qa.yml`](../.github/workflows/qa.yml)) runs on every PR to `develop` and `release/**`: Vitest unit tests and Storybook interaction + `@storybook/addon-a11y` component-level accessibility checks (`storybook test --ci`), in parallel. Code-correctness checks that run before any environment is involved.
98	
99	**SIT gate** ([`digital-sit.yml`](../.github/workflows/digital-sit.yml)) runs on push/PR to `release/**`: Playwright `p0` specs, bundle-size check, MuleSoft contract tests, Lighthouse CI thresholds, LHCI trend gate. Environment-dependent checks against the deployed Dev tier. On merge to `develop` it also deploys to Dev. Production deploys are gated on a clean SIT gate run plus stakeholder approval through Stage and UAT.
100	
101	**MRT targets** in [mobify.config.js](../mobify.config.js) map one-to-one to the topology: `dev | sit | stage | uat | production`. `ENVIRONMENT_NAME` (`local | dev | sit | stage | uat | prod`) is the per-tier tag emitted to Sentry, New Relic, and GTM.
102	
103	## SSR Requirement (DMU-030)
104	Server-side rendering is **mandatory** for product, category, and content pages (DMU-030, signed off). PWA Kit's SSR pipeline must be preserved — do not introduce client-only patterns (e.g. `typeof window !== 'undefined'` short-circuits, client-only data fetching on first paint, or `next/dynamic`-style `{ ssr: false }`) on these page types. Any componentry that cannot render on the server must be gated behind a hydration-safe boundary that still emits SEO-relevant markup on the server.
105	
106	## Overrides Pattern
107	All customizations live in `overrides/` mirroring the structure of `node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/`. Never edit `node_modules/`.
108	
109	**Minimise custom code.** When implementing Zimmermann's design and layout, stay as close to the base PWA Kit implementation as possible. Style changes (CSS, Chakra props, theme tokens) are always expected and need no confirmation. Structural changes — restructuring components, altering data flow, or significantly deviating from base template behaviour — must be confirmed with the user before proceeding.
110	
111	**Before any change:** check whether the file exists in `overrides/`. If not, create the override:
112	1. Copy from `node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/` to the mirrored path in `overrides/`.
113	2. Rename `.js`/`.jsx` → `.ts`/`.tsx`. Replace `PropTypes` with TypeScript `type` definitions. Add explicit types to all parameters, return values, and props. Use Commerce SDK types (`commerce-sdk-isomorphic`, `@salesforce/commerce-sdk-react`) where available. No `as any` or `// @ts-ignore`.
114	3. Verify `npx tsc --noEmit` passes with zero errors.
115	4. **Stop. Present the converted file to the user and wait for approval before making any functional changes.**
116	
117	## New vs. Override Components
118	- **Overriding a base template component:** copy from `node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/` to the mirrored path in `overrides/` (see Overrides Pattern above).
119	- **Brand-new components** (no base template equivalent): create them in `overrides/app/components/custom/`.
120	
121	## Key Paths
122	- **Country/locale/currency mappings:** `overrides/app/config/countries.ts` — single source of truth for URL slugs, locales, currencies, shipping countries, Global-e flag, and boutique regions. When adding a market also update `config/sites.js`.
123	- **Contentful config:** `overrides/app/config/contentful.ts` — always render locale-specific content using Contentful's native localisation fields. Gate preview/draft content behind a server-side check; never expose draft content in production.
124	- **Theme / design tokens:** `overrides/app/theme/` — `index.ts` composes the theme; brand tokens live in `foundation/` (colour, fonts, typography, gridSystem, spacing — Tier 1, UI Designer owned); per-component overrides live one file each in `components/` (e.g. `header.ts`, `listMenu.ts` — Tier 2). Register a new component override in `components/index.ts`.
125	- **App shell (Header/Footer):** `overrides/app/components/_app/index.tsx`
126	- **Header:** `overrides/app/components/header/index.tsx`
127	- **Custom components:** `overrides/app/components/custom/`
128	- **Assets:** `overrides/app/static/`, `overrides/app/assets/svg/`
129	
130	## Design Source of Truth
131	Figma file "29 April 2026" is the **current working draft** — not a signed-off final design. Implementations based on it are client-preview builds and may need to be revised when designs are finalised. Do not treat any Figma-derived decision as confirmed without explicit sign-off.
132	
133	Desktop prototype at zimm-prototype.vercel.app is AI-generated and desktop-only — also not a signed-off final design.
134	
135	## Header Layout (based on draft Figma, subject to change)
136	Two rows: top bar (nav + icons) and logo row. Implemented in `overrides/app/components/header/index.tsx`, with Chakra theme overrides split across `overrides/app/theme/components/header.ts` and `overrides/app/theme/components/listMenu.ts`.
137	
138	**Logo**: uses `BrandLogo` from the icons package (PWA default with the svg file replaced). The Z.IMMERSE variant has not been implemented yet.
139	
140	**ListMenu active-state gotcha**: `listMenuTriggerLinkActive` is JS-spread *after* `listMenuTriggerLink` on the same `<Link>` element. Any `_after` key in the active style entirely replaces the base `_after` object — all CSS properties must be repeated, not just the overriding ones.
141	
142	**Icons deferred**: Boutique, Contact, Newsletter (HPC-015) — icon assets not provided yet.
143	
144	**Base functionality retained**: All hooks, the account popover, wishlist, store locator, and all existing props are unchanged. Only layout and visual style changed so far.
145	
146	## Contentful Content Type Management
147	
148	Content types (schema) are never created manually in the Contentful web app. They are defined in code and synced via a script. This makes schema changes reviewable, repeatable, and team-safe.
149	
150	**Key paths:**
151	- `scripts/contentful/sync.js` — runner: upserts (creates or updates) and publishes every content type in the definitions directory
152	- `scripts/contentful/content-types/` — one `.js` file per content type (e.g. `shoppableImage.js`)
153	
154	**To register a new content type:**
155	1. Add a definition file to `scripts/contentful/content-types/<contentTypeId>.js` (see existing files for shape)
156	2. Run `npm run sync:contentful`
157	
158	**To run the sync:**
159	```
160	npm run sync:contentful
161	```
162	Requires `CONTENTFUL_MANAGEMENT_TOKEN` in `.env` at the repo root (never commit). Get it from `app.contentful.com/account/profile/cma_tokens`. `CONTENTFUL_SPACE_ID` and `CONTENTFUL_ENVIRONMENT_ID` are already in `.env`.
163	
164	The script is idempotent — safe to re-run. It preserves any existing fields not in the definition file (it will not delete fields from a live content type).
165	
166	**Relationship to the React component:**
167	Each content type definition in `scripts/contentful/content-types/` corresponds to a React component in `overrides/app/components/contentful/`. The content type's field IDs must match the TypeScript type in `overrides/app/types/contentful.ts`.
168	
169	**Experience Builder components** (drag-and-drop in Contentful Studio) are a separate concern — they are registered in `overrides/app/components/contentful/experiences/definitions.ts` and do not need a corresponding `sync:contentful` entry unless they also have a standard content type for use outside Studio.
170	
171	## Path Aliases
172	Configured in four places (keep in sync):
173	- `babel.config.js` — `babel-plugin-module-resolver` (covers `npm start` dev server + `npm run build`)
174	- `tsconfig.json` — `baseUrl` + `paths` (TypeScript / VS Code intellisense)
175	- `.storybook/main.js` — `webpackFinal` alias
176	- `jest.config.js` — `moduleNameMapper` (PWA Kit internals)
177	- `vitest.config.ts` — `resolve.alias` (project tests)
178	
179	| Alias | Resolves to |
180	|---|---|
181	| `~` | project root |
182	| `app` | `overrides/app` |
183	
184	## Integration Map
185	
186	All order-creation, fulfilment write, and CRM sync traffic from SFCC routes through MuleSoft as the middleware layer — SFCC does not call NewStore, AP21, Omneo, or Narvar directly. In addition, the PWA's MRT Node layer calls MuleSoft directly for read operations (order history, order details, boutique / BOPIS stock check, real-time stock availability, GiveX balance check) — SFCC is not in those read paths. A handful of services are also called **browser-direct from the PWA** and another set are **SFCC cartridge integrations** invoked server-side. The `Boundary` column makes this explicit so you know where to look when an integration breaks.
187	
188	**Boundary key:**
189	- **PWA-direct** — called from the browser directly. Vendor key (if any) is publishable/public and safe in the bundle.
190	- **MRT-mediated** — called from the PWA's Node layer via `/mobify/proxy/` or a server-only endpoint. API credentials held as MRT environment variables; never reach the browser bundle. Includes direct PWA → MuleSoft calls via MRT proxy.
191	- **SFCC (OOTB)** — Salesforce-bundled integration; no custom cartridge.
192	- **SFCC (cartridge)** — vendor-supplied or custom server-side cartridge running inside SFCC.
193	- **SFCC → MuleSoft** — SFCC calls MuleSoft, which fans out to the downstream system.
194	- **Browser handoff** — PWA hands the user off to a third party's hosted experience.
195	- **Out-of-band** — no runtime call from PWA or SFCC; the integration delivers data via a separate channel.
196	
197	| System | Role | Boundary | Notes |
198	|---|---|---|---|
199	| **Salesforce Commerce Cloud (SFCC)** | Storefront, product catalogue, order management (record of truth), customer accounts, Business Manager config | — | Domestic checkout owner |
200	| **MuleSoft** | Middleware / integration layer | SFCC → MuleSoft + MRT-mediated (direct PWA → MuleSoft calls) | All SFCC ↔ OMS, SFCC ↔ Omneo, SFCC ↔ Narvar calls go via MuleSoft. Select PWA operations also call MuleSoft directly via the MRT proxy layer (`/mobify/proxy/mulesoft/...`) with credentials held as MRT environment variables |
201	| **NewStore OMS** | Order management system, carrier selection, dispatch, label generation, boutique inventory; **system of record for order history** (no Magento order history is migrated — DMU-007/008) | SFCC → MuleSoft (writes) + MRT-mediated (reads) | **Write path (SFCC → MuleSoft → NewStore):** order creation, fulfilment, BOPIS. **Read path (MRT → MuleSoft → NewStore):** order history (CRM-056–057), order details (CRM-071–072), boutique / BOPIS stock check (CFD-043), real-time stock availability. SFCC is not in the read path. The customer-identification mechanism on the read path is **unconfirmed** (open item) — either MRT forwards the customer's SLAS JWT for MuleSoft to validate, or MRT passes the customer ID as a request parameter; whichever is agreed must prevent retrieval of an arbitrary customer's data |
202	| **AP21** | Retail Rewards (loyalty/VIP), product master, composition/material data; **source of product and pricing master data** | SFCC → MuleSoft | Real-time AP21 call at login for Retail Rewards balance; used for HS codes via Avalara. **Product and pricing feed** flows inbound AP21 → MuleSoft → SFCC to populate the SFCC catalogue and pricebooks the PWA reads via SCAPI; feed cadence and exact field set TBC. |
203	| **Omneo** | CRM sync layer / system of record for customer identity and loyalty | SFCC → MuleSoft | SFCC ↔ Omneo via MuleSoft; Omneo → Emarsys for marketing emails |
204	| **Emarsys** | Email marketing platform | Out-of-band | Receives opt-in/opt-out from Omneo; sends welcome and marketing emails |
205	| **Adyen** | Payment processing (all domestic storefronts) | SFCC (cartridge) + PWA-direct (Drop-in / Components SDK at checkout) | Credit/debit, PayPal, saved cards (tokens only). Apple Pay, Google Pay, Klarna targeting August 2026. Adyen Web Drop-in loads in the browser at checkout for tokenisation and 3DS2 challenges. As payment processing is strictly necessary (contractual necessity, not analytics/marketing tracking), the Drop-in is **not** Didomi consent-gated — it loads at the payment step regardless of consent choices. The fail-closed consent rule applies to analytics/marketing scripts, not to the payment flow. |
206	| **Global-e** | International checkout owner (HK, ME, all international orders) + server-side pricing/catalogue feed into SFCC | PWA-direct (iframe embed at checkout) + SFCC server-side (pricing/catalogue feed) | (1) **Iframe embed at checkout** — Global-e hosted checkout renders inside an iframe on a Zimmermann checkout route (not a full-page redirect). SFCC sends complete cart in target currency at handoff. CSP `frame-src` must allowlist the Global-e origin. (2) Server-side feed — nightly FX rates / coefficients / rounding rules from Global-e generate Global-e-market pricebooks in SFCC (PRC-34..43); daily SFCC → Global-e catalogue CSV via SFTP (PRC-54); GiveX validate/redeem/refund webhooks exposed to Global-e (PRC-44). REG-041 confirmed; PRC-34..43 final sign-off pending. |
207	| **Booxi** | Boutique appointment booking (My Account → appointment history; CRM-165–167) | MRT-mediated (PWA → MRT → Booxi) | **Not a MuleSoft path** — the PWA calls Booxi directly from the MRT Node layer; SFCC and MuleSoft are not involved. Booxi credentials held as MRT environment variables. Previously referred to as "Booksy" in older notes — Booxi is the correct vendor. Scope still TBC. |
208	| **Narvar** | EDD at checkout (Promise widget, formerly CONVERT), domestic order confirmation emails, shipping confirmation, tracking portal, returns portal | SFCC → MuleSoft (backend); PWA-direct (Promise widget) | Narvar is NOT used for international orders (Global-e owns those) |
209	| **Contentful** | CMS for editorial/homepage content, size guides, promotional banners | PWA-direct (CDA) + MRT-mediated (CPA preview, publish webhook) | Contentful Studio with live preview; locale-specific content via Contentful native localisation. Content types are managed via `npm run sync:contentful` — see Contentful Content Type Management below. Cache invalidation on entry publish via a Contentful → MRT webhook, HMAC-verified with `CMS_WEBHOOK_SECRET`. |
210	| **Vimeo** | Product video hosting (PDP gallery, runway/campaign clips — PRD-066/067) | PWA-direct (lazy embed) | Product videos referenced by embed URL stored in product data or the CMS; loaded behind a lightweight facade (poster image + click/scroll-to-load) so the Vimeo player JS stays off the LCP critical path. Editorial-page video is Contentful by default but may also embed Vimeo by URL (HPC-004). PRD-067 (Vimeo as the chosen platform) is still Open. |
211	| **Didomi** | Consent management platform (CMP) | PWA-direct | Cookie banner, preference persistence; GTM integrated via Google Consent Mode v2 |
212	| **Google Maps API** | Address autocomplete at checkout (delivery + billing) | MRT-mediated | API key held as MRT environment variable; calls proxied through `/mobify/proxy/google/...`. Replaces PCA Predict/Loqate. Graceful degradation to manual entry if unavailable. |
213	| **Google Tag Manager (GTM)** | Tag orchestration, data-layer consumer, Google Consent Mode v2, Enhanced Conversions; loads downstream marketing tags (Meta, Pinterest, TikTok, GA4, etc.) via Tell No Lies. **Optimizely Web and Crazy Egg are NOT in the GTM container** (confirmed 09-06, AAB-004/005) — see their own rows. | PWA-direct (post-consent), loaded from Addingwell first-party domain | GTM container is **hosted on Addingwell** (Didomi-owned managed tagging server) — the browser fetches `gtm.js` from a Zimmermann first-party subdomain, not `googletagmanager.com`. Container and downstream tag logic owned by Tell No Lies. PWA's responsibility ends at correctly emitting the data layer (AAB-001/002) and pointing the loader at the Addingwell hostname. Hashed email passed at order confirmation for Enhanced Conversions (REG-056). |
214	| **Optimizely Web** | A/B testing & experimentation (AAB-004) | PWA-direct front-end head tag (post-consent) | **Not a GTM tag.** PWA loads the Optimizely snippet directly in the page **head before render** (anti-flicker). **US storefront only; single snippet across all environments.** Zimmermann provides the script. Didomi-gated (Analytics). SFCC populates the data-layer segmentation attributes (authenticated state, customer group, loyalty status, storefront region, new vs returning, device type) per AAB-002. |
215	| **Crazy Egg** | Heatmapping & session replay (AAB-005) | PWA-direct front-end head tag (post-consent) | **Not a GTM tag.** PWA loads the Crazy Egg snippet directly in the page head — **async and post-Didomi-consent**, so it never blocks first paint (no anti-flicker exemption, unlike Optimizely). Didomi-gated (Analytics). SFCC populates data-layer attributes (page type, authenticated state, storefront region) per AAB-002. |
216	| **Avalara** | Tax calculation for US domestic, NZ, New Caledonia, and EU domestic | SFCC (cartridge) | EU domestic added 2026-06-19 (Third_Party_Integrations sheet update). UK uses SFCC native VAT tables; all other storefronts use SFCC native tax tables. |
217	| **GiveX** | Gift card processing | SCAPI/SFCC → NewStore adapter → GiveX for validate/redeem/refund + SCAPI/SFCC → MuleSoft → NewStore → GiveX for issuance + MRT → MuleSoft → GiveX for balance check (no SFCC GiveX cartridge) | GiveX speaks **persistent TCP socket** with JSON-RPC/XML-RPC payloads — not directly callable from MRT. **MuleSoft owns the socket pool, failover (primary + secondary host, Failover-Reversal 2.0 retry/iteration suffix), GiveX stuser credentials, and x509 peer certs** for the balance-check leg; the issuance and redemption legs reach GiveX downstream via NewStore. MRT exposes an HTTPS balance-check endpoint that proxies to MuleSoft and returns a typed JSON response to the PWA. The balance-check request carries the card number **and PIN** (secure PINs enabled — both payment credentials, POST body only, never logged). Checkout redemption flows server-side (PWA → SCAPI/SFCC → NewStore adapter → GiveX) as a SCAPI payment instrument, not through the PWA directly. **Gift card purchase** is a PWA-rendered surface: physical and digital products (separate product IDs), fixed denominations ($100/$200/$250/$300/$500), and a sender / recipient / recipient-email / delivery-date / optional-message form; the PWA persists these as basket line-item attributes, and issuance (E-Cert Order for digital, Activate for physical) is server-side via SCAPI/SFCC → MuleSoft → NewStore → GiveX. Separate from AP21 Retail Rewards — both can be used in a single checkout |
218	| **Transperfect** | Translation pipeline (for Contentful content) | Out-of-band | Translated copy lands in Contentful via vendor workflow. Translation workflow trigger TBD |
219	| **Inside Chat** | Customer support chat widget | Loaded by GTM / Addingwell (post-consent) | **Loaded via GTM script injection through the Addingwell container, not a direct PWA include** (HPC-039/040). Initialised only after Didomi consent; shown on relevant pages per Inside Chat rules |
220	| **Zendesk** | Customer service ticketing — hosts the public "Contact Us" form | Out-of-band (external link) | **Not an embedded integration.** The PWA's "Contact Us" CTA links out to the Zendesk-hosted form on a Zendesk domain — no iframe, no SDK, no API call from the PWA. Confirmed 2026-06-01. No Didomi gate needed (no third-party script loads in the storefront). |
221	| **Google reCAPTCHA** | Bot protection on registration/login | Browser-direct (site key) + MRT-mediated (token verification) | Site key public in bundle (`RECAPTCHA_SITE_KEY`); secret key held as `RECAPTCHA_SECRET_KEY` MRT environment variable — MRT verifies the token via Google's `siteverify` endpoint before forwarding to SCAPI; the secret key never reaches the browser. Loads on register/login **form interaction**. **Consent-gated in EU & UK only** (loads only post-Didomi-consent, so a visitor who declines is not challenged and there's no bot protection there); elsewhere it loads regardless of consent. |
222	| **GDPR cartridge** | DSAR export, right-to-erasure, configurable retention | SFCC (cartridge) | Replaces manual legal/IT ticketing. PWA-side touchpoints: localised privacy policy pages (from Contentful), the consent UI itself (Didomi), and surfacing the customer-initiated erasure / export trigger in My Account where exposed by SFCC. Full requirements: REG-060–067. |
223	| **Shippit / Ordoro** | Carrier label automation | OMS-level only | SFCC passes address to MuleSoft, not directly to these |
224	| **Google Business API** | Store hours feed (boutique opening hours) | Out-of-band (daily feed into SFCC) | Consumed by Find in Boutique / store-locator UI — PWA renders, does not call Google directly |
225	| **Feedonomics** | Product feed for downstream marketing channels (PRD-071) | Out-of-band | No PWA runtime touchpoint; flagged for SEO/marketing dependency awareness only |
226	| **Measmerize** | Find My Size widget + size guide overlay on PDP (PRD-050–053) | PWA-direct (script injection on PDP only) | Browser-direct; no MRT proxy. Script injected once on PDP mount; widget self-determines product availability and signals the PWA via events. Falls back to the Contentful size guide when Measmerize has no data for the product. **Consent approach unconfirmed — open item.** Implementation detail: [.docs/temp/integration/17-measmerize.md](.docs/temp/integration/17-measmerize.md). Vendor SDK reference: [.docs/vendor/measmerize.md](.docs/vendor/measmerize.md). |
227	
228	## Cross-Storefront Session & Basket Scope
229	All seven storefronts are path-prefixed on a single first-party domain and share one SFCC realm with shared customer data. The `httpOnly` SLAS refresh-token cookie set by the SSR layer is therefore presented on every storefront prefix — no cross-domain SSO bridge is needed. SLAS tokens are channel-scoped, so the SSR layer re-initialises the SLAS context per storefront; a registered shopper is silently re-recognised across a storefront switch (shared customer record), while a guest session is site-scoped and does not carry over. **The basket deliberately does not transfer across storefronts** — baskets are site-scoped and priced in the storefront's own currency/pricebook, so a shopper switching storefront starts a fresh basket. Carrying a basket across a currency boundary would produce incorrect pricing. The Global-e checkout handoff is a separate session boundary (Global-e owns its hosted checkout in full). The exact SLAS re-authorisation mechanism and the stay-signed-in UX are open items with the Salesforce integration team.
230	
231	## Customer Data Migration (DMU-004, updated 2026-05-29)
232	Only **email + Omneo customer ID** are migrated into SFCC at go-live. All other customer profile data — name, phone, addresses, communication preferences — is sourced **live from Omneo at login** via MuleSoft. Implication: My Account profile pages cannot rely on SFCC for the full customer record; an Omneo round-trip is required post-authentication. Graceful degradation for Omneo outages becomes load-bearing on account screens. Asset/CDN migration (DMU-010) is **de-scoped** — images stay in Contentful, no asset 301s.
233	
234	## Blast-Radius Mitigation
235	
236	Multiple upstream integrations (SFCC, MuleSoft/Omneo, Global-e, Narvar, Contentful, Didomi, Inside Chat) mean a failure or attack targeting one service must not cascade. A PWA-relevant mitigation can be done in the SSR layer.
237	
238	The SSR layer in `overrides/app/ssr.js` uses **Node's native `fetch`**, which is backed by `undici`. Undici's `dispatcher` option (the per-call `dispatcher` option on individual `fetch()` invocations) allows each upstream origin to be given its own connection pool with an independent cap. This prevents a slow or flooded integration (e.g. checkout APIs) from exhausting connections for unrelated origins (e.g. Contentful, JWKS).
239	
240	```ts
241	import { Pool } from 'undici'
242	
243	// 1. Create isolated pools for specific origins
244	const checkoutPool = new Pool('https://api.checkout-service.com', {
245	  connections: 10, // Hard limit of 10 concurrent connections to this origin
246	  timeout: 8000
247	})
248	
249	// 2. Use them explicitly in your fetch calls inside ssr.js
250	async function getCheckoutMetadata() {
251	  return await fetch('https://api.checkout-service.com/v1/metadata', {
252	    dispatcher: checkoutPool // Safely isolated!
253	  })
254	}
255	```
256	
257	The connection pool split is an engineering decision — the right pool boundaries and sizes depend on observed traffic patterns and the integration map in §7. Planned pools (connection caps should be validated later — see §9.3):
258	
259	| Pool | Origin | Calls | Cap | `connectTimeout` | `bodyTimeout` | Reasoning |
260	|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
261	| `sfcc-scapi` | `https://{shortCode}.api.commercecloud.salesforce.com` | SLAS JWKS (token validation for passwordless login, reset password) | 5 | 5 s | 8 s | `jose` caches the JWK set for its rotation period; actual network calls are rare. Isolated so a JWKS fetch is never starved by higher-volume pools. |
262	| `sfcc-payments` | `config.app.sfPayments.metadataUrl` host (a `*.demandware.net` or SCAPI hostname — confirm with Integration team) | Payment method metadata on every checkout page SSR | 10 | 5 s | 8 s | Called on every checkout page load; moderate frequency. Separate from `sfcc-scapi` because a checkout traffic spike must not consume SLAS connections. |
263	| `mulesoft` | `MULESOFT_BASE_URL` | Order history, order details, boutique / BOPIS stock check, GiveX balance check | 20 | 5 s | 10 s | Highest user-facing concurrency (My Account + PDP). GiveX balance calls carry payment credentials in the POST body — a slow MuleSoft response must not hold connections open and starve other pools. Highest cap reflects the broadest call surface. |
264	| `marketing-cloud-auth` | `https://{subdomain}.auth.marketingcloudapis.com` | Marketing Cloud client-credentials token exchange | 5 | 5 s | 15 s | User-triggered, infrequent; token cached at module scope for 15 min. Isolated so an MC outage cannot consume SFCC or MuleSoft connections. |
265	| `marketing-cloud-rest` | `https://{subdomain}.rest.marketingcloudapis.com` | Magic-link email send (passwordless login, reset password) | 5 | 5 s | 15 s | Same trigger as above; higher body timeout because email delivery APIs can respond slowly under load. |
266	| `google-places` | `https://places.googleapis.com` (Places API — New) | Address autocomplete at checkout (CFD-023, CFD-030, CFD-059) | 5 | 3 s | 5 s | Non-critical-path; graceful fallback to manual entry. Short timeouts ensure a Places API slowdown releases connections quickly. |
267	| `booxi` | Booxi base URL (TBD — confirm with Integration team) | Boutique appointment read in My Account (CRM-165–167) | 5 | 3 s | 5 s | My Account only; non-critical-path within that page. |

# Architecture

*Key technical decisions, stack overview, overrides pattern, component organisation, and key paths. Update this file when the stack changes, a new integration is added, or a structural decision is made.*

Production storefront for www.zimmermann.com — multi-locale, multi-currency, seven storefronts across six regions (AU, US, UK, EU, HK, ME), with the EU as two storefronts (domestic + international).

## Pre-Build Decisions

These decisions affect tooling, CI, and code shape that's hard to retrofit later. Status as of 2026-05-29.

| # | Decision | Status |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Browser & device matrix | ✅ Confirmed (informal) |
| 2 | Accessibility manual testing | 🟡 Partial — vendor info pending |
| 3 | Performance budgets | ✅ Confirmed (informal) |
| 4 | Client-side error reporting | ⚪ Accepted risk — no tool |
| 5 | Feature-flag tool | ⚪ Accepted risk — Optimizely Web only |
| 6 | Translation fallback chain | 🟡 Partial — Brand/Legal pending |

### #1 — Browser & device matrix ✅
**Mobile perf-test floor:** current OS version −2 on iPhone and Android (iOS 17+, Android 14+), verified via BrowserStack Automate. `package.json` browserslist aligned to match.
**Desktop matrix** ([.browserstack.yml](../../.browserstack.yml)): Chrome + Safari (macOS Sonoma), Firefox + Edge (Windows 11) — all latest.

### #2 — Accessibility 🟡
**Target:** WCAG 2.2 AA, at least 2.1 AA. **Automated:** axe-core in Vitest + Playwright; Storybook a11y addon; Lighthouse CI a11y ≥0.90 ([lighthouserc.js](../../lighthouserc.js)). **Manual:** client's existing a11y vendor.
**Pending:** vendor name, screen-reader/browser matrix, audit cadence, remediation owner.

### #3 — Performance budgets ✅
**Client-mandated:** **LCP ≤ 2s** at p75 mobile, plus Lighthouse Performance ≥ 0.80, Accessibility ≥ 0.90, Best Practices ≥ 0.90. These are the only performance numbers in the signed TSD (§9).
**Other CWV (internal working defaults, not client-mandated):** INP ≤ 200ms · CLS ≤ 0.1. Lighthouse mobile defaults at p75.
**CI gate (SIT gate):** Lighthouse CI (`@lhci/cli`) asserts the Lighthouse score floors above, plus a >5pt trend-drop gate (LHCI server required). SEO intentionally not asserted. Runs on every PR to `develop` ([`digital-sit.yml`](../../.github/workflows/digital-sit.yml)), deploys to the **Dev** tier on merge — treat its numbers as a **regression indicator**, not the contractual measurement.
**Contractual measurement:** Client-mandated LCP and Lighthouse numbers are validated on **Stage** — the prod-mimicking tier (same MRT bundle size class, same CDN/edge configuration, same SFCC realm tier as production). The Dev tier is slower and further from the edge, so its absolute numbers will be worse — that is expected and not a sign-off concern. Full environment topology in [tsd-architecture.md §14.1](./temp/tsd-architecture.md).
**Bundle ceilings — internal CI policy, NOT client requirements:** `main.js` 180 kB · `vendor.js` 250 kB · `main.css` 50 kB (`bundlesize` in `package.json`). (These were set as aspirational targets early in the project. ## SSR Requirement (DMU-030)
Server-side rendering is **mandatory** for product, category, and content pages (DMU-030, signed off). PWA Kit's SSR pipeline must be preserved — do not introduce client-only patterns (e.g. `typeof window !== 'undefined'` short-circuits, client-only data fetching on first paint, or `next/dynamic`-style `{ ssr: false }`) on these page types. Any componentry that cannot render on the server must be gated behind a hydration-safe boundary that still emits SEO-relevant markup on the server.

## Overrides Pattern
All customizations live in `overrides/` mirroring the structure of `node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/`. Never edit `node_modules/`.

**Minimise custom code.** When implementing Zimmermann's design and layout, stay as close to the base PWA Kit implementation as possible. Style changes (CSS, Chakra props, theme tokens) are always expected and need no confirmation. Structural changes — restructuring components, altering data flow, or significantly deviating from base template behaviour — must be confirmed with the user before proceeding.

**Before any change:** check whether the file exists in `overrides/`. If not, create the override:
1. Copy from `node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/` to the mirrored path in `overrides/`.
2. Rename `.js`/`.jsx` → `.ts`/`.tsx`. Replace `PropTypes` with TypeScript `type` definitions. Add explicit types to all parameters, return values, and props. Use Commerce SDK types (`commerce-sdk-isomorphic`, `@salesforce/commerce-sdk-react`) where available. No `as any` or `// @ts-ignore`.
3. Verify `npx tsc --noEmit` passes with zero errors.
4. **Stop. Present the converted file to the user and wait for approval before making any functional changes.**

## Contentful Content Type Management

Content types (schema) are never created manually in the Contentful web app. They are defined in code and synced via a script. This makes schema changes reviewable, repeatable, and team-safe.

**Key paths:**
- `scripts/contentful/sync.js` — runner: upserts (creates or updates) and publishes every content type in the definitions directory
- `scripts/contentful/content-types/` — one `.js` file per content type (e.g. `shoppableImage.js`)

**To register a new content type:**
1. Add a definition file to `scripts/contentful/content-types/<contentTypeId>.js` (see existing files for shape)
2. Run `npm run sync:contentful`

**To run the sync:**
```
npm run sync:contentful
```
Requires `CONTENTFUL_MANAGEMENT_TOKEN` in `.env` at the repo root (never commit). Get it from `app.contentful.com/account/profile/cma_tokens`. `CONTENTFUL_SPACE_ID` and `CONTENTFUL_ENVIRONMENT_ID` are already in `.env`.

The script is idempotent — safe to re-run. It preserves any existing fields not in the definition file (it will not delete fields from a live content type).

**Relationship to the React component:**
Each content type definition in `scripts/contentful/content-types/` corresponds to a React component in `overrides/app/components/contentful/`. The content type's field IDs must match the TypeScript type in `overrides/app/types/contentful.ts`.

**Experience Builder components** (drag-and-drop in Contentful Studio) are a separate concern — they are registered in `overrides/app/components/contentful/experiences/definitions.ts` and do not need a corresponding `sync:contentful` entry unless they also have a standard content type for use outside Studio.

## Integration Map

All order-creation, fulfilment write, and CRM sync traffic from SFCC routes through MuleSoft as the middleware layer — SFCC does not call NewStore, AP21, Omneo, or Narvar directly. In addition, the PWA's MRT Node layer calls MuleSoft directly for read operations (order history, order details, boutique / BOPIS stock check, real-time stock availability, GiveX balance check) — SFCC is not in those read paths. A handful of services are also called **browser-direct from the PWA** and another set are **SFCC cartridge integrations** invoked server-side. The `Boundary` column makes this explicit so you know where to look when an integration breaks.

**Boundary key:**
- **PWA-direct** — called from the browser directly. Vendor key (if any) is publishable/public and safe in the bundle.
- **MRT-mediated** — called from the PWA's Node layer via `/mobify/proxy/` or a server-only endpoint. API credentials held as MRT environment variables; never reach the browser bundle. Includes direct PWA → MuleSoft calls via MRT proxy.
- **SFCC (OOTB)** — Salesforce-bundled integration; no custom cartridge.
- **SFCC (cartridge)** — vendor-supplied or custom server-side cartridge running inside SFCC.
- **SFCC → MuleSoft** — SFCC calls MuleSoft, which fans out to the downstream system.
- **Browser handoff** — PWA hands the user off to a third party's hosted experience.
- **Out-of-band** — no runtime call from PWA or SFCC; the integration delivers data via a separate channel.

## Cross-Storefront Session & Basket Scope
All seven storefronts are path-prefixed on a single first-party domain and share one SFCC realm with shared customer data. The `httpOnly` SLAS refresh-token cookie set by the SSR layer is therefore presented on every storefront prefix — no cross-domain SSO bridge is needed. SLAS tokens are channel-scoped, so the SSR layer re-initialises the SLAS context per storefront; a registered shopper is silently re-recognised across a storefront switch (shared customer record), while a guest session is site-scoped and does not carry over. **The basket deliberately does not transfer across storefronts** — baskets are site-scoped and priced in the storefront's own currency/pricebook, so a shopper switching storefront starts a fresh basket. Carrying a basket across a currency boundary would produce incorrect pricing. The Global-e checkout handoff is a separate session boundary (Global-e owns its hosted checkout in full). The exact SLAS re-authorisation mechanism and the stay-signed-in UX are open items with the Salesforce integration team.

## Customer Data Migration (DMU-004, updated 2026-05-29)
Only **email + Omneo customer ID** are migrated into SFCC at go-live. All other customer profile data — name, phone, addresses, communication preferences — is sourced **live from Omneo at login** via MuleSoft. Implication: My Account profile pages cannot rely on SFCC for the full customer record; an Omneo round-trip is required post-authentication. Graceful degradation for Omneo outages becomes load-bearing on account screens. Asset/CDN migration (DMU-010) is **de-scoped** — images stay in Contentful, no asset 301s.

## Blast-Radius Mitigation

Multiple upstream integrations (SFCC, MuleSoft/Omneo, Global-e, Narvar, Contentful, Didomi, Inside Chat) mean a failure or attack targeting one service must not cascade. A PWA-relevant mitigation can be done in the SSR layer.

The SSR layer in `overrides/app/ssr.js` uses **Node's native `fetch`**, which is backed by `undici`. Undici's `dispatcher` option (the per-call `dispatcher` option on individual `fetch()` invocations) allows each upstream origin to be given its own connection pool with an independent cap. This prevents a slow or flooded integration (e.g. checkout APIs) from exhausting connections for unrelated origins (e.g. Contentful, JWKS).

```ts
import { Pool } from 'undici'

// 1. Create isolated pools for specific origins
const checkoutPool = new Pool('https://api.checkout-service.com', {
  connections: 10, // Hard limit of 10 concurrent connections to this origin
  timeout: 8000
})

// 2. Use them explicitly in your fetch calls inside ssr.js
async function getCheckoutMetadata() {
  return await fetch('https://api.checkout-service.com/v1/metadata', {
    dispatcher: checkoutPool // Safely isolated!
  })
}
```

The connection pool split is an engineering decision — the right pool boundaries and sizes depend on observed traffic patterns and the integration map in §7. Planned pools (connection caps should be validated later — see §9.3):

| Pool | Origin | Calls | Cap | `connectTimeout` | `bodyTimeout` | Reasoning |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `sfcc-scapi` | `https://{shortCode}.api.commercecloud.salesforce.com` | SLAS JWKS (token validation for passwordless login, reset password) | 5 | 5 s | 8 s | `jose` caches the JWK set for its rotation period; actual network calls are rare. Isolated so a JWKS fetch is never starved by higher-volume pools. |
| `sfcc-payments` | `config.app.sfPayments.metadataUrl` host (a `*.demandware.net` or SCAPI hostname — confirm with Integration team) | Payment method metadata on every checkout page SSR | 10 | 5 s | 8 s | Called on every checkout page load; moderate frequency. Separate from `sfcc-scapi` because a checkout traffic spike must not consume SLAS connections. |
| `mulesoft` | `MULESOFT_BASE_URL` | Order history, order details, boutique / BOPIS stock check, GiveX balance check | 20 | 5 s | 10 s | Highest user-facing concurrency (My Account + PDP). GiveX balance calls carry payment credentials in the POST body — a slow MuleSoft response must not hold connections open and starve other pools. Highest cap reflects the broadest call surface. |
| `marketing-cloud-auth` | `https://{subdomain}.auth.marketingcloudapis.com` | Marketing Cloud client-credentials token exchange | 5 | 5 s | 15 s | User-triggered, infrequent; token cached at module scope for 15 min. Isolated so an MC outage cannot consume SFCC or MuleSoft connections. |
| `marketing-cloud-rest` | `https://{subdomain}.rest.marketingcloudapis.com` | Magic-link email send (passwordless login, reset password) | 5 | 5 s | 15 s | Same trigger as above; higher body timeout because email delivery APIs can respond slowly under load. |
| `google-places` | `https://places.googleapis.com` (Places API — New) | Address autocomplete at checkout (CFD-023, CFD-030, CFD-059) | 5 | 3 s | 5 s | Non-critical-path; graceful fallback to manual entry. Short timeouts ensure a Places API slowdown releases connections quickly. |
| `booxi` | Booxi base URL (TBD — confirm with Integration team) | Boutique appointment read in My Account (CRM-165–167) | 5 | 3 s | 5 s | My Account only; non-critical-path within that page. |

## Back-merge rules (GitFlow)

To prevent `develop` drifting from production:
- When a `release/*` branch is merged to `main` at go-live, it must also be merged back to `develop`.
- When a `hotfix/*` is merged to `main`, it must also be merged back to `develop`.
- When a `fix/release-*` is merged into its `release/*` parent and the release later ships, the forward-merge to `develop` happens as part of the release back-merge above — no separate action.

## Release Branch Behaviour

When on a `release/*` branch, the following rules apply in addition to all Hard Rules.

**Before writing any code, always:**
1. State a plan — which files will change, what will change in each, and why.
2. Assess blast radius — how many components, hooks, or pages consume each file being changed? Flag explicitly if any file has more than 3 consumers or is Tier 2 or above.
3. Wait for explicit developer confirmation before making any edit, including trivial ones.

**Allowed on release branches:**
- Read-only skills: `/generate-changelog`, `/pr-checklist`, `/code-quality`
- Trivial non-code changes (copy corrections, version bumps, feature flag toggles) — plan + confirm required
- Code logic fixes — only on a `fix/release-{version}_{description}` sub-branch, never directly on the release branch

**Not allowed on release branches:**
- New features or scope additions not in the release
- Refactoring
- Dependency changes
- Tier 1 or Tier 2 file changes without the same owner approval required on feature branches

**How to make a code fix on a release branch:**

The fix PR targets the release branch. Once the release ships, the fix flows into `develop` via the release back-merge — do not open a separate PR from `fix/release-*` to `develop`.

```bash
# Branch from the release branch — not from develop
git checkout release/v0.1.0
git checkout -b fix/release-v0.1.0-payment-error-description

# Make the fix, open a PR targeting the release branch
gh pr create --base release/v0.1.0 --title "fix(checkout): SFCC-999 payment error on release"
```

# Upstream update policy

How we handle new releases of `@salesforce/retail-react-app` (and the surrounding PWA Kit SDKs).

## Principle

**Bump opportunistically — not on a schedule.** Stay on the current version unless a release contains something we actually care about.

Reasons to bump:
- **Security** — CVE fix, dependency patch with a known vulnerability, advisory we are exposed to.
- **SDK** — a change in `pwa-kit-runtime`, `pwa-kit-react-sdk`, `commerce-sdk-react`, or `pwa-kit-dev` that affects code we depend on (SSR, routing, hooks we use, build pipeline).
- **Bug fix or feature we have been waiting for** — a fix to behaviour we currently work around, or a feature that lets us delete custom code, or will help us on implementing a planned feature.

Reasons **not** to bump:
- A release with only template/UI changes that we have already overridden.
- A release whose changelog touches packages or paths we do not use.
- "It's been a while."

## Discipline

When the upstream-release-watch workflow opens a tracking issue (see [.github/workflows/upstream-release-watch.yml](../.github/workflows/upstream-release-watch.yml)):

1. Open the linked release notes.
2. Skim for the three categories above.
3. If nothing relevant, close the issue with a one-line reason and update `Reviewed up to` in [.docs/memory/upstreamBaseline.md](memory/upstreamBaseline.md). **Do not bump.**
4. If something relevant, bump — then update `Current` and `Reviewed up to` together.

## What we do not do

- **No drift detection script.** We do not diff our `overrides/` against the upstream template on a schedule. Drift is the *point* of the overrides pattern.
- **No two-track review.** There is no separate "SDK package review" vs "template code skim." If we bump, we bump; the changelog tells us what to test.
- **No bump because it's been N weeks.** Time alone is not a reason.

## Related

- Current baseline: [.docs/memory/upstreamBaseline.md](memory/upstreamBaseline.md)
- Watch workflow: [.github/workflows/upstream-release-watch.yml](../.github/workflows/upstream-release-watch.yml)
- CI security gate (once CI lands): `npm audit --audit-level=high` — fail on new highs only.
