1	---
2	name: code-quality
3	description: Audit recently changed or specified files for code quality issues — naming, circular imports, TypeScript coverage, test/story existence, and structural debt. Read-only. Use after implementing a feature or before opening a PR.
4	---
5	
6	Audit code quality for the specified scope. Do not modify any files — this is a read-only
7	diagnostic. Produce a prioritised report with actionable fixes.
8	
9	---
10	
11	## Input
12	
13	The user will provide one of:
14	- A file path or directory to audit
15	- No argument — default to files changed on the current branch: `git diff --name-only main`
16	
17	If no argument is given, run: `git diff --name-only main` and audit those files.
18	Exclude test files (`*.test.ts`, `*.spec.ts`), stories (`*.stories.tsx`), and any registry files.
19	
20	---
21	
22	## Parallel execution
23	
24	For audits covering more than 5 files, split into four independent checks and run them
25	as parallel agents simultaneously. Each agent receives only its own checklist — do not
26	bundle all checks into one agent.
27	
28	- **Agent A — Naming & structure**
29	- **Agent B — Import analysis**
30	- **Agent C — TypeScript coverage**
31	- **Agent D — Test & story coverage**
32	
33	For 5 files or fewer, run all checks sequentially in a single pass.
34	
35	---
36	
37	## Agent A — Naming & structure
38	
39	Rules are defined once in [.claude/rules/conventions.md](../../rules/conventions.md) —
40	read it first, then apply each rule to the files in scope. Do not re-list the rules here;
41	that's how the two files drift apart.
42	
43	Walk the file list and audit each file against the relevant section of conventions.md:
44	
45	- Every file → **General** section.
46	- `.tsx` under `overrides/app/components/` or `overrides/app/pages/` → **Components** + **File naming and folder structure**.
47	- `.ts` under `overrides/app/hooks/` → **Hooks**.
48	- `.ts` under `overrides/app/utils/` → **Utilities**.
49	
50	For each violation, record `file:line` and which conventions.md bullet failed — the
51	section anchor is enough (e.g. "Components → Props type placement").
52	
53	---
54	
55	## Agent B — Import analysis
56	
57	For each file, read the import statements and check:
58	
59	- No circular imports: if File A imports from File B, File B must not import from File A
60	  (check by reading the imported file's imports in turn — one level deep is sufficient).
61	- No imports from a higher tier without justification:
62	  - A component must not import directly from internal `commerce-sdk-react` source paths.
63	  - A page must not bypass its own hooks to call raw API functions.
64	- No imports from a later-sprint feature (reference `.docs/memory/sprintScope.md` when present).
65	- No `../../../..` chains longer than 3 levels — flag for path alias review.
66	
67	---
68	
69	## Agent C — TypeScript coverage
70	
71	Check each file against the relevant section of [conventions.md](../../rules/conventions.md):
72	
73	- Components → **Components** (props type name, placement, optional `?`, callback naming, JSDoc).
74	- Hooks → **Hooks** (typed params, explicit return type, JSDoc with `@returns`).
75	- Every `.ts`/`.tsx` → **General** (no `any` without justification).
76	
77	Then run `npx tsc --noEmit` **once** for the whole branch (not per file) and report any
78	errors. Cross-reference any new errors against the files in scope.
79	
80	---
81	
82	## Agent D — Test & story coverage
83	
84	For each component file under `overrides/app/components/` or `overrides/app/pages/`:
85	- A paired `*.stories.tsx` exists in the same directory (required by [AGENTS.md](../../../AGENTS.md) > Testing).
86	- For logic-heavy components or hooks: a `*.test.ts` exists OR a `play` function exists in the story.
87	- If a test file exists, verify:
88	  - At least one test covers the primary render case.
89	  - At least one test covers a user interaction (click, input) if the component has interactive elements.
90	  - No tests use `toBeTruthy()` as the sole assertion — check for meaningful assertions.
91	- If a paired `.stories.tsx` is missing, flag as MISSING STORY (mandatory).
92	- If a logic-heavy file has neither a `.test.ts` nor a `play` function, flag as MISSING TEST.
93	
94	For each utility file under `overrides/app/utils/`:
95	- **`.test.ts` required** when the utility has ≥1 conditional branch or performs ≥1
96	  transformation (currency, locale, mapping, parsing, etc.). Trivial re-exports and
97	  one-liners are exempt.
98	- If a test file exists, verify it covers both the happy path and at least one edge case
99	  (empty input, null, locale variation — whichever applies).
100	
101	---
102	
103	## Output format
104	
105	Combine all agent results into a single prioritised report:
106	
107	```
108	## Code Quality Report
109	**Scope:** [files audited]
110	**Branch:** [current branch]
111	**Date:** [today]
112	
113	### 🔴 Must fix before PR merge
114	[Issues that would fail review or cause runtime errors — one line per issue with file:line]
115	
116	### 🟡 Should fix in this PR
117	[Issues that affect maintainability or violate conventions — one line per issue with file:line]
118	
119	### 🔵 Backlog (log, don't block)
120	[Minor style issues, missing test cases for edge cases — one line per issue]
121	
122	### ✅ No issues found
123	[List checks that passed cleanly]
124	
125	### Summary
126	X must-fix · Y should-fix · Z backlog items
127	```
128	
129	Do not suggest refactors beyond the scope of the changed files.
130	Do not modify any files — report only.
131

  - No tests use `toBeTruthy()` as the sole assertion — check for meaningful assertions.
- If a paired `.stories.tsx` is missing, flag as MISSING STORY (mandatory).

For each utility file under `overrides/app/utils/`:
- **`.test.ts` required** when the utility has ≥1 conditional branch or performs ≥1
  transformation (currency, locale, mapping, parsing, etc.). Trivial re-exports and
  one-liners are exempt.
- If a test file exists, verify it covers both the happy path and at least one edge case
  (empty input, null, locale variation — whichever applies).

---

Combine all agent results into a single prioritised report:

```
## Code Quality Report
**Scope:** [files audited]
**Branch:** [current branch]
**Date:** [today]

### 🔴 Must fix before PR merge
[Issues that would fail review or cause runtime errors — one line per issue with file:line]

### 🟡 Should fix in this PR
[Issues that affect maintainability or violate conventions — one line per issue with file:line]

### 🔵 Backlog (log, don't block)
[Minor style issues, missing test cases for edge cases — one line per issue]

### ✅ No issues found
[List checks that passed cleanly]

### Summary
X must-fix · Y should-fix · Z backlog items
```

Do not suggest refactors beyond the scope of the changed files.
Do not modify any files — report only.

---
name: contentful-drift-check
description: Check for drift between React component props and their Contentful Studio component definitions. Use when a developer wants to verify definitions are still in sync after props have changed, or to audit all registered components at once.
allowed-tools: Read, Bash, Glob, Grep
---

# Contentful Drift Check

## Purpose
Compare React component props against their paired `*ContentfulDefinition.ts` files
and report any drift: added props, removed props, or type mismatches.

## Input
`$ARGUMENTS` may be:
- A specific component file path (e.g. `overrides/app/components/hero/hero.tsx`) — check that one component
- A directory path — check all components with definitions in that directory
- Empty — scan the entire `overrides/app/components/` (and any `overrides/app/ui/` directory if it exists)

## Steps

### 1. Find the component/definition pairs to check

If `$ARGUMENTS` is a specific file:
- Use that file as the single target
- Derive the definition path: same directory, `[ComponentName]ContentfulDefinition.ts`

If `$ARGUMENTS` is a directory or empty:
- Run: `find overrides/app/components overrides/app/ui -name "*ContentfulDefinition.ts" 2>/dev/null`
- For each definition file found, derive the component path by stripping `ContentfulDefinition.ts` and adding `.tsx`
- Skip any definition whose paired component file does not exist

### 2. For each pair, read both files

Use the Read tool to read:
1. The component file (`.tsx`)
2. The definition file (`*ContentfulDefinition.ts`)

### 3. Extract props from the component

From the component file, identify:
- The Props `type` or `interface` (e.g. `type HeroProps = { ... }`)
- Each prop name, its TypeScript type, and whether it is optional (`?`) or required
- Ignore event handler props (names starting with `on`) — these are never Contentful variables

### 4. Extract variables from the definition

From the definition file, identify:
- Each key in the `variables: { }` object
- Its declared `type` value
- Whether `required: true` or `required: false`

### 5. Compare and report drift

For each component/definition pair output a section:

**Component**: `[file path]`
**Definition**: `[definition file path]`

Then one of:
- ✅ **In sync** — all props are represented correctly
- ⚠️ **Drift detected** — with a table:

| Prop | Status | Detail |
|------|--------|--------|
| propName | Missing from definition | Add as type X |
| oldProp | In definition but not in component | Remove or check if renamed |
| variantProp | Type mismatch | Component: `'sm' \| 'lg'`, Definition: `Text/shortText` (should be `Text/select`) |

### 6. Summary

At the end, output:
- Total pairs checked
- Number in sync
- Number with drift
- If any drift was found: "Run /contentful-register-component to regenerate a definition, or edit the definition file manually."

## Important
- Do not modify any files — this skill is read-only
- If a component has no paired definition file, skip it silently (it is not registered with Contentful)
- If a definition file exists but its paired component cannot be found, flag it as a stale definition

4	allowed-tools: Read, Write, Edit, Bash, Glob, Grep
5	---
6	
7	# Contentful Component Registration Skill
8	
9	## Purpose
10	Register an existing Zimmermann React component (under `overrides/app/`) with
11	Contentful Studio Experiences by reading its TypeScript props, generating a
12	component definition, and wiring it into the `defineComponents` registry.
13	
14	## Steps
15	
16	### 1. Read the target component
17	- Ask the developer for the component file path if not provided (`overrides/app/components/<name>/<name>.tsx`).
18	- Read the component file using the Read tool.
19	- Extract all TypeScript prop types and their types (string, boolean, number,
20	  union types, optional vs required).
21	- Identify any nested object types that need to be flattened for Contentful.
22	
23	### 2. Map React props to Contentful variable types
24	Use this mapping table strictly:
25	
26	| TypeScript type       | Contentful variable type | Control type       |
27	|-----------------------|--------------------------|--------------------|
28	| string                | Text                     | shortText          |
29	| string (long/rich)    | Text                     | longText           |
30	| string union (enum)   | Text                     | select             |
31	| boolean               | Boolean                  | toggle             |
32	| number                | Number                   | number             |
33	| React.ReactNode       | — (use children: true)   | —                  |
34	| image/media object    | Media                    | — (media field)    |
35	| href / url string     | Text                     | shortText          |
36	| array of strings      | Text                     | shortText (repeat) |
37	
38	Rules:
39	- Optional props (`prop?: type`) should have `required: false` in the definition.
40	- Required props should have `required: true`.
41	- Props named `children` or that accept `ReactNode` must use `children: true` on
42	  the component registration, NOT a variable.
43	- Do not expose internal/handler props (`onClick`, `onChange`, `onX`) as variables —
44	  these are not content fields. Flag them to the developer.
45	- Union string types (e.g. `'primary' | 'secondary'`) must produce a `select`
46	  control with options matching each union member.
47	
48	### 3. Generate the component definition file
49	Create a new file alongside the component named
50	`[componentName]ContentfulDefinition.ts` with this structure:
51	
52	```ts
53	import { ComponentDefinition } from '@contentful/experiences-sdk-react';
54	
55	export const [componentName]Definition: ComponentDefinition = {
56	  id: '[component-name-kebab-case]',
57	  name: '[Human Readable Component Name]',
58	  category: 'Zimmermann Components',
59	  thumbnailUrl: '',
60	  variables: {
61	    // One entry per mapped prop
62	    [propName]: {
63	      displayName: '[Prop Name in Title Case]',
64	      type: '[Contentful type from mapping table]',
65	      defaultValue: [appropriate default],
66	      required: [true|false],
67	      // Add for select controls:
68	      // validations: { in: [{ value: 'option1' }, { value: 'option2' }] }
69	    },
70	  },
71	};
72	```
73	
74	### 4. Update the defineComponents registry
75	- Locate the file that calls `defineComponents` (ask the developer if unsure —
76	  typically under `overrides/app/` somewhere like `registeredComponents.ts`).
77	- Read the current file contents.
78	- Add the import for the new component and its definition.
79	- Add the registration entry to the `defineComponents` array.
80	- Write the updated file.
81	
82	### 5. Output a summary to the developer
83	Print a clear summary including:
84	- Which props were mapped and how.
85	- Which props were SKIPPED and why (e.g. event handlers, children).
86	- Any props that could not be automatically mapped and need manual review.
87	- The files created or modified.
88	- A reminder that the component definition `thumbnailUrl` is empty and should
89	  be updated with a preview image path.
90	
91	## Important constraints
92	- Never modify the original React component file.
93	- Never add Contentful imports into the component itself — keep the definition
94	  separate.
95	- If a prop type cannot be determined (e.g. complex object, external type
96	  import), flag it clearly and skip it rather than guess.
97	- The registry file must be TypeScript (`.ts`) per the TypeScript-only rule for
98	  `overrides/`.
99	- Always verify the `defineComponents` file exists before trying to update it;
100	  if it does not exist, create it and note this in the summary.
101

description: Register a Zimmermann React component with Contentful Studio Experiences. Use when a developer asks to register, add, or expose a React component to Contentful, or when they need to create a Contentful component definition for an existing component.
allowed-tools: Read, Write, Edit, Bash, Glob, Grep
---

# Contentful Component Registration Skill

## Purpose
Register an existing Zimmermann React component (under `overrides/app/`) with
Contentful Studio Experiences by reading its TypeScript props, generating a
component definition, and wiring it into the `defineComponents` registry.

## Steps

### 1. Read the target component
- Ask the developer for the component file path if not provided (`overrides/app/components/<name>/<name>.tsx`).
- Read the component file using the Read tool.
- Extract all TypeScript prop types and their types (string, boolean, number,
  union types, optional vs required).
- Identify any nested object types that need to be flattened for Contentful.

### 2. Map React props to Contentful variable types
Use this mapping table strictly:

| TypeScript type       | Contentful variable type | Control type       |
|-----------------------|--------------------------|--------------------|
| string                | Text                     | shortText          |
| string (long/rich)    | Text                     | longText           |
| string union (enum)   | Text                     | select             |
| boolean               | Boolean                  | toggle             |
| number                | Number                   | number             |
| React.ReactNode       | — (use children: true)   | —                  |
| image/media object    | Media                    | — (media field)    |
| href / url string     | Text                     | shortText          |
| array of strings      | Text                     | shortText (repeat) |

Rules:
- Optional props (`prop?: type`) should have `required: false` in the definition.
- Required props should have `required: true`.
- Props named `children` or that accept `ReactNode` must use `children: true` on
  the component registration, NOT a variable.
- Do not expose internal/handler props (`onClick`, `onChange`, `onX`) as variables —
  these are not content fields. Flag them to the developer.
- Union string types (e.g. `'primary' | 'secondary'`) must produce a `select`
  control with options matching each union member.

### 3. Generate the component definition file
Create a new file alongside the component named
`[componentName]ContentfulDefinition.ts` with this structure:

```ts
import { ComponentDefinition } from '@contentful/experiences-sdk-react';

export const [componentName]Definition: ComponentDefinition = {
  id: '[component-name-kebab-case]',
  name: '[Human Readable Component Name]',
  category: 'Zimmermann Components',
  thumbnailUrl: '',
  variables: {
    // One entry per mapped prop
    [propName]: {
      displayName: '[Prop Name in Title Case]',
      type: '[Contentful type from mapping table]',
      defaultValue: [appropriate default],
      required: [true|false],
      // Add for select controls:
      // validations: { in: [{ value: 'option1' }, { value: 'option2' }] }
    },
  },
};
```

### 4. Update the defineComponents registry
- Locate the file that calls `defineComponents` (ask the developer if unsure —
  typically under `overrides/app/` somewhere like `registeredComponents.ts`).
- Read the current file contents.
- Add the import for the new component and its definition.
- Add the registration entry to the `defineComponents` array.
- Write the updated file.

### 5. Output a summary to the developer
Print a clear summary including:
- Which props were mapped and how.
- Which props were SKIPPED and why (e.g. event handlers, children).
- Any props that could not be automatically mapped and need manual review.
- The files created or modified.
- A reminder that the component definition `thumbnailUrl` is empty and should
  be updated with a preview image path.

## Important constraints
- Never modify the original React component file.
- Never add Contentful imports into the component itself — keep the definition
  separate.
- If a prop type cannot be determined (e.g. complex object, external type
  import), flag it clearly and skip it rather than guess.
- The registry file must be TypeScript (`.ts`) per the TypeScript-only rule for
  `overrides/`.
- Always verify the `defineComponents` file exists before trying to update it;
  if it does not exist, create it and note this in the summary.

3	description: Turn a plain-English feature request into a scoped implementation plan before any code is written. Asks one clarifying question at a time, then produces a spec Claude Code can execute safely. Use this before starting any non-trivial implementation session.
4	---
5	
6	Produce a scoped implementation spec for a feature before any code is written.
7	Follow each phase in order. Do not write code — this skill produces a plan only.
8	
9	---
10	
11	## Phase 1 — Clarification (one question at a time)
12	
13	Read the feature description the user has provided.
14	
15	Identify what is unclear or under-specified. Then ask ONE clarifying question — the most
16	important one. Wait for the answer. Ask the next question only after receiving a response.
17	
18	Continue until you have answers to all of these (stop earlier if the feature is simple):
19	- Which sprint does this belong to? (reference `.docs/memory/sprintScope.md` when present)
20	- Which PRD in [.docs/prd/](../../../.docs/prd/) is the source of truth for this feature? Cite section + requirement ID.
21	- Is this Zimmermann-specific or an enhancement to an existing PWA Kit pattern?
22	- Which squad owns the primary files involved? (A: checkout/cart/payments — B: PDP/PLP/search/account)
23	- Are there any Tier 1 or Tier 2 files that will need to change?
24	- Does this touch any third-party integration (Global-e, Adyen, Contentful, Searchspring/Einstein, Didomi, Omneo, Emarsys, AP21, Narvar, Google Maps)?
25	- What does "done" look like — what is the acceptance criterion?
26	- Are there any consent / Didomi gating requirements for scripts the feature loads?
27	
28	Do not ask about things the feature description already makes clear.
29	
30	---
31	
32	## Phase 2 — Parallel research
33	
34	Once clarification is complete, spawn three agents in parallel to research the codebase.
35	Each agent is independent and self-contained.
36	
37	**Agent A — Registry / file scan:**
38	*If `.claude/registry/` exists*, read `.claude/registry/components.md`,
39	`hooks.md`, and `utils.md`. *Otherwise*, do a direct scan: `find overrides/app/components overrides/app/hooks overrides/app/utils -type f` and grep for anything relevant.
40	Return: a list of relevant existing assets with their file paths.
41	
42	**Agent B — Pattern scan:**
43	Find the most similar existing feature in the codebase under `overrides/app/`.
44	Look for a component or page that has a similar interaction pattern or data shape.
45	Read its implementation to understand the conventions used (how it calls hooks, how it
46	handles loading/error states, how it structures its JSX, which Chakra components it uses).
47	Return: the path of the most similar existing implementation and a brief description of
48	the pattern it uses.
49	
50	**Agent C — Upstream check:**
51	Search `node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/` for any existing upstream implementation
52	of this feature or a related one. If found, assess whether the copy-first override workflow
53	(see [AGENTS.md](../../../AGENTS.md) — "Copy-first rule") should be applied.
54	Return: upstream file path if found, and a Take / Override / Skip recommendation.
55	
56	Wait for all three agents to return before proceeding to Phase 3.
57	
58	---
59	
60	## Phase 3 — Sprint check
61	
62	Reference `.docs/memory/sprintScope.md` (when present) and [.docs/memory/projectState.md](../../../.docs/memory/projectState.md).
63	
64	State which sprint this feature belongs to and confirm all its dependencies exist.
65	If the feature requires something from a later sprint, say so explicitly:
66	> "This feature depends on [X] which is Sprint [N] work and does not exist yet."
67	
68	Ask the developer whether to proceed with a placeholder or wait.
69	
70	---
71

75	
76	---
77	
78	```markdown

80	**PRD source:** [.docs/prd/<file>.md § <section> — <REQ-ID>]
81	**Sprint:** [N]
82	**Squad:** [A / B / Both]
83	**Estimated scope:** [S / M / L — S = 1 file, M = 2-5 files, L = 6+ files]
84	
85	### New files to create
86	| File path | What it is |
87	|---|---|
88	| overrides/app/... | [component / hook / util / test / story] |
89	
90	### Existing files to modify
91	| File path | Tier | Change needed |
92	|---|---|---|
93	| [path] | [1/2/3/4] | [description] |
94	
95	### Copy-first overrides required
96	| Base file (node_modules) | Target path under overrides/ | TS conversion needed? |
97	|---|---|---|
98	
99	### Hooks involved
100	| Hook | Status | Notes |
101	|---|---|---|
102	| [hook name] | [reuse / new / modify] | [any constraints] |
103	
104	### API / data shape
105	[What SCAPI endpoint or `@salesforce/commerce-sdk-react` hook provides the data? What does the response shape look like?]
106	
107	### Third-party integration touchpoints
108	[Any Global-e, Adyen, Contentful, Searchspring/Einstein, Didomi, Omneo, Emarsys, AP21, Narvar, Google Maps interaction — or "None". Include graceful-degradation behaviour per AGENTS.md.]
109	
110	### Acceptance criteria
111	[Bullet list from the developer's answer in Phase 1]
112	
113	### Suggested Claude Code prompt
114	[A ready-to-use, scoped prompt the developer can paste directly into Claude Code.
115	It must: name every file explicitly under overrides/app/..., state what to build,
116	end with "Do not modify any other files."]
117	
118	### PR checklist
119	- [ ] New files created at the paths above (TypeScript only inside `overrides/`)
120	- [ ] `*.stories.tsx` exists for every new UI component
121	- [ ] `*.test.ts` exists for every logic-heavy hook/util
122	- [ ] Tier 2 files (if any) flagged for second-developer review
123	- [ ] `npx tsc --noEmit` clean
124	- [ ] [/code-quality](../code-quality/SKILL.md) run on changed files before PR opened
125	```
126	
127	---
128	
129	## Notes
130	
131	- If the feature is genuinely simple (one file, no shared dependencies), skip Phase 2 and say so.
132	- If the developer cannot answer a clarifying question, treat it as a blocker and note it in the spec.
133	- The suggested prompt at the end is the primary deliverable — it is what gets pasted into the next Claude Code session.

6	Scaffold a new Zimmermann custom component.
7	
8	The component name is: $ARGUMENTS
9	
10	## Conventions
11	
12	Follow [.claude/rules/conventions.md](../../rules/conventions.md) — single source of truth
13	for naming, folder layout, props types, JSDoc policy, and Chakra token usage. Higher-level
14	project rules live in [AGENTS.md](../../../AGENTS.md). Do not restate rules here — read
15	conventions.md before scaffolding.
16	
17	Key implications for scaffolding:
18	- Component lives in its own folder: `componentName/index.tsx` (Zimmermann-authored) or
19	  `component-name/index.tsx` (override of a base SF component).
20	- Props type named `<ComponentName>Props`, declared at the top of `index.tsx` by default.
21	- Storybook story is mandatory; Vitest only when the component owns non-trivial logic.
22	
23	## Steps
24	
25	1. Read one nearby existing custom component under [overrides/app/components/](../../../overrides/app/components/) to match code style, import order, and Chakra usage. If no Zimmermann-authored component exists yet, read a base template component from `node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/` and convert the style to TypeScript + Chakra props.
26	
27	2. Create `overrides/app/components/<componentName>/index.tsx`:
28	   - Functional React component, named export (`export function <ComponentName>`) plus default export.
29	   - `type <ComponentName>Props = { ... }` at the top of the file.
30	   - JSDoc above the component if it will be consumed by ≥2 callers (shared/Tier 2).
31	   - Chakra primitives for layout (`Box`, `Flex`, `Text`, etc.) using theme tokens — no hardcoded hex, pixel spacing, or raw font sizes.
32	   - No commerce state hooks (`useCurrentBasket`, `useCurrentCustomer`, etc.) — accept data as props; the parent owns data fetching.
33	
34	3. Create `overrides/app/components/<componentName>/index.stories.tsx` — but first decide
35	   if a story is needed at all. Per [conventions.md](../../rules/conventions.md) →
36	   **Storybook**, purely internal sub-components that only render inside one parent
37	   don't need their own story; cover their variants via the parent. If a story *is* needed:
38	   - Storybook 8.6 CSF3 default export.
39	   - Pick the right category prefix from conventions.md — `Foundation/`, `Primitives/`,
40	     `Commerce/`, `Layout/`, `Forms/`, or `Pages/`. Ask the developer if it's not obvious
41	     which one fits (with your recommendation).
42	   - `title: '<Category>/<ComponentName>'` (e.g. `'Commerce/ProductTile'`,
43	     `'Layout/Header'`).
44	   - At least one named export `Default`. Add named exports for meaningful states only —
45	     not every prop combination.
46	   - Add a `play` function only if the component has interactive behaviour worth asserting.
47	
48	4. Optional: if the component owns non-trivial logic, also create `index.test.ts` (Vitest) in the same folder. Skip otherwise.
49	
50	5. Optional: if the props type exceeds ~30 lines or will be consumed by sibling files, move it to `types.ts` in the same folder. Otherwise leave it inline.
51	
52	6. Run `npx tsc --noEmit` and confirm zero new errors.
53	
54	## Constraints
55	
56	- Do not modify any existing files (no auto-wiring into routes, parents, or the theme registry).
57	- Do not add npm packages — see [AGENTS.md](../../../AGENTS.md) Hard Rule 7.
58	- Do not import from `node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/` source directly — re-export from `@salesforce/retail-react-app/...` paths.

60	
61	## Output

64	- The paths of every file created.
65	- The import to copy: `import <ComponentName> from '.../components/<componentName>'` (no filename — resolves via `index.tsx`).

1. Read one nearby existing custom component under [overrides/app/components/](../../../overrides/app/components/) to match code style, import order, and Chakra usage. If no Zimmermann-authored component exists yet, read a base template component from `node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/` and convert the style to TypeScript + Chakra props.

2. Create `overrides/app/components/<componentName>/index.tsx`:

   - `type <ComponentName>Props = { ... }` at the top of the file.

   - Chakra primitives for layout (`Box`, `Flex`, `Text`, etc.) using theme tokens — no hardcoded hex, pixel spacing, or raw font sizes.
   - No commerce state hooks (`useCurrentBasket`, `useCurrentCustomer`, etc.) — accept data as props; the parent owns data fetching.

3. Create `overrides/app/components/<componentName>/index.stories.tsx` — but first decide
   if a story is needed at all. Per [conventions.md](../../rules/conventions.md) →

   don't need their own story; cover their variants via the parent. If a story *is* needed:
   - Storybook 8.6 CSF3 default export.
   - Pick the right category prefix from conventions.md — `Foundation/`, `Primitives/`,

3	description: Interactive onboarding for new developers and QA engineers joining the Zimmermann PWA Kit project. Asks role at the start, checks the mechanical setup items, then orients the person to the rules and tools relevant to their role and squad. Run this in the first Claude Code session on a new machine or a first day on the project.
4	---
5	
6	Welcome the developer or QA engineer and explain what this skill does in one sentence.
7	Then proceed through the phases below. Ask one question at a time. Do not front-load.
8	
9	---
10	
11	## Phase 1 — Role and context
12	
13	Ask:
14	> "Are you joining as a developer or a QA engineer?"
15	
16	Wait for the answer. Then:
17	
18	**If developer:** Ask:
19	> "Which squad are you on — Squad A (checkout, cart, payments, order management, tax, GivX) or Squad B (Homepage, PDP, PLP, search, account, Brochureware Content)?"
20	
21	**If QA:** No squad question needed — QA covers both squads.
22	
23	Ask (both roles):
24	> "Is this your first time working on this project, or are you returning on a new machine?"
25	
26	New = full walkthrough. Returning on new machine = focus on mechanical setup, skip orientation.
27	
28	---
29	
30	## Phase 2 — Mechanical setup checks
31	
32	Run these checks inline using the Bash tool. Report results as you go.
33	
34	```bash
35	node --version
36	npm --version
37	claude --version 2>/dev/null || echo "NOT FOUND"
38	git branch --show-current
39	ls -la .git/hooks/ | grep -E 'pre-commit|commit-msg' || echo "hooks missing"
40	```
41	
42	For each issue found:
43	
44	**Hooks missing:**
45	> "The git hooks aren't installed on this machine. Run both of these now:"
46	```bash
47	cp scripts/hooks/pre-commit .git/hooks/pre-commit && chmod +x .git/hooks/pre-commit
48	cp scripts/hooks/commit-msg .git/hooks/commit-msg && chmod +x .git/hooks/commit-msg
49	```
50	Verify after: `ls -la .git/hooks/ | grep -E 'pre-commit|commit-msg'`
51	
52	**On develop or main:**
53	> "You're on the `{branch}` branch. You must always work on a feature branch. Create one now:"
54	```bash
55	git checkout -b feature/your-ticket-onboarding-setup
56	```
57	
58	**Node too old:** Point to the project's node requirement (24 LTS) and ask them to update before continuing.
59	
60	**Claude Code not found:** `npm install -g @anthropic-ai/claude-code` then `claude login`.
61	
62	Once all checks pass, say: "Setup is confirmed. Let's cover the rules and tools."
63	
64	---
65	
66	## Phase 3 — Developer orientation
67	
68	*Skip this phase for QA — go to Phase 4.*
69	
70	### Rules overview
71	
72	Walk through these in order — brief, one at a time, confirm understanding before continuing.
73	
74	**Branch rule (non-negotiable):**
75	> "Never work directly on `develop` or `main`. Every task gets a feature branch.
76	> Before each session: `git branch --show-current`. If it says develop, stop."
77	
78	**Protection tiers:**
79	> "Every file in this repo has a tier. Tier 1 = frozen, you cannot touch it without explicit
80	> owner approval. Tier 2 = protected, requires a second reviewer on the PR.
81	> The Tier 1 list is in [.claude/rules/frozenFiles.md](../../rules/frozenFiles.md). Read it before your first task."
82	
83	Point them to the full tier map: [.claude/rules/frozenFiles.md](../../rules/frozenFiles.md) and [.claude/rules/protectedFiles.md](../../rules/protectedFiles.md).

86	> "Every file you create or modify under `overrides/` must be `.ts` or `.tsx`.
87	> `.js`/`.jsx` are not acceptable in that folder — including theme files, stories, and config modules.
88	> Run `npx tsc --noEmit` before finishing any task that touches `overrides/`."

91	> "If requirements are unclear, Claude will ask one clarifying question at a time and wait.
92	> If you're prompting Claude and it asks a question, answer it before sending the next instruction."

---
name: onboarding
description: Interactive onboarding for new developers and QA engineers joining the Zimmermann PWA Kit project. Asks role at the start, checks the mechanical setup items, then orients the person to the rules and tools relevant to their role and squad. Run this in the first Claude Code session on a new machine or a first day on the project.
---

Welcome the developer or QA engineer and explain what this skill does in one sentence.
Then proceed through the phases below. Ask one question at a time. Do not front-load.

---

## Phase 1 — Role and context

Ask:
> "Are you joining as a developer or a QA engineer?"

Wait for the answer. Then:

**If developer:** Ask:
> "Which squad are you on — Squad A (checkout, cart, payments, order management, tax, GivX) or Squad B (Homepage, PDP, PLP, search, account, Brochureware Content)?"

**If QA:** No squad question needed — QA covers both squads.

Ask (both roles):
> "Is this your first time working on this project, or are you returning on a new machine?"

New = full walkthrough. Returning on new machine = focus on mechanical setup, skip orientation.

---

## Phase 2 — Mechanical setup checks

Run these checks inline using the Bash tool. Report results as you go.

```bash
node --version
npm --version
claude --version 2>/dev/null || echo "NOT FOUND"
git branch --show-current
ls -la .git/hooks/ | grep -E 'pre-commit|commit-msg' || echo "hooks missing"
```

For each issue found:

**Hooks missing:**
> "The git hooks aren't installed on this machine. Run both of these now:"
```bash
cp scripts/hooks/pre-commit .git/hooks/pre-commit && chmod +x .git/hooks/pre-commit
cp scripts/hooks/commit-msg .git/hooks/commit-msg && chmod +x .git/hooks/commit-msg
```
Verify after: `ls -la .git/hooks/ | grep -E 'pre-commit|commit-msg'`

**On develop or main:**
> "You're on the `{branch}` branch. You must always work on a feature branch. Create one now:"
```bash
git checkout -b feature/your-ticket-onboarding-setup
```

**Node too old:** Point to the project's node requirement (24 LTS) and ask them to update before continuing.

**Claude Code not found:** `npm install -g @anthropic-ai/claude-code` then `claude login`.

Once all checks pass, say: "Setup is confirmed. Let's cover the rules and tools."

---

## Phase 3 — Developer orientation

*Skip this phase for QA — go to Phase 4.*

### Rules overview

Walk through these in order — brief, one at a time, confirm understanding before continuing.

**Branch rule (non-negotiable):**
> "Never work directly on `develop` or `main`. Every task gets a feature branch.
> Before each session: `git branch --show-current`. If it says develop, stop."

**Protection tiers:**
> "Every file in this repo has a tier. Tier 1 = frozen, you cannot touch it without explicit
> owner approval. Tier 2 = protected, requires a second reviewer on the PR.
> The Tier 1 list is in [.claude/rules/frozenFiles.md](../../rules/frozenFiles.md). Read it before your first task."

Point them to the full tier map: [.claude/rules/frozenFiles.md](../../rules/frozenFiles.md) and [.claude/rules/protectedFiles.md](../../rules/protectedFiles.md).

**TypeScript-only rule:**
> "Every file you create or modify under `overrides/` must be `.ts` or `.tsx`.
> `.js`/`.jsx` are not acceptable in that folder — including theme files, stories, and config modules.
> Run `npx tsc --noEmit` before finishing any task that touches `overrides/`."

**Hard Rule #12:**
> "If requirements are unclear, Claude will ask one clarifying question at a time and wait.
> If you're prompting Claude and it asks a question, answer it before sending the next instruction."

**Contact map:**
Read [AGENTS.md](../../../AGENTS.md) contact map section. Tell them:
> "Design tokens → UI Designer (#design-system). Commerce hooks → Integration Lead (#integration).
> Checkout / cart → Squad A Lead. PDP / search / account → Squad B Lead."

### Sprint order

Read `.docs/memory/sprintScope.md` and [.docs/memory/projectState.md](../../../.docs/memory/projectState.md). Tell them which sprint the project is currently in.

> "We're in Sprint [N]. That means [what exists]. Code from Sprint [N+1] doesn't exist yet —
> don't reference it in your tasks."

### Squad-specific orientation

**Squad A (checkout, cart, payments):**
> "Your squad owns `overrides/app/pages/checkout/`, `overrides/app/components/order-summary/`,
> `overrides/app/components/promo-code/`, and `overrides/app/components/pickup-or-delivery/`.
> Before touching the header, footer, or shared product components, message Squad B Lead."

**Squad B (PDP, PLP, search, account):**
> "Your squad owns `overrides/app/pages/product-detail/`, `overrides/app/pages/product-list/`,
> `overrides/app/pages/account/`, and `overrides/app/components/product-tile/`.
> Before touching checkout or cart components, message Squad A Lead."

### Key skills

Tell them which skills to reach for first:
- [/session-start](../session-start/SKILL.md) — run at the start of every session (mandatory)
- [/feature-spec](../feature-spec/SKILL.md) — before starting any non-trivial implementation
- [/code-quality](../code-quality/SKILL.md) — before opening a PR
- [/pr-checklist](../pr-checklist/SKILL.md) — to generate PR description
- [/qa-generate](../qa-generate/SKILL.md) — when you need E2E test coverage for a user journey

### First task

> "Your first task: read [AGENTS.md](../../../AGENTS.md) and [.claude/rules/frozenFiles.md](../../rules/frozenFiles.md) end to end.
> Then run `/session-start` to see the current project state.
> When you have a ticket to work on, start with `/feature-spec` before writing any code."

---

## Phase 4 — QA orientation

*Skip this phase for developers — they went through Phase 3.*

### The QA model

> "This project uses a human-in-the-lead QA model. Claude generates tests — you validate them.
> A test is not complete until you have approved the Gherkin `.feature` file.
> Never accept a Playwright spec without reading and confirming the `.feature` file first."

### Testing layers

Three layers, three purposes (per [AGENTS.md](../../../AGENTS.md) > Testing):
1. **Vitest** — unit logic.
2. **Storybook `play` functions** — component interactions.
3. **Playwright** — E2E user journeys (this is where Gherkin lives).

### Feature file workflow

Walk through the workflow:
1. Developer creates a Jira story.
2. Developer runs [/qa-generate](../qa-generate/SKILL.md) in Claude Code.
3. Claude drafts a Gherkin `.feature` file and **stops**.
4. QA reads the `.feature` file — it's in `e2e/features/{area}/`.
5. QA annotates corrections in the file with `# QA ANNOTATION: [correction]`.
6. Developer runs `/qa-generate` again with the annotation.
7. Claude updates the feature file (confirm), then generates the Playwright spec.

Point them to `e2e/features/README.md` and the [Guide 4: E2E Testing — Playwright & Gherkin Repo Conventions](https://zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/SFCC/pages/305528833) Confluence page.

### Tags they must verify

Every `.feature` file needs:
- `@{JIRA-KEY}` — Jira traceability for Zephyr. **If missing, results won't sync.**
- `@{area}` — functional area tag
- `@p0` — only on confirmed critical paths (checkout, ATC, auth, PDP variant selection)

> "If a feature file is missing the Jira tag, flag it to the developer before the test is generated."

### Magento baseline regression

> "Files in `e2e/features/regression/` document Magento 2 expected behaviour.
> When a baseline test fails against SFCC, do NOT update it to pass.
> Add `# DELTA:` and bring it to the next standup for classification."

### BrowserStack and Zephyr

> "BrowserStack cross-browser runs trigger automatically on PRs to `release/**`.
> Results link to your Zephyr stories via BrowserStack Test Observability.
> Check with the delivery lead that your Jira account has access to the BrowserStack project."

### First task

> "Your first task: read the [Guide 4: E2E Testing — Playwright & Gherkin Repo Conventions](https://zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/SFCC/pages/305528833) Confluence page end to end.
> Then review the reference `.feature` file under `e2e/features/checkout/`. If you spot anything that reads like a technical implementation detail rather than plain English, that's exactly the kind of thing to flag in an annotation."

---

## Phase 5 — Confirm and close

Ask:
> "Any questions before you start?"

Answer questions, one at a time. Then close with:
> "You're set up. Run `/session-start` at the start of every session — it reads the tracking
> docs and confirms where the project is before any code is written.
> If something is unclear mid-task, ask in #dev-team before running Claude Code on it."

1	---
2	name: project-init
3	description: One-time project setup walkthrough. Runs the state detection script, fixes automatable items, asks one question at a time for human-input items, and updates the 7.1c CI/CD & Environment Setup Checklist Confluence page as each item is confirmed. Run this once when setting up the project for the first time, or when returning to check setup status.
4	---
5	
6	This skill has five phases. Do not skip ahead — the script output in Phase 1 determines
7	which phases are needed and in what order.
8	
9	---
10	
11	## Phase 1 — Run the state detector
12	
13	Run the check script:
14	```bash
15	bash scripts/projectInitCheck.sh
16	```
17	
18	Read the output carefully. Note every [FAIL], [WARN], and [TODO] item.
19	
20	Say to the developer:
21	> "Here's the current project setup status. I'll work through the issues in order."
22	
23	---
24	
25	## Phase 2 — Fix automatable failures
26	
27	For each [FAIL] item in the script output, in priority order:
28	
29	**Git hooks missing:**
30	Propose both commands together (they're always installed as a pair):
31	```bash
32	cp scripts/hooks/pre-commit .git/hooks/pre-commit && chmod +x .git/hooks/pre-commit
33	cp scripts/hooks/commit-msg .git/hooks/commit-msg && chmod +x .git/hooks/commit-msg
34	```
35	Ask for confirmation before running. After running, verify with:
36	```bash
37	ls -la .git/hooks/ | grep -E 'pre-commit|commit-msg'
38	```
39	
40	**Claude Code not installed:**
41	Provide the install command — do not run it yourself:
42	> "Run: `npm install -g @anthropic-ai/claude-code` then `claude login`"
43	
44	**GitHub CLI not installed:**
45	> "Install `gh` from https://cli.github.com/ — needed for branch protection setup in Phase 4."
46	
47	**Other FAIL items:** Provide the fix command, ask for confirmation, run it.
48	
49	After addressing all [FAIL] items, re-run `scripts/projectInitCheck.sh` and confirm PASS count improved.
50	
51	---
52	
53	## Phase 3 — Human-input items
54	
55	Work through [TODO] and [WARN] items one at a time. Ask one question, wait for the answer, update the relevant files, then ask the next.
56	
57	**Tracking setup status:** Setup status is tracked on the [7.1c CI/CD & Environment Setup Checklist](https://zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/SFCC/pages/305430530) Confluence page (space `SFCC`, page ID `305430530`), not in a repo file. Use the `confluence_get_page` tool to read current status before marking anything, and `confluence_update_page` to write back — resend the full page content with only the relevant Status cell changed from ⬜ to ✅. Never drop existing rows or other confirmed items when writing back.
58	
59	**Jira project key prefix**
60	> "What is the Jira project key prefix for this project? (e.g. ZIM, ZIM, PWA — shown before the ticket number)"
61	
62	When answered:
63	- Replace the placeholder `ZIM` in `e2e/features/README.md` (the naming section and tag examples)
64	- Replace `ZIM-000` in `e2e/features/checkout/ZIM-000_guest-checkout.feature` filename and tags — rename and update content
65	- Replace `ZIM-000` in `e2e/tests/zimm/checkout/ZIM-000_guest-checkout.p0.spec.ts` — rename and update
66	- Confirm the Jira key format used in the [Guide 4: E2E Testing](https://zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/SFCC/pages/305528833) Confluence page examples (`{JIRA-KEY}`, `@SFCC-NNN`) matches — update the page if the org uses a different prefix format
67	- Mark ✅ on the 7.1c Confluence page (see "Tracking setup status" above)
68	
69	**Upstream baseline (if WARN: UNSET)**
70	> "What `@salesforce/retail-react-app` version are we on? Check `package.json`."
71	
72	When answered: Update [.docs/memory/upstreamBaseline.md](../../../.docs/memory/upstreamBaseline.md) with the current version. Mark ✅ in checklist.
73	
74	**BrowserStack account**
75	> "Has a BrowserStack account been set up for this project? Have BROWSERSTACK_USERNAME and BROWSERSTACK_ACCESS_KEY been added to GitHub Secrets?"
76	
77	If yes: Mark ✅ in checklist. If no: Note who to contact (DevOps / Delivery Lead) and mark ⬜.
78	
79	**QA test account credentials**
80	> "Have PWA_E2E_USER_EMAIL and PWA_E2E_USER_PASSWORD been added to GitHub Secrets? These are the credentials for the registered test account in the SIT environment."
81	
82	Mark accordingly.
83	
84	**E2E product SKUs**
85	> "Have the test product SKUs been confirmed in the SIT catalogue and added to GitHub Secrets? (E2E_STANDARD_PRODUCT_SKU, E2E_VARIANT_PRODUCT_SKU, E2E_OOS_PRODUCT_SKU, E2E_SALE_PRODUCT_SKU)"
86	
87	Mark accordingly.
88	
89	**Zephyr integration**
90	> "Which Zephyr product does the team use — Zephyr Scale (Cloud) or Zephyr Squad? This determines how BrowserStack Test Observability syncs results."
91	
92	When answered: Update the comment in `.browserstack.yml` to name the correct product. Mark ✅ in checklist.
93	
94	**LHCI secrets**
95	> "Have LHCI_SERVER_BASE_URL, LHCI_TOKEN, and LHCI_TARGET_URL_SIT been added to GitHub Secrets? These power the Lighthouse CI trend server."
96	
97	Mark accordingly.
98	
99	**MuleSoft contract endpoint**
100	> "Has the MuleSoft team confirmed a contract endpoint or shared OpenAPI spec for the SIT environment? The `test:contracts` script is a placeholder until this is in place."
101	
102	Mark accordingly.
103	
104	**GitHub Pages**
105	> "Has GitHub Pages been enabled? Settings → Pages → source: GitHub Actions. This is required for Playwright report publishing on develop pushes."
106	
107	Mark accordingly.
108	
109	---
110	
111	## Phase 4 — Branch protection setup
112	
113	If `gh` is installed and the developer is ready to configure branch protection:
114	
115	> "Would you like me to set up release/** branch protection now? This requires admin access to the repo."
116	
117	If yes, propose this command for the developer to confirm and run:
118	```bash
119	gh api repos/{OWNER}/{REPO}/branches/release%2F*/protection \
120	  --method PUT \
121	  --field required_status_checks='{"strict":true,"contexts":["Digital SIT Gate"]}' \
122	  --field enforce_admins=true \
123	  --field required_pull_request_reviews=null \
124	  --field restrictions=null
125	```
126	
127	Note: Replace `{OWNER}/{REPO}` with the actual repo. The developer must have admin access.
128	Do not run this command yourself — propose it and let the developer confirm.
129	
130	If `gh` is not installed or the developer is not ready: note it as pending in the checklist.
131	
132	---
133

---
name: project-init
description: One-time project setup walkthrough. Runs the state detection script, fixes automatable items, asks one question at a time for human-input items, and updates the 7.1c CI/CD & Environment Setup Checklist Confluence page as each item is confirmed. Run this once when setting up the project for the first time, or when returning to check setup status.
---

This skill has five phases. Do not skip ahead — the script output in Phase 1 determines
which phases are needed and in what order.

---

## Phase 1 — Run the state detector

Run the check script:
```bash
bash scripts/projectInitCheck.sh
```

Read the output carefully. Note every [FAIL], [WARN], and [TODO] item.

Say to the developer:
> "Here's the current project setup status. I'll work through the issues in order."

---

## Phase 2 — Fix automatable failures

For each [FAIL] item in the script output, in priority order:

**Git hooks missing:**
Propose both commands together (they're always installed as a pair):
```bash
cp scripts/hooks/pre-commit .git/hooks/pre-commit && chmod +x .git/hooks/pre-commit
cp scripts/hooks/commit-msg .git/hooks/commit-msg && chmod +x .git/hooks/commit-msg
```
Ask for confirmation before running. After running, verify with:
```bash
ls -la .git/hooks/ | grep -E 'pre-commit|commit-msg'
```

**Claude Code not installed:**
Provide the install command — do not run it yourself:
> "Run: `npm install -g @anthropic-ai/claude-code` then `claude login`"

**GitHub CLI not installed:**
> "Install `gh` from https://cli.github.com/ — needed for branch protection setup in Phase 4."

**Other FAIL items:** Provide the fix command, ask for confirmation, run it.

After addressing all [FAIL] items, re-run `scripts/projectInitCheck.sh` and confirm PASS count improved.

---

## Phase 3 — Human-input items

Work through [TODO] and [WARN] items one at a time. Ask one question, wait for the answer, update the relevant files, then ask the next.

**Tracking setup status:** Setup status is tracked on the [7.1c CI/CD & Environment Setup Checklist](https://zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/SFCC/pages/305430530) Confluence page (space `SFCC`, page ID `305430530`), not in a repo file. Use the `confluence_get_page` tool to read current status before marking anything, and `confluence_update_page` to write back — resend the full page content with only the relevant Status cell changed from ⬜ to ✅. Never drop existing rows or other confirmed items when writing back.

**Jira project key prefix**
> "What is the Jira project key prefix for this project? (e.g. ZIM, ZIM, PWA — shown before the ticket number)"

When answered:
- Replace the placeholder `ZIM` in `e2e/features/README.md` (the naming section and tag examples)
- Replace `ZIM-000` in `e2e/features/checkout/ZIM-000_guest-checkout.feature` filename and tags — rename and update content
- Replace `ZIM-000` in `e2e/tests/zimm/checkout/ZIM-000_guest-checkout.p0.spec.ts` — rename and update
- Confirm the Jira key format used in the [Guide 4: E2E Testing](https://zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/SFCC/pages/305528833) Confluence page examples (`{JIRA-KEY}`, `@SFCC-NNN`) matches — update the page if the org uses a different prefix format
- Mark ✅ on the 7.1c Confluence page (see "Tracking setup status" above)

**Upstream baseline (if WARN: UNSET)**
> "What `@salesforce/retail-react-app` version are we on? Check `package.json`."

When answered: Update [.docs/memory/upstreamBaseline.md](../../../.docs/memory/upstreamBaseline.md) with the current version. Mark ✅ in checklist.

**BrowserStack account**
> "Has a BrowserStack account been set up for this project? Have BROWSERSTACK_USERNAME and BROWSERSTACK_ACCESS_KEY been added to GitHub Secrets?"

If yes: Mark ✅ in checklist. If no: Note who to contact (DevOps / Delivery Lead) and mark ⬜.

**QA test account credentials**
> "Have PWA_E2E_USER_EMAIL and PWA_E2E_USER_PASSWORD been added to GitHub Secrets? These are the credentials for the registered test account in the SIT environment."

Mark accordingly.

**E2E product SKUs**
> "Have the test product SKUs been confirmed in the SIT catalogue and added to GitHub Secrets? (E2E_STANDARD_PRODUCT_SKU, E2E_VARIANT_PRODUCT_SKU, E2E_OOS_PRODUCT_SKU, E2E_SALE_PRODUCT_SKU)"

Mark accordingly.

**Zephyr integration**
> "Which Zephyr product does the team use — Zephyr Scale (Cloud) or Zephyr Squad? This determines how BrowserStack Test Observability syncs results."

When answered: Update the comment in `.browserstack.yml` to name the correct product. Mark ✅ in checklist.

**LHCI secrets**
> "Have LHCI_SERVER_BASE_URL, LHCI_TOKEN, and LHCI_TARGET_URL_SIT been added to GitHub Secrets? These power the Lighthouse CI trend server."

Mark accordingly.

**MuleSoft contract endpoint**
> "Has the MuleSoft team confirmed a contract endpoint or shared OpenAPI spec for the SIT environment? The `test:contracts` script is a placeholder until this is in place."

Mark accordingly.

**GitHub Pages**
> "Has GitHub Pages been enabled? Settings → Pages → source: GitHub Actions. This is required for Playwright report publishing on develop pushes."

Mark accordingly.

---

## Phase 4 — Branch protection setup

If `gh` is installed and the developer is ready to configure branch protection:

> "Would you like me to set up release/** branch protection now? This requires admin access to the repo."

If yes, propose this command for the developer to confirm and run:
```bash
gh api repos/{OWNER}/{REPO}/branches/release%2F*/protection \
  --method PUT \
  --field required_status_checks='{"strict":true,"contexts":["Digital SIT Gate"]}' \
  --field enforce_admins=true \
  --field required_pull_request_reviews=null \
  --field restrictions=null
```

Note: Replace `{OWNER}/{REPO}` with the actual repo. The developer must have admin access.
Do not run this command yourself — propose it and let the developer confirm.

If `gh` is not installed or the developer is not ready: note it as pending in the checklist.

---

## Phase 5 — Final state and summary

Re-read the [7.1c CI/CD & Environment Setup Checklist](https://zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/SFCC/pages/305430530) Confluence page (via `confluence_get_page`) and confirm the current state of all items.

Produce a final summary:
```
✅ [N] items confirmed complete
⬜ [N] items still pending — owner and channel for each
```

List each pending item with its owner from the checklist table.

Then say:
> "Run `/project-init` again after each pending item is resolved to update the checklist.
> When all items are ✅, the project is ready for the first sprint."

---

## Notes

- Never modify `config/default.js`, `config/sites.js`, `overrides/app/ssr.js`, `worker/main.js`, or `.github/workflows/` during this skill
- Never push to `develop` or `main`
- For items that require infrastructure (BrowserStack, LHCI server, MuleSoft), note the owner and move on — do not block the session on them
- If this is a re-run (some items already ✅), skip confirmed items and focus only on what remains ⬜

4	---
5	
6	QA test generation is a two-step, human-gated process. Do not generate the Playwright spec
7	until the `.feature` file has been explicitly confirmed by Lead QA.
8	
9	> **Three testing layers in this project** (per [AGENTS.md](../../../AGENTS.md)):
10	> - Vitest — unit logic
11	> - Storybook `play` functions — component interactions
12	> - Playwright — E2E user journeys (this skill)

15	> the Vitest / Storybook layers — write all three where each applies.

18	> If `e2e/` does not yet exist, stop and tell the developer the QA harness must land first.
19	
20	---
21	
22	## Phase 1 — Gather story details
23	
24	Ask these questions one at a time. Wait for the answer before asking the next.
25	
26	1. What is the Jira story key? (e.g. SFCC-142)
27	2. What is the story title?
28	3. What are the acceptance criteria? (paste them directly)
29	4. Which squad owns this story? (Squad A: checkout/cart/payments — Squad B: PDP/PLP/search/account)
30	5. Which sprint is this? (Check `.docs/memory/sprintScope.md` — flag if the story references a later-sprint dependency)
31	6. Is this a P0 journey? (P0 = Digital SIT gate critical path: guest checkout, registered checkout, PDP variant selection, ATC, auth)
32	
33	---
34	
35	## Phase 2 — Draft the .feature file
36	
37	Write the Gherkin file to:
38	`e2e/features/{area}/{JIRA-KEY}_{short-description}.feature`
39	
40	Follow the standard in `e2e/features/README.md`:
41	- Tags: `@{JIRA-KEY} @{area}` — add `@p0` if confirmed in Phase 1
42	- Feature block with persona, goal, and value
43	- Background block for shared preconditions
44	- At least one happy path scenario and one failure/edge scenario
45	- Plain English only — no selectors, URLs, or implementation detail
46	- Under 150 lines — split by scenario group if longer
47	
48	**Stop here. Do not generate the Playwright test yet.**
49	
50	Present the draft and say:
51	> "This is the draft `.feature` file. Please share it with Lead QA for validation.
52	> When QA has approved or annotated it, reply with their feedback and I will proceed."
53	
54	---
55	
56	## Phase 3 — Apply QA annotations (if any)
57	
58	If Lead QA returns annotations in this format:
59	```
60	# QA ANNOTATION: [correction]
61	```
62	
63	Update the `.feature` file to reflect the correction. Confirm the change explicitly:
64	> "Updated [what changed]. No other changes made."
65	
66	Repeat until Lead QA confirms the file is correct.
67	
68	---
69	
70	## Phase 4 — Generate the Playwright spec
71	
72	Only proceed when Lead QA has confirmed the `.feature` file.
73	
74	Write the Playwright test to:
75	- `e2e/tests/zimm/{area}/{JIRA-KEY}_{description}.spec.ts` — for standard tests
76	- `e2e/tests/zimm/{area}/{JIRA-KEY}_{description}.p0.spec.ts` — for P0 tests
77	
78	Rules:
79	- Files are TypeScript (`.spec.ts`) — the TS-only convention applies to E2E too.
80	- Import Page Objects from `e2e/support/pages/` — never use raw selectors in the test file.
81	- Selector priority in POMs: accessible selectors (role + accessible name, label, text) > semantic HTML attributes (alt, title) > `data-testid` (only when no semantics apply). See [.claude/rules/testing.md](../../rules/testing.md).
82	- Import fixtures from `e2e/fixtures/` — never hardcode test data. Fixtures must be keyed by `SITE_ID` (Zimmermann has 7 storefronts across 11 active locales).
83	- Test description must match the Scenario name in the `.feature` file exactly.
84	- Use `waitForSelector` or `waitForResponse` — never `waitForTimeout`.
85	- Under 200 lines — extract shared logic to `e2e/support/helpers/` if needed.
86	
87	---
88	
89	## Phase 5 — Check for new Page Object needs
90	
91	Read the generated test. If it references an element not yet in any Page Object:
92	- Propose the addition to the relevant `e2e/support/pages/*.ts` file.
93	- Do not create a new Page Object file without confirming the path first.
94	- Page Object files stay under 150 lines — propose a split if exceeded.
95	
96	---
97	
98	## Phase 6 — Summary
99	
100	List every file created or modified:
101	- `.feature` file path
102	- `.spec.ts` file path
103	- Any Page Object additions
104	
105	Then say:
106	> "The `.feature` file requires Lead QA sign-off before this test is considered complete.
107	> If QA annotates further changes, run `/qa-generate` again with the updated story key."
108	
109	---
110	
111	## Notes
112	
113	- Never generate tests on `develop` or `main` — check `git branch --show-current` first.
114	- If the story references a component or hook from a later sprint (per `.docs/memory/sprintScope.md`),
115	  stop and flag it: the test may need to be deferred or the spec written with a placeholder.
116	- For Magento baseline regression tests, write to `e2e/features/regression/BASELINE-{area}-{behaviour}.feature`
117	  and note that these files use a `@baseline @regression` tag set, not a Jira key tag.

1	---
2	name: session-start
3	description: Run the mandatory session start ritual — reads tracking docs, runs branch + health checks, states current position. Use at the start of every coding session.
4	---
5	
6	Run the mandatory session start ritual defined in [AGENTS.md](../../../AGENTS.md). Do this before writing any code.
7	
8	## Steps (in order — do not skip any)
9	
10	1. **Confirm branch** — run `git branch --show-current`. If the output is `develop` or `main`, stop immediately — no edits permitted (see [AGENTS.md](../../../AGENTS.md) Hard Rule 1). If it matches `release/*` or `hotfix/*`, read [.docs/releaseBranchesRules.md](../../../.docs/releaseBranchesRules.md) in full before proceeding — the supervised-edit and back-merge rules there apply on top of the Hard Rules.
11	
12	2. **Read tracking docs** — read these in parallel:
13	   - [.docs/memory/projectState.md](../../../.docs/memory/projectState.md) — current phase, integration statuses (mock/live/not started), what's done and pending
14	   - [.docs/memory/sprintScope.md](../../../.docs/memory/sprintScope.md) — what exists this sprint, what is deferred. **Read before scoping any new work.**
15	   - [.docs/memory/feedback.md](../../../.docs/memory/feedback.md) — patterns to avoid or repeat
16	   - [.docs/memory/upstreamBaseline.md](../../../.docs/memory/upstreamBaseline.md) — current `@salesforce/retail-react-app` version and review state
17	   - [../session-notes.md](../session-notes.md) — lightweight, **gitignored, per-developer** carryover notes from your last local session (a Claude-writable staging area — see "Living Memory" below for how this differs from `.docs/memory/`). If it has pending items, surface them in step 4's "blockers or outstanding issues" and clear/promote each once resolved. It won't exist for a fresh clone or a teammate who hasn't used it — that's expected, skip silently.
18	
19	3. **Health checks** — run when the helper exists:
20	   - `bash scripts/healthCheckAll.sh` — If the script does not exist yet, state that clearly and skip.
21	
22	4. **State current position** — in plain language, say exactly:
23	   - Current branch
24	   - Current sprint / phase (from `projectState.md`)
25	   - The last completed task and the next task
26	   - Any blockers or outstanding issues
27	
28	   Format: "Resuming from: [last completed task]. Next: [next task]. [Any blockers or health issues]."
29	
30	5. **Confirm readiness** — ask if the user wants to proceed with the stated next task or redirect to something else.
31	
32	Do not write any code until this ritual is complete and the user has confirmed direction.
33	
34	---
35	
36	## Living Memory — what belongs where
37	
38	`.docs/memory/` is the project's persistent memory. Keep it current — update the relevant file whenever a session produces new information that belongs there.
39	
40	**`.claude/session-notes.md` is different: a lightweight, Claude-writable, gitignored, per-developer staging area** (same pattern as `userProfile.md` below, but for tasks rather than profile info) for short-lived carryover items (e.g. "still need to do X next session") that haven't been promoted to `.docs/memory/` yet. It's **not** shared via git — each developer's notes stay local, so they never conflict or overwrite a teammate's. Unlike the files below, Claude may write to it directly. Use it for quick pending-item tracking; move anything durable and team-relevant into the right `.docs/memory/` file once it's confirmed, and clear the note.
41	
42	| File | What belongs there | When to update |

---
name: session-start
description: Run the mandatory session start ritual — reads tracking docs, runs branch + health checks, states current position. Use at the start of every coding session.
---

Run the mandatory session start ritual defined in [AGENTS.md](../../../AGENTS.md). Do this before writing any code.

## Steps (in order — do not skip any)

1. **Confirm branch** — run `git branch --show-current`. If the output is `develop` or `main`, stop immediately — no edits permitted (see [AGENTS.md](../../../AGENTS.md) Hard Rule 1). If it matches `release/*` or `hotfix/*`, read [.docs/releaseBranchesRules.md](../../../.docs/releaseBranchesRules.md) in full before proceeding — the supervised-edit and back-merge rules there apply on top of the Hard Rules.

2. **Read tracking docs** — read these in parallel:
   - [.docs/memory/projectState.md](../../../.docs/memory/projectState.md) — current phase, integration statuses (mock/live/not started), what's done and pending
   - [.docs/memory/sprintScope.md](../../../.docs/memory/sprintScope.md) — what exists this sprint, what is deferred. **Read before scoping any new work.**
   - [.docs/memory/feedback.md](../../../.docs/memory/feedback.md) — patterns to avoid or repeat
   - [.docs/memory/upstreamBaseline.md](../../../.docs/memory/upstreamBaseline.md) — current `@salesforce/retail-react-app` version and review state
   - [../session-notes.md](../session-notes.md) — lightweight, **gitignored, per-developer** carryover notes from your last local session (a Claude-writable staging area — see "Living Memory" below for how this differs from `.docs/memory/`). If it has pending items, surface them in step 4's "blockers or outstanding issues" and clear/promote each once resolved. It won't exist for a fresh clone or a teammate who hasn't used it — that's expected, skip silently.

3. **Health checks** — run when the helper exists:
   - `bash scripts/healthCheckAll.sh` — If the script does not exist yet, state that clearly and skip.

4. **State current position** — in plain language, say exactly:
   - Current branch
   - Current sprint / phase (from `projectState.md`)
   - The last completed task and the next task
   - Any blockers or outstanding issues

   Format: "Resuming from: [last completed task]. Next: [next task]. [Any blockers or health issues]."

5. **Confirm readiness** — ask if the user wants to proceed with the stated next task or redirect to something else.

Do not write any code until this ritual is complete and the user has confirmed direction.

---

## Living Memory — what belongs where

`.docs/memory/` is the project's persistent memory. Keep it current — update the relevant file whenever a session produces new information that belongs there.

**`.claude/session-notes.md` is different: a lightweight, Claude-writable, gitignored, per-developer staging area** (same pattern as `userProfile.md` below, but for tasks rather than profile info) for short-lived carryover items (e.g. "still need to do X next session") that haven't been promoted to `.docs/memory/` yet. It's **not** shared via git — each developer's notes stay local, so they never conflict or overwrite a teammate's. Unlike the files below, Claude may write to it directly. Use it for quick pending-item tracking; move anything durable and team-relevant into the right `.docs/memory/` file once it's confirmed, and clear the note.

| File | What belongs there | When to update |
|---|---|---|
| `architecture.md` | Stack decisions, overrides pattern, key paths, structural choices | A new integration is added, a structural decision is made, or a key path changes |
| `projectState.md` | Phase, integration statuses (mock/live/not started), what's done and pending, unresolved dependencies | Any integration goes live, a phase changes, a feature is completed, or a dependency is resolved |
| `feedback.md` | What worked, what failed, patterns to avoid or repeat | After discovering a gotcha, a failed approach, or a validated pattern |
| `references.md` | Service URLs, API keys, credentials, logins, dashboards | A new credential or service URL is introduced (system roles live in `architecture.md`) |
| `userProfile.md` | User's role, expertise, working style, preferences | User shares a preference or working-style detail that should persist |

**Rules:**
- Never leave a file with only its placeholder comment — populate it the moment you learn something that belongs there.
- **No duplication.** Every fact has exactly one home. Before writing something, check whether it already lives in another doc — if it does, reference that doc instead of copying. Applies across all `.md` files: `AGENTS.md`, memory files, and PRDs.
- **Conciseness.** Keep all `.md` instructions concise.

2	name: upstream-sync-review
3	description: Review the release notes / changelog for a new @salesforce/retail-react-app version before bumping. Lightweight policy — see .docs/upstreamPolicy.md.
4	---
5	
6	This is a **slim overrides project** on `@salesforce/retail-react-app` — not a framework fork.
7	The policy is **"read the changelog, bump opportunistically"** — see [.docs/upstreamPolicy.md](../../../.docs/upstreamPolicy.md).
8	
9	This skill helps you review a candidate version bump before doing it.
10	
11	---
12	
13	## Input
14	
15	Ask the developer:
16	> "What candidate `@salesforce/retail-react-app` version are we considering? Paste a link to the GitHub release notes or the version number."
17	
18	If they give just a version (e.g. `10.1.0`), generate the release notes URL:
19	`https://github.com/SalesforceCommerceCloud/pwa-kit/releases/tag/v<X.Y.Z>`
20	
21	---
22	
23	## Step 1 — Capture current state
24	
25	Read [.docs/memory/upstreamBaseline.md](../../../.docs/memory/upstreamBaseline.md). Note:
26	- Current version
27	- Reviewed-up-to version
28	- Any deferred items
29	
30	---
31	
32	## Step 2 — Read the release notes
33	
34	Fetch the GitHub release notes for the candidate version (and any intermediate versions
35	between current and candidate). Summarise:
36	- Security fixes
37	- SCAPI / SDK breaking changes
38	- New configuration options
39	- Bug fixes that affect surfaces we override
40	
41	The bump policy says: bump opportunistically only when a release contains **security** or
42	**SDK** changes that affect us. Otherwise stay put.
43	
44	---
45	
46	## Step 3 — Map changes to our override surface
47	
48	For each notable change in the release notes, check whether we override the affected file
49	under `overrides/app/`. If yes, the upgrade may need a re-port of the override.
50	
51	Quick check:
52	```bash
53	ls overrides/app/<area-from-release-notes>/ 2>/dev/null
54	```
55	
56	For each override that may be affected, flag it as **Review** — the override must be
57	diffed against the new base file in `node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/` after the bump.
58	
59	---
60	
61	## Step 4 — Output a short recommendation
62	
63	Produce a brief recommendation in this shape:
64	
65	```markdown
66	## Upstream review: @salesforce/retail-react-app v<X.Y.Z>
67	
68	**Current:** vA.B.C (per upstreamBaseline.md)
69	**Candidate:** vX.Y.Z
70	**Reviewed:** [today's date]
71	
72	### Notable changes
73	- [bullet per relevant item from release notes]
74	
75	### Overrides that may need re-porting
76	| Override path | Reason |
77	|---|---|
78	| overrides/app/... | [release-note item] |
79	
80	### Recommendation
81	[BUMP / DEFER / WAIT FOR NEXT RELEASE] — with one-sentence reason.
82	
83	### If bumping
84	- [ ] Update `package.json` and `package-lock.json` via `npm install @salesforce/retail-react-app@<X.Y.Z>`
85	- [ ] Re-diff each flagged override against the new base file
86	- [ ] Run `npx tsc --noEmit`, `npm run lint`, `npm run build`
87	- [ ] Update `.docs/memory/upstreamBaseline.md` (Current + Reviewed up to)
88	```
89	
90	---
91	
92	## Notes
93	
94	- This skill does **not** modify any files — it produces a recommendation only.
95	- For Tier 1 files affected by the upgrade (`config/*`, `overrides/app/ssr.js`, `worker/main.js`), flag explicitly and require Integration lead approval before bumping.
96	- Do not run `npm install` yourself — the developer must approve and run it (see [AGENTS.md](../../../AGENTS.md) Hard Rule 7).

12	- Invoke a skill by typing `/skill-name` (optionally followed by an argument) in a Claude
13	  Code session. Each skill is a structured, reviewable process defined in its own
14	  `<skill-name>/SKILL.md` file — not a freeform prompt.

16	  follows the skill name, e.g. `/new-component productBadge` or `/audit-tier overrides/app/hooks/use-wish-list.ts`.

19	  checkpoint, or produces a read-only report/plan rather than making changes outright.
20	  See the checkpoint column in each table below.
21	- These `SKILL.md` files are also the master source for `.cursor/rules/skills/*.mdc` and

Run on a **first session on a new machine or first day on the project**.                    | Confirms understanding at each phase before moving on             |

Use before editing anything you're unsure about.                                                                                                                                          | Tells you who to notify before you touch the file                        |

51	| ---------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |

Produces a prioritised 🔴/🟡/🔵 report. Use after implementing a feature or before opening a PR. | Report only — you decide what to fix and when                                  |
53	| [`/pr-checklist`](pr-checklist/SKILL.md) | `/pr-checklist`                                                                         | Runs `/code-quality` on the current branch's changed files, classifies each by tier and reviewer requirement, and generates a copy-paste-ready PR description with a test checklist. 56	
57	| Skill                                  | Usage                                              | What it does                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               | Human-in-the-lead checkpoint                                                    |

62	
63	| Skill                                                                      | Usage                                                                                                  | What it does                                                                                                                                                                                               | Human-in-the-lead checkpoint                                                                              |
64	| -------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
65	| [`/contentful-register-component`](contentful-register-component/SKILL.md) | `/contentful-register-component <component file path>`                                                 | Reads an existing component's TypeScript props, generates a `*ContentfulDefinition.ts` file mapping each prop to a Contentful variable type, and wires it into the `defineComponents` registry.            | You review the generated definition (and any skipped/ambiguous props) before it's published in Contentful |
66	| [`/contentful-drift-check`](contentful-drift-check/SKILL.md)               | `/contentful-drift-check [component or directory path]` (no argument = scan all registered components) | **Read-only** comparison of component props against their paired Contentful definitions — reports added props, removed props, and type mismatches. Use after props change, or to audit everything at once. | Report only — you resolve any drift found                                                                 |
67	
68	## Release management
69	
70	| Skill                                                    | Usage                                                                                    | What it does                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    | Human-in-the-lead checkpoint                                                                                    |
71	| -------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
72	| [`/generate-changelog`](generate-changelog/SKILL.md)     | `/generate-changelog` (then answers version/range questions)                             | Builds a structured, four-audience changelog (dev team, QA, product, GitHub Release) from conventional commits and the upstream baseline. Writes to `docs/releases/`. Use before cutting a release branch.                                      | You review the changelog before it's published; the GitHub Release command is proposed, never run automatically |
73	| [`/upstream-sync-review`](upstream-sync-review/SKILL.md) | `/upstream-sync-review` (then supply a candidate `@salesforce/retail-react-app` version) | Reviews upstream release notes against `.docs/memory/upstreamBaseline.md`, maps changes to our override surface, and recommends BUMP / DEFER / WAIT — per the "read the changelog, bump opportunistically" policy in `.docs/upstreamPolicy.md`. | Recommendation only — you approve and run the actual `npm install` bump                                         |
74	
75	## Adding a new skill
76	
77	1. Create `.claude/skills/<skill-name>/SKILL.md` with `name` and `description` frontmatter (see any existing skill for the format).
78	2. Add it to the appropriate table above.
79	3. Add it to the skill list in [scripts/syncCursorRules.mjs](../../scripts/syncCursorRules.mjs) so it gets mirrored to `.cursor/rules/skills/` and `.vscode/instructions/workflows.md`, then run `npm run sync:ai-rules:fix`.
80	4. If it belongs in the [Project Setup Overview](https://zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/SFCC/pages/305102849) Confluence page's "Part 2" narrative, add a one-line mention there — but keep the detailed reference here to avoid duplication.

```
