1	# 13 — Google Tag Manager on Addingwell (Data Layer, Consent Mode v2, Tag Orchestration)
2	
3	## 1. Purpose and scope
4	
5	Google Tag Manager (GTM) is the tag orchestration layer for analytics and marketing on Zimmermann storefronts. The GTM container is **hosted on Addingwell** — a Didomi-owned managed tagging server — so the browser fetches `gtm.js` from a Zimmermann first-party subdomain (`ruffles.zimmermann.com`), not `www.googletagmanager.com`. The tags deployed via GTM (GA4, Meta Pixel, and any other tags Tell No Lies configures) are therefore served through Addingwell.
6	
7	> **Optimizely Web and Crazy Egg are NOT in GTM** (confirmed 2026-06-09). They load as separate **frontend-direct** tags, Didomi-consent-gated, not housed in the GTM container or served via Addingwell.
8	
9	The storefront's responsibility ends at correctly emitting a comprehensive data layer and pointing the loader at the Addingwell tagging-server URL. All downstream tags are loaded, configured, and maintained inside the GTM container by Zimmermann's marketing-technology partner Tell No Lies, who also operates the Addingwell workspace.
10	
11	In scope at the PWA layer:
12	
13	- GTM container loader (`gtm.js`) injection from the Addingwell first-party domain, post-Didomi consent
14	- A native, SFCC-aligned data layer (`window.dataLayer`) populated on every relevant event
15	- Google Consent Mode v2 default and update signal emission, propagated from Didomi to GTM
16	- Enhanced Conversions data — a hashed email at order confirmation (REG-056)
17	
18	Out of scope of this document (owned by Tell No Lies):
19	
20	- All tag configuration inside GTM (which tags fire, with what data, on which triggers)
21	- Downstream vendor scripts loaded via GTM: GA4, Meta Pixel, etc.
22	- Tag-side consent gating beyond what Consent Mode v2 conveys
23	- Experiment definitions in Optimizely; heatmap configuration in Crazy Egg (and the loading of those two scripts, which are frontend-direct tags owned by Tell No Lies — not GTM tags, per the note in §1)
24	
25	The handover boundary is fixed by AAB-001 and AAB-002: Accenture emits the data layer; Tell No Lies consumes it inside GTM.
26	
27	### Responsibilities boundary — Didomi, PWA, Addingwell, GTM, Tell No Lies
28	
29	| Party | Role | PWA relationship |
30	|---|---|---|
31	| **Didomi** (CMP) | Shows the cookie banner, captures consent, and signals which purposes/vendors are allowed. | PWA integrates the `@didomi/react` SDK and gates scripts on its signals. |
32	| **PWA** (storefront) | (1) Always emits the first-party data layer; (2) after Didomi grants consent, loads the GTM container from the Addingwell URL; (3) emits Consent Mode v2 signals derived from Didomi's state. | This is the full PWA scope. |
33	| **Addingwell** (Didomi-owned) | First-party hosting for the GTM container — serves `gtm.js` from a Zimmermann subdomain instead of `googletagmanager.com`. | PWA points the loader at the Addingwell URL; nothing more. |
34	| **GTM container** | Holds and fires GA4, Meta, and other TNL-configured tags. (Optimizely Web and Crazy Egg are NOT in GTM — they are frontend-direct tags; see §1 note.) | Out of PWA scope. |
35	| **Tell No Lies** | Zimmermann's marketing-technology partner; configures the GTM container and operates the Addingwell workspace. | Owns everything downstream of the data layer. |
36	
37	In one line: Didomi = consent; PWA = data layer + Consent Mode + load-GTM-post-consent; Addingwell = first-party hosting for GTM; GTM = the tag container; Tell No Lies = configures it all.
38	
39	## 2. Vendor relationship
40	
41	- **Vendor (orchestration layer):** Google — Google Tag Manager.
42	- **Vendor (hosting):** Addingwell, a Didomi-owned managed server-side GTM platform. The GTM container is hosted on Addingwell; the browser loads it from a Zimmermann first-party subdomain. Container IDs and Addingwell tagging-server URLs are provided to the PWA team by Tell No Lies.
43	- **Container ID (likely single).** Tell No Lies expects a **single GTM container ID** across all environments (to be confirmed — 2026-06-09 call). Any environment separation would be handled via the data layer rather than separate container IDs.
44	
45	## 3. Browser-side architecture
46	
47	```
48	Page load
49	        │
50	        ▼
51	Didomi loads first (strictly necessary) and emits Consent Mode v2 defaults to gtag
52	        gtag('consent', 'default', { ad_storage: 'denied', analytics_storage: 'denied', … })
53	        │
54	        ▼
55	Data layer is populated with first-party SFCC events regardless of consent (AAB-003)
56	        window.dataLayer.push({ event: 'page_view', page: { … } })
57	        │
58	        ▼
59	Didomi resolves the user's consent choice
60	        gtag('consent', 'update', { ad_storage: 'granted', analytics_storage: 'granted', … })
61	        │
62	        ▼
63	GTM container loads from the Addingwell first-party subdomain
64	(`https://ruffles.zimmermann.com/9i683nqysc4y77v.js?awl=M8PJ5D`), when analytics or
65	marketing consent is granted
66	        │
67	        ▼
68	Tell No Lies-configured tags fire per consent state — GA4 collects (with consent),
69	marketing tags only on grant. All tag requests route through Addingwell.
70	```
71	
72	- The data layer is always populated (AAB-003). It is first-party SFCC state — not a third-party script — and never gates on consent.
73	- The GTM container script is served from the Addingwell first-party subdomain and is loaded only after Didomi grants the relevant purpose. Because the request is first-party, it survives most cookie/tracking-prevention browser modes.
74	- Consent Mode v2 defaults are emitted as soon as Didomi reports user state, even before the GTM container loads. This follows Google's recommended pattern and enables Google's cookieless modelling downstream (configured by Tell No Lies).
75	
76	## 4. Authentication and credentials
77	
78	- GTM container ID: **`GTM-M8PJ5D`** — confirmed by Zimmermann 2026-06-10. Public; embedded in the loader.
79	- Addingwell tagging-server URL (`GTM_SERVER_URL`) — public, embedded in the loader. The first-party subdomain is **`ruffles.zimmermann.com`** (confirmed 2026-06-09). It is a Zimmermann-owned subdomain resolving to Addingwell infrastructure (DNS CNAME owned by Zimmermann; TLS cert managed by Addingwell). Per-environment host provisioning is a Zimmermann/Tell No Lies/Addingwell task.
80	- No secret credentials at the storefront layer. The Addingwell workspace API credentials live inside Tell No Lies' Addingwell account, not the PWA bundle.
81	
82	### Loader snippets (Tell No Lies, 2026-07-01)
83	
84	Confirmed Addingwell loader snippets provided by Tell No Lies on 2026-07-01. These supersede the vanilla GTM snippet Zimmermann sent on 2026-06-10. The Addingwell loader uses a custom path (`/9i683nqysc4y77v.js`) and `awl=` query parameter (the container ID with the `GTM-` prefix stripped), not the standard GTM CDN URL.
85	
86	In `<head>` as high as possible, post-Didomi-consent:
87	```html
88	<!-- Google Tag Manager -->
89	<script>(function(w,d,s,l,i){w[l]=w[l]||[];w[l].push({'gtm.start':
90	new Date().getTime(),event:'gtm.js'});var f=d.getElementsByTagName(s)[0],
91	j=d.createElement(s),dl=l!='dataLayer'?'&l='+l:'';j.async=true;j.src=
92	'https://ruffles.zimmermann.com/9i683nqysc4y77v.js?awl='+i.replace(/^GTM-/, '')+dl;f.parentNode.insertBefore(j,f);
93	})(window,document,'script','dataLayer','GTM-M8PJ5D');</script>
94	<!-- End Google Tag Manager -->
95	```
96	
97	Immediately after `<body>` (noscript fallback):
98	```html
99	<!-- Google Tag Manager (noscript) -->
100	<noscript><iframe src="https://ruffles.zimmermann.com/ns.html?id=GTM-M8PJ5D"
101	height="0" width="0" style="display:none;visibility:hidden"></iframe></noscript>
102	<!-- End Google Tag Manager (noscript) -->
103	```
104	
105	> **Note:** The noscript fallback renders when JavaScript is disabled. Because Didomi also requires JS, when this iframe fires the consent signal is irrelevant; the noscript path is a graceful degradation row.
106	
107	## 5. Data layer schema
108	
109	Per AAB-002, the data layer is the single source of truth. The storefront emits structured events for the lifecycle moments below. Event names follow GA4 e-commerce conventions for compatibility with the most common downstream consumer.
110	
111	> **Unconfirmed — pending Tell No Lies sign-off (open item 3).** The schema below is a proposal based on GA4 conventions and PRD requirements (AAB-002, AAB-004, AAB-005). Tell No Lies must confirm it satisfies the GTM tags before implementation.
112	
113	| Event | When | Key fields |
114	|---|---|---|
115	| `page_view` | Every page load and SPA route change | page type, storefront, locale, customer hash (if logged in), authenticated state, customer group |
116	| `view_item_list` | PLP or search results page | list ID, list name, items[] |
117	| `view_item` | PDP load | item (id, name, brand, category, price, currency, variant, size) |
118	| `select_item` | PLP tile click | list context, item |
119	| `add_to_cart` | Add-to-bag success | item, currency, value |
120	| `remove_from_cart` | Cart remove | item, currency, value |
121	| `view_cart` | Cart page load | items[], currency, value |
122	| `begin_checkout` | Checkout entry | items[], currency, value |
123	| `add_shipping_info` | Delivery method selected | shipping_tier, items[], currency, value |
124	| `add_payment_info` | Payment method selected | payment_type, items[], currency, value |
125	| `purchase` | Order placed | transaction_id, value, currency, tax, shipping, items[], hashed email (REG-056) |
126	| `refund` | Order refunded (where surfaced in storefront) | transaction_id, value |
127	| `login` | Successful login | method |
128	| `sign_up` | Successful registration | method |
129	| `consent_decision` | Didomi banner dismissed | decision_summary (non-PII) |
130	
131	Attributes available on every event (AAB-004 Optimizely segmentation; AAB-005 Crazy Egg):
132	
133	- `storefront_region` (AU, US, UK, EU, EU-INTL, HK, ME) — sourced from Zimmermann's geolocation logic and the Global-e platform (AAB-002)
134	- `locale` (en-AU, fr-EU, …)
135	- `currency` (storefront base currency)
136	- `authenticated` (boolean)
137	- `customer_group` (SFCC customer group)
138	- `loyalty_status` (Retail Rewards tier)
139	- `visitor_type` (new vs returning)
140	- `existing_customer` (boolean — returning vs first-time customer, AAB-002)
141	- `lifetime_value` (customer lifetime value, AAB-002)
142	- `device_type` (mobile, tablet, desktop)
143	
144	## 6. Consent Mode v2 mapping (Didomi → gtag)
145	
146	> **Left column unconfirmed.** The Didomi purpose names below are Didomi's standard IAB TCF identifiers. Zimmermann's actual Didomi configuration may use different IDs — verify against the provisioned account once Didomi open item 1 is resolved. The right column (Consent Mode v2 signals) is from Google's official Consent Mode v2 documentation and is authoritative.
147	
148	| Didomi purpose | Consent Mode v2 signal |
149	|---|---|
150	| `measure_audience` / `analytics` | `analytics_storage` |
151	| `select_personalized_ads` / `targeted_advertising` | `ad_storage`, `ad_personalization`, `ad_user_data` |
152	| `personalize_content` | `personalization_storage` |
153	| `functional` | `functionality_storage`, `security_storage` |
154	
155	Defaults emitted before Didomi resolves are all denied (fail-closed). The update is emitted as soon as Didomi reports the user's choice. The `region` parameter on the default `gtag('consent', 'default', …)` call is used where regulation differs (e.g. `region: ['US']` for the US opt-out posture; rest of world is opt-in). The per-region default states themselves are owned by the Didomi configuration.
156	
157	## 7. Performance and loading strategy
158	
159	- The GTM loader script is small and loaded asynchronously, deferred until after Didomi grants the relevant consent. It does not contribute to LCP.
160	- `<link rel="preconnect">` to the Addingwell first-party hostname (`GTM_SERVER_URL`) is emitted from the document head once consent is granted. No preconnect to `www.googletagmanager.com` is needed — the container is not served from there.
161	
162	## 8. Multi-region behaviour
163	
164	- One GTM container ID across all storefronts (and most likely across all environments too — Tell No Lies to confirm), with region and storefront discrimination via the data layer attributes in §5. This is the assumed Tell No Lies pattern and the simplest model to maintain.
165	- Per-region Consent Mode default states (US opt-out posture vs rest-of-world opt-in posture) are emitted via the `region` parameter on the default `gtag('consent', 'default', …)` call. The actual per-region defaults are configured in the Didomi Console; the storefront translates Didomi state into Consent Mode signals without holding regional logic itself.
166	
167	## 9. Failure modes and graceful degradation
168	
169	| Failure | Behaviour |
170	|---|---|
171	| GTM container fails to load | Storefront unaffected. The data layer continues to populate; tags simply do not fire. |
172	| Didomi never resolves consent | GTM is never loaded; Consent Mode defaults remain denied. Pages work; analytics is absent. |
173	| A downstream tag configured by Tell No Lies errors | Tag-level — does not affect the page. GTM isolates tag failures. |
174	| A data-layer push throws | Every `dataLayer.push` is wrapped in `try / catch`; on failure the storefront logs to monitoring but never blocks the user flow. |
175	
176	## 10. Security and privacy
177	
178	- The hashed email on `purchase` is a SHA-256 hash of the normalised customer email (REG-056). No raw email appears in the data layer. Normalisation follows Google's Enhanced Conversions spec: trim whitespace, lowercase; for `@gmail.com` / `@googlemail.com` addresses additionally remove dots from the local part and strip any `+suffix`.
179	- No PII appears in any data layer event beyond the hashed email. Customer IDs are hashed when present.
180	- No card data ever reaches the data layer. PCI scope is not affected by this integration.
181	
182	## 11. Open items requiring client confirmation
183	
184	1. **Addingwell tagging-server URL (per environment).** The production first-party subdomain is confirmed as `ruffles.zimmermann.com` (2026-06-09). **Zimmermann/Accenture** to provision the equivalent first-party host for each non-production environment (each must be first-party to that environment's storefront domain). # 13 — Google Tag Manager on Addingwell (Data Layer, Consent Mode v2, Tag Orchestration)

## 1. Purpose and scope

Google Tag Manager (GTM) is the tag orchestration layer for analytics and marketing on Zimmermann storefronts. The GTM container is **hosted on Addingwell** — a Didomi-owned managed tagging server — so the browser fetches `gtm.js` from a Zimmermann first-party subdomain (`ruffles.zimmermann.com`), not `www.googletagmanager.com`. The tags deployed via GTM (GA4, Meta Pixel, and any other tags Tell No Lies configures) are therefore served through Addingwell.

> **Optimizely Web and Crazy Egg are NOT in GTM** (confirmed 2026-06-09). They load as separate **frontend-direct** tags, Didomi-consent-gated, not housed in the GTM container or served via Addingwell.

The storefront's responsibility ends at correctly emitting a comprehensive data layer and pointing the loader at the Addingwell tagging-server URL. All downstream tags are loaded, configured, and maintained inside the GTM container by Zimmermann's marketing-technology partner Tell No Lies, who also operates the Addingwell workspace.

In scope at the PWA layer:

- GTM container loader (`gtm.js`) injection from the Addingwell first-party domain, post-Didomi consent
- A native, SFCC-aligned data layer (`window.dataLayer`) populated on every relevant event
- Google Consent Mode v2 default and update signal emission, propagated from Didomi to GTM
- Enhanced Conversions data — a hashed email at order confirmation (REG-056)

Out of scope of this document (owned by Tell No Lies):

- All tag configuration inside GTM (which tags fire, with what data, on which triggers)
- Downstream vendor scripts loaded via GTM: GA4, Meta Pixel, etc.
- Tag-side consent gating beyond what Consent Mode v2 conveys
- Experiment definitions in Optimizely; heatmap configuration in Crazy Egg (and the loading of those two scripts, which are frontend-direct tags owned by Tell No Lies — not GTM tags, per the note in §1)

The handover boundary is fixed by AAB-001 and AAB-002: Accenture emits the data layer; Tell No Lies consumes it inside GTM.

### Responsibilities boundary — Didomi, PWA, Addingwell, GTM, Tell No Lies

| Party | Role | PWA relationship |
|---|---|---|
| **Didomi** (CMP) | Shows the cookie banner, captures consent, and signals which purposes/vendors are allowed. | PWA integrates the `@didomi/react` SDK and gates scripts on its signals. |
| **PWA** (storefront) | (1) Always emits the first-party data layer; (2) after Didomi grants consent, loads the GTM container from the Addingwell URL; (3) emits Consent Mode v2 signals derived from Didomi's state. | This is the full PWA scope. |
| **Addingwell** (Didomi-owned) | First-party hosting for the GTM container — serves `gtm.js` from a Zimmermann subdomain instead of `googletagmanager.com`. | PWA points the loader at the Addingwell URL; nothing more. |
| **GTM container** | Holds and fires GA4, Meta, and other TNL-configured tags. (Optimizely Web and Crazy Egg are NOT in GTM — they are frontend-direct tags; see §1 note.) | Out of PWA scope. |
| **Tell No Lies** | Zimmermann's marketing-technology partner; configures the GTM container and operates the Addingwell workspace. | Owns everything downstream of the data layer. |

In one line: Didomi = consent; PWA = data layer + Consent Mode + load-GTM-post-consent; Addingwell = first-party hosting for GTM; GTM = the tag container; Tell No Lies = configures it all.

## 2. Vendor relationship

- **Vendor (orchestration layer):** Google — Google Tag Manager.
- **Vendor (hosting):** Addingwell, a Didomi-owned managed server-side GTM platform. The GTM container is hosted on Addingwell; the browser loads it from a Zimmermann first-party subdomain. Container IDs and Addingwell tagging-server URLs are provided to the PWA team by Tell No Lies.
- **Container ID (likely single).** Tell No Lies expects a **single GTM container ID** across all environments (to be confirmed — 2026-06-09 call). Any environment separation would be handled via the data layer rather than separate container IDs.

## 3. Browser-side architecture

```
Page load
        │
        ▼
Didomi loads first (strictly necessary) and emits Consent Mode v2 defaults to gtag
        gtag('consent', 'default', { ad_storage: 'denied', analytics_storage: 'denied', … })
        │
        ▼
Data layer is populated with first-party SFCC events regardless of consent (AAB-003)
        window.dataLayer.push({ event: 'page_view', page: { … } })
        │
        ▼
Didomi resolves the user's consent choice
        gtag('consent', 'update', { ad_storage: 'granted', analytics_storage: 'granted', … })
        │
        ▼
GTM container loads from the Addingwell first-party subdomain
(`https://ruffles.zimmermann.com/9i683nqysc4y77v.js?awl=M8PJ5D`), when analytics or
marketing consent is granted
        │
        ▼
Tell No Lies-configured tags fire per consent state — GA4 collects (with consent),
marketing tags only on grant. All tag requests route through Addingwell.
```

- The data layer is always populated (AAB-003). It is first-party SFCC state — not a third-party script — and never gates on consent.
- The GTM container script is served from the Addingwell first-party subdomain and is loaded only after Didomi grants the relevant purpose. Because the request is first-party, it survives most cookie/tracking-prevention browser modes.
- Consent Mode v2 defaults are emitted as soon as Didomi reports user state, even before the GTM container loads. This follows Google's recommended pattern and enables Google's cookieless modelling downstream (configured by Tell No Lies).

## 4. Authentication and credentials

- GTM container ID: **`GTM-M8PJ5D`** — confirmed by Zimmermann 2026-06-10. Public; embedded in the loader.
- Addingwell tagging-server URL (`GTM_SERVER_URL`) — public, embedded in the loader. The first-party subdomain is **`ruffles.zimmermann.com`** (confirmed 2026-06-09). It is a Zimmermann-owned subdomain resolving to Addingwell infrastructure (DNS CNAME owned by Zimmermann; TLS cert managed by Addingwell). Per-environment host provisioning is a Zimmermann/Tell No Lies/Addingwell task.
- No secret credentials at the storefront layer. The Addingwell workspace API credentials live inside Tell No Lies' Addingwell account, not the PWA bundle.

### Loader snippets (Tell No Lies, 2026-07-01)

Confirmed Addingwell loader snippets provided by Tell No Lies on 2026-07-01. These supersede the vanilla GTM snippet Zimmermann sent on 2026-06-10. The Addingwell loader uses a custom path (`/9i683nqysc4y77v.js`) and `awl=` query parameter (the container ID with the `GTM-` prefix stripped), not the standard GTM CDN URL.

In `<head>` as high as possible, post-Didomi-consent:
```html
<!-- Google Tag Manager -->
<script>(function(w,d,s,l,i){w[l]=w[l]||[];w[l].push({'gtm.start':
new Date().getTime(),event:'gtm.js'});var f=d.getElementsByTagName(s)[0],
j=d.createElement(s),dl=l!='dataLayer'?'&l='+l:'';j.async=true;j.src=
'https://ruffles.zimmermann.com/9i683nqysc4y77v.js?awl='+i.replace(/^GTM-/, '')+dl;f.parentNode.insertBefore(j,f);
})(window,document,'script','dataLayer','GTM-M8PJ5D');</script>
<!-- End Google Tag Manager -->
```

Immediately after `<body>` (noscript fallback):
```html
<!-- Google Tag Manager (noscript) -->
<noscript><iframe src="https://ruffles.zimmermann.com/ns.html?id=GTM-M8PJ5D"
height="0" width="0" style="display:none;visibility:hidden"></iframe></noscript>
<!-- End Google Tag Manager (noscript) -->
```

> **Note:** The noscript fallback renders when JavaScript is disabled. Because Didomi also requires JS, when this iframe fires the consent signal is irrelevant; the noscript path is a graceful degradation row.

## 5. Data layer schema

Per AAB-002, the data layer is the single source of truth. The storefront emits structured events for the lifecycle moments below. Event names follow GA4 e-commerce conventions for compatibility with the most common downstream consumer.

> **Unconfirmed — pending Tell No Lies sign-off (open item 3).** The schema below is a proposal based on GA4 conventions and PRD requirements (AAB-002, AAB-004, AAB-005). Tell No Lies must confirm it satisfies the GTM tags before implementation.

| Event | When | Key fields |
|---|---|---|
| `page_view` | Every page load and SPA route change | page type, storefront, locale, customer hash (if logged in), authenticated state, customer group |
| `view_item_list` | PLP or search results page | list ID, list name, items[] |
| `view_item` | PDP load | item (id, name, brand, category, price, currency, variant, size) |
| `select_item` | PLP tile click | list context, item |
| `add_to_cart` | Add-to-bag success | item, currency, value |
| `remove_from_cart` | Cart remove | item, currency, value |
| `view_cart` | Cart page load | items[], currency, value |
| `begin_checkout` | Checkout entry | items[], currency, value |
| `add_shipping_info` | Delivery method selected | shipping_tier, items[], currency, value |
| `add_payment_info` | Payment method selected | payment_type, items[], currency, value |
| `purchase` | Order placed | transaction_id, value, currency, tax, shipping, items[], hashed email (REG-056) |
| `refund` | Order refunded (where surfaced in storefront) | transaction_id, value |
| `login` | Successful login | method |
| `sign_up` | Successful registration | method |
| `consent_decision` | Didomi banner dismissed | decision_summary (non-PII) |

Attributes available on every event (AAB-004 Optimizely segmentation; AAB-005 Crazy Egg):

- `storefront_region` (AU, US, UK, EU, EU-INTL, HK, ME) — sourced from Zimmermann's geolocation logic and the Global-e platform (AAB-002)
- `locale` (en-AU, fr-EU, …)
- `currency` (storefront base currency)
- `authenticated` (boolean)
- `customer_group` (SFCC customer group)
- `loyalty_status` (Retail Rewards tier)
- `visitor_type` (new vs returning)
- `existing_customer` (boolean — returning vs first-time customer, AAB-002)
- `lifetime_value` (customer lifetime value, AAB-002)
- `device_type` (mobile, tablet, desktop)

## 6. Consent Mode v2 mapping (Didomi → gtag)

> **Left column unconfirmed.** The Didomi purpose names below are Didomi's standard IAB TCF identifiers. Zimmermann's actual Didomi configuration may use different IDs — verify against the provisioned account once Didomi open item 1 is resolved. The right column (Consent Mode v2 signals) is from Google's official Consent Mode v2 documentation and is authoritative.

| Didomi purpose | Consent Mode v2 signal |
|---|---|
| `measure_audience` / `analytics` | `analytics_storage` |
| `select_personalized_ads` / `targeted_advertising` | `ad_storage`, `ad_personalization`, `ad_user_data` |
| `personalize_content` | `personalization_storage` |
| `functional` | `functionality_storage`, `security_storage` |

Defaults emitted before Didomi resolves are all denied (fail-closed). The update is emitted as soon as Didomi reports the user's choice. The `region` parameter on the default `gtag('consent', 'default', …)` call is used where regulation differs (e.g. `region: ['US']` for the US opt-out posture; rest of world is opt-in). The per-region default states themselves are owned by the Didomi configuration.

## 7. Performance and loading strategy

- The GTM loader script is small and loaded asynchronously, deferred until after Didomi grants the relevant consent. It does not contribute to LCP.
- `<link rel="preconnect">` to the Addingwell first-party hostname (`GTM_SERVER_URL`) is emitted from the document head once consent is granted. No preconnect to `www.googletagmanager.com` is needed — the container is not served from there.

## 8. Multi-region behaviour

- One GTM container ID across all storefronts (and most likely across all environments too — Tell No Lies to confirm), with region and storefront discrimination via the data layer attributes in §5. This is the assumed Tell No Lies pattern and the simplest model to maintain.
- Per-region Consent Mode default states (US opt-out posture vs rest-of-world opt-in posture) are emitted via the `region` parameter on the default `gtag('consent', 'default', …)` call. The actual per-region defaults are configured in the Didomi Console; the storefront translates Didomi state into Consent Mode signals without holding regional logic itself.

## 9. Failure modes and graceful degradation

| Failure | Behaviour |
|---|---|
| GTM container fails to load | Storefront unaffected. The data layer continues to populate; tags simply do not fire. |
| Didomi never resolves consent | GTM is never loaded; Consent Mode defaults remain denied. Pages work; analytics is absent. |
| A downstream tag configured by Tell No Lies errors | Tag-level — does not affect the page. GTM isolates tag failures. |
| A data-layer push throws | Every `dataLayer.push` is wrapped in `try / catch`; on failure the storefront logs to monitoring but never blocks the user flow. |

## 10. Security and privacy

- The hashed email on `purchase` is a SHA-256 hash of the normalised customer email (REG-056). No raw email appears in the data layer. Normalisation follows Google's Enhanced Conversions spec: trim whitespace, lowercase; for `@gmail.com` / `@googlemail.com` addresses additionally remove dots from the local part and strip any `+suffix`.
- No PII appears in any data layer event beyond the hashed email. Customer IDs are hashed when present.
- No card data ever reaches the data layer. PCI scope is not affected by this integration.

## 11. Open items requiring client confirmation

1. **Addingwell tagging-server URL (per environment).** The production first-party subdomain is confirmed as `ruffles.zimmermann.com` (2026-06-09). **Zimmermann/Accenture** to provision the equivalent first-party host for each non-production environment (each must be first-party to that environment's storefront domain). The PWA points the loader at this URL.
2. **Data layer schema confirmation.** GTM's own tags (GA4, Meta) consume the data layer. The **frontend-direct** Optimizely and Crazy Egg scripts (which are *not* GTM tags — see §1) may also read it, but whether they require any PWA-emitted attributes at all is open (AAB-004 / AAB-005 — Tell No Lies to confirm; may be dropped). Tell No Lies to confirm the event and attribute schema in §5 satisfies the GTM tags, and to confirm whether any additional attributes are needed for Optimizely segmentation (AAB-004) or Crazy Egg filtering (AAB-005).

# 15 — Optimizely Web (Experimentation)

## 1. Purpose and scope

Optimizely Web Experimentation provides A/B testing and personalisation on the **US storefront only**. It runs as a **frontend-direct** script — not through GTM or Addingwell (AAB-004). Zimmermann provides the snippet. A single snippet serves all environments.

PWA obligations:

- Inject the Optimizely snippet in the page `<head>` before render, gated on Didomi consent — US storefront only (AAB-004)
- Populate the data layer with the segmentation attributes Optimizely reads for audience targeting (AAB-002 + AAB-004)

Tell No Lies owns experiment definitions, variation logic, and audience configuration inside Optimizely.

## 2. Loading architecture

The snippet must be in the `<head>` before render so experiments apply synchronously, without flicker.

```
Page load (US storefront only)
         │
         ▼
Storefront populates window.dataLayer with segmentation attributes
         │
         ▼
Didomi grants the relevant consent category (TBC — see open item 2)
         │
         ▼
PWA injects Optimizely snippet in the page <head> before render
         │
         ▼
Optimizely reads data-layer attributes and applies experiments — no flicker
```

**LCP trade-off:** a synchronous head script can affect LCP. Where head-loading conflicts with the LCP budget, anti-flicker takes priority — a deliberate, scoped exception limited to the US storefront (decision 2026-06-11). All other storefronts are unaffected.

## 3. Authentication and credentials

- No server-side secret at the storefront layer. The Optimizely project ID and snippet URL are embedded in the snippet itself and are public.
- **Snippet confirmed by Zimmermann 2026-06-10.** One snippet serves all environments.
- **Project ID:** `4599769641779200`

### Snippet

```html
<script src="https://cdn.optimizely.com/js/4599769641779200.js"></script>
```

Place as close to the opening `<head>` tag as possible on all pages of the **US storefront only**, gated on Didomi consent (see §5).

## 4. Data layer

| Attribute | Notes |
|---|---|
| Authenticated state | Logged-in or guest |
| Customer group | SFCC customer group |
| Loyalty status | From AP21 / Omneo post-login |
| Storefront region | Which of the seven storefronts |

The exact attribute names must be agreed with Tell No Lies as part of the shared data-layer schema confirmation (see GTM open item §13.3 in `openItems.md`). No raw PII is included.

## 5. Consent

The snippet loads only after Didomi grants the relevant consent category (TBC — Zimmermann Privacy to confirm; expected to be Analytics). If consent is denied or undetermined the snippet does not load and the shopper sees the default experience. Fail closed: on unknown consent state, do not load.

## 6. Failure modes

| Failure | Behaviour |
|---|---|
| Snippet fails to load | No experiments run; storefront renders the default experience |
| Consent denied or undetermined | Snippet not loaded; default experience |

## 7. Open items

1	# 16 — Crazy Egg (Heatmaps & Session Recording)
2	
3	## 1. Purpose and scope
4	
5	Crazy Egg provides heatmaps and session recordings for behavioural analysis across all Zimmermann storefronts. It runs as a **frontend-direct** script — not through GTM or Addingwell (AAB-005). The PWA loads the snippet in the page `<head>` so capture begins from page load. The snippet is gated on Didomi consent (category TBC — Zimmermann Privacy to confirm; expected Analytics).
6	
7	PWA obligations:
8	
9	- Inject the Crazy Egg snippet in the page `<head>`, after Didomi consent, so capture begins from page load (AAB-005)
10	- Populate the data layer with page type, authenticated state, and storefront region so Crazy Egg can segment and suppress recordings (AAB-002 + AAB-005)
11	- Render payment and PII fields with stable, maskable selectors so Tell No Lies can reliably target them for suppression in the Crazy Egg app (see §5)
12	
13	Segmentation, suppression, and masking configuration sit in the Crazy Egg application, owned by Tell No Lies outside the PWA.
14	
15	## 2. Loading architecture
16	
17	```
18	Page load
19	         │
20	         ▼
21	Storefront populates window.dataLayer with page type, auth state, storefront region
22	         │
23	         ▼
24	Didomi grants the relevant consent category (TBC — see open item 3)
25	         │
26	         ▼
27	PWA injects Crazy Egg snippet in the page <head>
28	         │
29	         ▼
30	Crazy Egg begins heatmap and session recording per the Crazy Egg app configuration
31	```
32	
33	## 3. Authentication and credentials
34	
35	**[Zimmermann-provided — Dani, 11 Jun 2026 (Do not remove)]**
36	
37	```html
38	<script type="text/javascript" src="//script.crazyegg.com/pages/scripts/0120/6243.js" async="async"></script>
39	```
40	
41	| Field | Value |
42	|---|---|
43	| Account ID | `0120` |
44	| Site ID | `6243` |
45	
46	- Crazy Egg account / site ID — public, embedded in the snippet. No server-side secret at the storefront layer.
47	- Dani's understanding is that this account is used on **zimmermann.com production only** due to a limited subscription. Courtney to confirm — see open item 1.

50	
51	The storefront must populate `window.dataLayer` with the following before the snippet fires (AAB-002 + AAB-005):
52	
53	| Attribute | Notes |
54	|---|---|
55	| Page type | Used by Crazy Egg for per-page segmentation and suppression |
56	| Authenticated state | Logged-in or guest |

61	## 5. Masking requirements
62	
63	Crazy Egg session recordings must never capture payment or PII fields. Tell No Lies applies masking configuration inside the Crazy Egg app. The PWA's responsibility is to make that configuration reliable:
64	
65	- Render payment fields (card number, CVV, gift card number, gift card PIN) and PII fields (email, phone, address) with **stable, predictable selectors** — consistent `data-*` attributes or stable class names that the masking config can target across builds.
66	- Do not render sensitive data in canvas, SVG, or other elements that CSS-based masking cannot reach.
67	- Do not dynamically generate or rotate field identifiers in a way that breaks the masking selector between releases.
68	
69	## 6. Consent
70	
71	The snippet loads only after Didomi grants the relevant consent category (TBC — Zimmermann Privacy to confirm; expected Analytics). If consent is denied or undetermined the snippet does not load and nothing is recorded. Fail closed: on unknown consent state, do not load.

# 16 — Crazy Egg (Heatmaps & Session Recording)

## 1. Purpose and scope

Crazy Egg provides heatmaps and session recordings for behavioural analysis across all Zimmermann storefronts. It runs as a **frontend-direct** script — not through GTM or Addingwell (AAB-005). The PWA loads the snippet in the page `<head>` so capture begins from page load. The snippet is gated on Didomi consent (category TBC — Zimmermann Privacy to confirm; expected Analytics).

PWA obligations:

- Inject the Crazy Egg snippet in the page `<head>`, after Didomi consent, so capture begins from page load (AAB-005)
- Populate the data layer with page type, authenticated state, and storefront region so Crazy Egg can segment and suppress recordings (AAB-002 + AAB-005)
- Render payment and PII fields with stable, maskable selectors so Tell No Lies can reliably target them for suppression in the Crazy Egg app (see §5)

Segmentation, suppression, and masking configuration sit in the Crazy Egg application, owned by Tell No Lies outside the PWA.

## 2. Loading architecture

```
Page load
         │
         ▼
Storefront populates window.dataLayer with page type, auth state, storefront region
         │
         ▼
Didomi grants the relevant consent category (TBC — see open item 3)
         │
         ▼
PWA injects Crazy Egg snippet in the page <head>
         │
         ▼
Crazy Egg begins heatmap and session recording per the Crazy Egg app configuration
```

## 3. Authentication and credentials

**[Zimmermann-provided — Dani, 11 Jun 2026 (Do not remove)]**

```html
<script type="text/javascript" src="//script.crazyegg.com/pages/scripts/0120/6243.js" async="async"></script>
```

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Account ID | `0120` |
| Site ID | `6243` |

- Crazy Egg account / site ID — public, embedded in the snippet. No server-side secret at the storefront layer.
- Dani's understanding is that this account is used on **zimmermann.com production only** due to a limited subscription. Courtney to confirm — see open item 1.

## 4. Data layer

The storefront must populate `window.dataLayer` with the following before the snippet fires (AAB-002 + AAB-005):

| Attribute | Notes |
|---|---|
| Page type | Used by Crazy Egg for per-page segmentation and suppression |
| Authenticated state | Logged-in or guest |
| Storefront region | Which of the seven storefronts |

No raw PII is included. The exact attribute names must be agreed with Tell No Lies as part of the shared data-layer schema confirmation (see GTM open item §13.3 in `openItems.md`).

## 5. Masking requirements

Crazy Egg session recordings must never capture payment or PII fields. Tell No Lies applies masking configuration inside the Crazy Egg app. The PWA's responsibility is to make that configuration reliable:

- Render payment fields (card number, CVV, gift card number, gift card PIN) and PII fields (email, phone, address) with **stable, predictable selectors** — consistent `data-*` attributes or stable class names that the masking config can target across builds.
- Do not render sensitive data in canvas, SVG, or other elements that CSS-based masking cannot reach.
- Do not dynamically generate or rotate field identifiers in a way that breaks the masking selector between releases.

## 6. Consent

The snippet loads only after Didomi grants the relevant consent category (TBC — Zimmermann Privacy to confirm; expected Analytics). If consent is denied or undetermined the snippet does not load and nothing is recorded. Fail closed: on unknown consent state, do not load.

## 7. Performance

The PRD requires the snippet to load in the `<head>` from page load (AAB-005) while remaining non-blocking for LCP. Unlike Optimizely, there is no anti-flicker reason to run the script synchronously before render, so an async injection is the natural approach. The exact load technique must be confirmed during build to satisfy both the head-from-page-load and non-blocking-LCP constraints.

## 8. Failure modes

| Failure | Behaviour |
|---|---|
| Snippet fails to load | No heatmap or session data captured; the storefront is unaffected |
| Consent denied or undetermined | Snippet not loaded; nothing captured |

## 9. Open items

1. **Environment scope.** Script and site ID confirmed by Dani (11 Jun 2026): account `0120`, site `6243`. Dani's understanding is production only (zimmermann.com) due to a limited subscription — **Courtney to confirm** whether any separate account or snippet exists for staging / UAT / SIT.
2. **Masking configuration ownership.** Confirm that Tell No Lies owns and applies the session-recording masking configuration (payment and PII fields suppressed) inside the Crazy Egg application. The storefront-side scope is confirmed (AAB-005): the PWA populates the data layer and renders maskable fields with stable selectors; masking itself is outside the PWA.
3. **Didomi consent category and vendor / feature ID.** Zimmermann Privacy to confirm which Didomi consent category covers Crazy Egg (expected: Analytics). Tell No Lies to then provide the corresponding Didomi vendor or feature ID so the consent-gated loader can be wired correctly.

1	# 17 — Measmerize (Find My Size / Size Guide)
2	
3	## 1. Purpose and scope
4	
5	Measmerize is the third-party sizing widget on the PDP. It powers two surfaces:
6	
7	1. **Find My Size** — takes body measurements from the customer, generates a size recommendation, and updates the CTA to display "Recommended: Size X" (PRD-050).
8	2. **Size guide overlay** — opens as a slide-out without navigating away from the PDP (PRD-053, confirmed — size guide is a Measmerize overlay).
9	
10	The PWA's job is narrow: inject the Measmerize script on PDP, place the required DOM containers, detect whether Measmerize has data for the current product, and fall back to the Contentful-managed size guide if it does not.
11	
12	In scope:
13	- Script injection on PDP (once on first mount, deferred behind LCP)
14	- Placing DOM containers (`#measmerize-button`, `#measmerize-modal`, `#measmerize-recommendation`)
15	- Detecting data availability via custom events and showing or hiding the trigger accordingly
16	- Updating the product code via the Global Object on SPA navigation
17	- Rendering the Contentful size guide as a fallback when Measmerize has no data for the product
18	- Injecting the checkout tracking script on the order confirmation page
19	
20	Out of scope:
21	- Widget configuration in the Measmerize console (Zimmermann and Measmerize own this)
22	- Size guide content — Measmerize owns it where the widget has data; Contentful owns the fallback
23	- Measurement units toggle (cm / inches) — part of the Contentful fallback size guide (PRD-056), not the Measmerize widget
24	
25	## 2. How it works
26	
27	```
28	PDP page mounts
29	        │
30	        ▼
31	PWA injects Measmerize script tag once (deferred — after LCP image)
32	  with data-brand-code, data-product-code (SFCC SKU), data-lang-code, data-country-code
33	        │
34	        ▼
35	Measmerize initialises and checks its data store for this product
36	        │
37	        ├── data exists → fires measmerize.widget.ready
38	        │       │
39	        │       ▼
40	        │   Measmerize mounts the widget in #measmerize-button / #measmerize-modal
41	        │   Customer clicks → Measmerize takes over and renders its overlay
42	        │   Recommendation generated → fires measmerize.widget.recommend
43	        │   PWA reads event.detail.defaultSize to show "Recommended: Size X"
44	        │
45	        └── no data → fires measmerize.widget.unavailable
46	                PWA shows the Contentful size guide link instead
47	                Customer clicks → PWA renders its own slide-out
48	                                  with Contentful content + cm/in toggle
49	```
50	
51	**Integration modes:** Measmerize supports two DOM integration patterns:
52	
53	- **Standard** — place `<div id="measmerize-button">` on the PDP. Measmerize renders and manages its own "Find Your Size" button inside it. Use when no pre-existing size-guide modal exists.
54	- **Modal** — the PWA provides its own CTAs (e.g. separate "Find My Size" and "Size Guide" links). When the customer opens the overlay, the PWA calls `window.measmerize.modal.mount()`, which injects the widget into `<div id="measmerize-modal">`. No `#measmerize-button` div is needed.
55	
56	Both surfaces (Find My Size and Size Guide) point to the same Measmerize widget. The specific integration mode must be confirmed when implementation begins, based on the final Figma design.
57	
58	**Injection pattern:** Inject the script once on first PDP mount inside a `useEffect` with an empty dependency array. Never place it inside a dynamically re-rendered container.
59	
60	**SPA navigation:** When the customer navigates to a different product (no page reload), update the product code via the Global Object:
61	
62	```js
63	window.measmerize.script.productCode = 'NEW_SKU'
64	```
65	
66	`brandCode` cannot be changed at runtime — it requires a page reload.
67	
68	**Button re-mount:** If React re-renders the `#measmerize-button` or `#measmerize-modal` container, call `window.measmerize.button.mount()` or `window.measmerize.modal.mount()` to restore the widget.
69	
70	**SSR pre-check (optional):** To avoid a flash of the wrong UI on first paint, an unauthenticated REST check can determine at SSR time whether Measmerize has data for a product:
71	
72	```
73	GET https://api.client.measmerize.com/integrations/v1/brands/{brandCode}/products/{productCode}
74	```
75	
76	Returns `200` if Measmerize has the product, `404` if not.
77	
78	**Cleanup:** Remove event listeners and the script element on full component unmount.
79	
80	### Key custom events
81	
82	Events are fired on the script element (`document.getElementById('measmerize-script')`):
83	
84	| Event | When it fires | Payload |
85	|---|---|---|
86	| `measmerize.script.ready` | Script loaded with a valid brand code | — |
87	| `measmerize.script.unavailable` | Script loaded with an invalid brand code | — |
88	| `measmerize.widget.ready` | Widget has data for this product and is about to mount | — |
89	| `measmerize.widget.unavailable` | Widget has no data for this product — show Contentful fallback | — |
90	| `measmerize.widget.recommend` | A recommendation was generated | `event.detail.defaultSize`, `event.detail.convertedSize` |
91	| `measmerize.widget.addToCart` | Customer clicked Add to Cart inside the widget | `event.detail.size` |
92	
93	## 3. Credentials and script attributes
94	
95	| Credential / attribute | Value | Sensitivity |
96	|---|---|---|
97	| Script URL | `https://client.measmerize.com/script.js` | Public |
98	| Checkout script URL | `https://client.measmerize.com/checkout.js` | Public |
99	| `data-brand-code` | UUID provided by Measmerize — one production UUID, one staging UUID shared across Dev / SIT / Stage / UAT | Public — open item §5.2 |
100	| `data-product-code` | SFCC product SKU | Not sensitive |
101	| `data-lang-code` | ISO 639-1 language code (e.g. `en`, `fr`) — from storefront locale | Not sensitive |
102	| `data-country-code` | ISO 3166-1 Alpha-2 (e.g. `AU`, `GB`) — from storefront context | Not sensitive |
103	
104	The script tag uses `id="measmerize-script"` and the `async` attribute. No server-side call or MRT proxy is needed; the script is CDN-served and the brand code is a public identifier. All seven storefronts use the widget — `data-lang-code` and `data-country-code` must be set from the storefront context on every PDP.
105	
106	**Checkout tracking script:** Inject `checkout.js` on the order confirmation page only, with `data-brand-code` and `data-order-code` (the SFCC order ID). This enables ML training and return-rate reporting for Measmerize. It is independent of the PDP widget script.
107	
108	## 4. Consent and gating
109	
110	Measmerize sets cookies in three categories:
111	
112	- **Essential** — session and recommendation matching. Cannot be disabled; always set when the script loads.
113	- **Functional / Personalisation** — stored body measurements across PDPs. Disable via `window.measmerize.cookies.disableFunctional()`.
114	- **Analytical** — Google Analytics and Measmerize custom tracking. Disable via `window.measmerize.tracking.disableAnalytics()` and `window.measmerize.tracking.disableCustom()`.
115	
116	The consent approach is an open item (§5.1): whether to load the script freely and disable non-essential tracking via the SDK when consent is denied, or to gate the entire script load behind a Didomi consent category. The implementation must be built so the gate can be switched without changing the injection logic.
117	
118	## 5. Performance
119	
120	The Measmerize script is injected after the LCP image has painted — it is never on the critical paint path. If consent-gated, it loads only after Didomi consent, pushing the load further off the critical path. The Contentful fallback size guide loads lazily as part of the slide-out component.
121	
122	## 6. Failure modes and graceful degradation
123	
124	| Failure | Behaviour |
125	|---|---|
126	| Script fails to load (CDN outage, network block, consent declined) | Fall back silently to the Contentful size guide. |
127	| Script loads but signals no data (`measmerize.widget.unavailable`) | Show the Contentful size guide link. This is the expected path for some products. |
128	| Contentful size guide also unavailable | Hide the size guide entry point entirely. Do not show a broken overlay. |
129	| Measmerize overlay fails to open after customer click | Show a toast: "Size guide temporarily unavailable." The purchase flow is never blocked on sizing. |
130	
131	## 7. Open items requiring client confirmation
132	
133	1. **Consent approach.** Zimmermann privacy / legal to confirm which of two approaches applies: (a) load the script freely and call `window.measmerize.tracking.disableAnalytics()` / `disableCustom()` / `cookies.disableFunctional()` when consent is denied (Essential cookies always run), or (b) gate the entire script load behind a Didomi consent category. This is a **blocking** decision. If approach (b) is chosen, Zimmermann Privacy to also confirm the Didomi consent category and Tell No Lies to supply the corresponding Didomi vendor / feature ID. **Owner:** Zimmermann.
134	
135	2. **Brand code UUIDs.** Measmerize issues exactly two brand codes per retailer: one for production and one shared across all non-production environments (Dev / SIT / Stage / UAT). Measmerize to supply both values to be set as MRT environment variables. **Owner:** Zimmermann / Measmerize.

1	# 18 — Vimeo (Product and Editorial Video)
2	
3	## 1. Purpose and scope
4	
5	Vimeo hosts video content embedded in the Zimmermann storefront at two surfaces:
6	
7	1. **Product video on PDP** — runway and campaign clips in the product gallery (PRD-066, PRD-067).
8	2. **Editorial video on content pages** — brand and campaign video referenced via embed URL in Contentful CMS entries (HPC-003, HPC-004).
9	
10	**Vimeo as the video platform is not yet confirmed (PRD-067 open).** This doc is provisional until that decision is made — see open item §6.1.
11	
12	The PWA's job is to embed the Vimeo player as a facade-loaded iframe and apply the correct privacy posture per the confirmed consent approach (§4). All other concerns — video hosting, transcoding, CDN delivery, player configuration — are owned by Vimeo and Zimmermann.
13	
14	In scope:
15	- Facade-loaded Vimeo iframe embed on PDP and editorial/content pages
16	- Applying `dnt=1` or Didomi consent gating per the confirmed approach (§4)
17	- Adding `player.vimeo.com` to the `Content-Security-Policy` `frame-src` directive
18	- Graceful fallback when Vimeo is unavailable or an embed URL is missing
19	
20	Out of scope:
21	- Video upload, hosting, and management in Vimeo (Zimmermann)
22	- Player configuration (colours, controls, autoplay) — set via embed URL parameters or Vimeo account settings
23	
24	## 2. How it works
25	
26	```
27	Page renders
28	        │
29	        ▼
30	PWA renders a lightweight facade:
31	  • poster image (lazy-loaded, correct aspect ratio)
32	  • play button overlay
33	  • no Vimeo JS loaded yet
34	        │
35	        ▼
36	Customer clicks play (or video scrolls into view for muted autoplay hero clips)
37	        │
38	        ▼
39	PWA swaps facade for the Vimeo iframe embed URL
40	  (with ?dnt=1, or standard URL gated behind consent, per confirmed approach — §4)
41	        │
42	        ▼
43	Vimeo player loads and begins playback
44	```
45	
46	**PDP:** the embed URL is stored in product data (sourced from Contentful or SFCC product attributes — content ownership is a Contentful open item, openItems §2.2).
47	
48	**Editorial pages:** the CMS author pastes the Vimeo share URL into a Contentful field. The PWA reads and embeds it.
49	
50	No authentication or credentials are required. The embed URL is a public Vimeo player URL — no server-side call or MRT proxy is needed.
51	
52	## 3. Performance
53	
54	- The facade keeps the Vimeo player JS entirely off the critical path. The player loads only on click or on scroll-into-view (muted autoplay hero clips only).
55	- The poster image is lazy-loaded and served at the correct display size from the Contentful Images API or the Vimeo thumbnail API. Never serve full-resolution frames at thumbnail dimensions.
56	- If consent approach (b) is chosen and consent has not been granted, the facade stays visible — no additional performance impact from a deferred load.
57	
58	## 4. Consent and gating
59	
60	Vimeo's standard embed sets analytics and tracking cookies unless the `dnt=1` query parameter is appended (`https://player.vimeo.com/video/{id}?dnt=1`). With `dnt=1`, Vimeo suppresses all tracking cookies and no Didomi gate is needed.
61	
62	Two possible approaches:
63	
64	- **(a) Always use `dnt=1`** — no consent gate required. The facade swaps in the `?dnt=1` URL unconditionally. Simpler implementation.
65	- **(b) Standard embed gated behind Didomi consent** — without consent the facade stays visible. With consent, the standard embed URL loads. Tell No Lies to supply the Didomi vendor / feature ID.

# 18 — Vimeo (Product and Editorial Video)

## 1. Purpose and scope

Vimeo hosts video content embedded in the Zimmermann storefront at two surfaces:

1. **Product video on PDP** — runway and campaign clips in the product gallery (PRD-066, PRD-067).
2. **Editorial video on content pages** — brand and campaign video referenced via embed URL in Contentful CMS entries (HPC-003, HPC-004).

**Vimeo as the video platform is not yet confirmed (PRD-067 open).** This doc is provisional until that decision is made — see open item §6.1.

The PWA's job is to embed the Vimeo player as a facade-loaded iframe and apply the correct privacy posture per the confirmed consent approach (§4). All other concerns — video hosting, transcoding, CDN delivery, player configuration — are owned by Vimeo and Zimmermann.

In scope:
- Facade-loaded Vimeo iframe embed on PDP and editorial/content pages
- Applying `dnt=1` or Didomi consent gating per the confirmed approach (§4)
- Adding `player.vimeo.com` to the `Content-Security-Policy` `frame-src` directive
- Graceful fallback when Vimeo is unavailable or an embed URL is missing

Out of scope:
- Video upload, hosting, and management in Vimeo (Zimmermann)
- Player configuration (colours, controls, autoplay) — set via embed URL parameters or Vimeo account settings

## 2. How it works

```
Page renders
        │
        ▼
PWA renders a lightweight facade:
  • poster image (lazy-loaded, correct aspect ratio)
  • play button overlay
  • no Vimeo JS loaded yet
        │
        ▼
Customer clicks play (or video scrolls into view for muted autoplay hero clips)
        │
        ▼
PWA swaps facade for the Vimeo iframe embed URL
  (with ?dnt=1, or standard URL gated behind consent, per confirmed approach — §4)
        │
        ▼
Vimeo player loads and begins playback
```

**PDP:** the embed URL is stored in product data (sourced from Contentful or SFCC product attributes — content ownership is a Contentful open item, openItems §2.2).

**Editorial pages:** the CMS author pastes the Vimeo share URL into a Contentful field. The PWA reads and embeds it.

No authentication or credentials are required. The embed URL is a public Vimeo player URL — no server-side call or MRT proxy is needed.

## 3. Performance

- The facade keeps the Vimeo player JS entirely off the critical path. The player loads only on click or on scroll-into-view (muted autoplay hero clips only).
- The poster image is lazy-loaded and served at the correct display size from the Contentful Images API or the Vimeo thumbnail API. Never serve full-resolution frames at thumbnail dimensions.
- If consent approach (b) is chosen and consent has not been granted, the facade stays visible — no additional performance impact from a deferred load.

## 4. Consent and gating

Vimeo's standard embed sets analytics and tracking cookies unless the `dnt=1` query parameter is appended (`https://player.vimeo.com/video/{id}?dnt=1`). With `dnt=1`, Vimeo suppresses all tracking cookies and no Didomi gate is needed.

Two possible approaches:

- **(a) Always use `dnt=1`** — no consent gate required. The facade swaps in the `?dnt=1` URL unconditionally. Simpler implementation.
- **(b) Standard embed gated behind Didomi consent** — without consent the facade stays visible. With consent, the standard embed URL loads. Tell No Lies to supply the Didomi vendor / feature ID.

**This is a blocking open item (§6.1).** The implementation supports either path without structural change; only the embed URL construction and the optional consent-gate wrapper differ.

Fail closed: if consent state cannot be determined and approach (b) is chosen, the facade stays — no Vimeo iframe loads.

## 5. Failure modes and graceful degradation

| Failure | Behaviour |
|---|---|
| Vimeo CDN unavailable or iframe fails to load | Facade poster image stays visible. Do not show an error; do not break the page layout. |
| Embed URL missing from product data or CMS entry | Omit the video from the PDP gallery or the video section from the editorial page. No broken placeholder. |
| Consent approach (b): customer declines consent | Facade stays visible with no play affordance, or a brief inline "Enable analytics cookies to watch" message — design decision. Never block the surrounding page. |

## 6. Open items requiring client confirmation

1. **Consent approach.** Zimmermann privacy / legal to confirm: (a) always append `dnt=1` to the embed URL — no Didomi gate needed; or (b) load the standard embed gated behind a Didomi consent category — Tell No Lies to supply the Didomi vendor / feature ID. This is a **blocking** decision. **Owner:** Zimmermann.

2. **Vimeo platform confirmation (PRD-067).** The Third Party Integrations sheet lists Vimeo as the video platform, but PRD-067 is explicitly open: "Vimeo has not been 100% confirmed — open action to confirm best solution for smoothest FE experience." Zimmermann to confirm Vimeo as the platform before PDP video implementation begins. **Owner:** Zimmermann.

=== weekly-agents.yml ===
name: Weekly Agents

on:
  schedule:
    - cron: '0 1 * * 1'   # Every Monday at 1am UTC (after upstream-release-watch at midnight)
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  contents: read
  issues: write
  pull-requests: read

jobs:
  quality-sweep:
    name: Quality sweep — missing tests or stories
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Find components and hooks without paired tests/stories
        id: sweep
        run: |
          missing=()

          # Components under overrides/app/components/ — TypeScript only per AGENTS.md.
          # Per Zimmermann convention every UI component must have a paired .stories.tsx;
          # a .test.ts(x) is required for logic-heavy components but not for every leaf.
          # Flag any component file that lacks BOTH a story and a test.
          while IFS= read -r file; do
            base="${file%.*}"
            dir=$(dirname "$file")
            name=$(basename "$base")
            found=false
            # Check for paired test or story (same basename or co-located in the same folder)
            for t in "${base}.test.ts" "${base}.test.tsx" "${base}.stories.tsx" \
                     "${dir}/${name}.test.ts" "${dir}/${name}.test.tsx" "${dir}/${name}.stories.tsx" \
                     "${dir}/index.test.ts" "${dir}/index.test.tsx" "${dir}/index.stories.tsx"; do
              [[ -f "$t" ]] && found=true && break
            done
            $found || missing+=("$file")
          done < <(find overrides/app/components \
            \( -name "index.tsx" -o -name "index.ts" \) \
            ! -path "*/node_modules/*" 2>/dev/null | sort)

          # Hooks: look for use-*.ts (override convention keeps kebab-case) and useFoo.ts
          # (Zimmermann camelCase convention) without a paired test file.
          while IFS= read -r file; do
            base="${file%.*}"
            found=false
            for t in "${base}.test.ts" "${base}.test.tsx"; do
              [[ -f "$t" ]] && found=true && break
            done
            $found || missing+=("$file")
          done < <(find overrides/app/hooks \
            \( -name "use-*.ts" -o -name "use[A-Z]*.ts" \) \
            ! -path "*/node_modules/*" 2>/dev/null | sort)

          # Write results
          COUNT=${#missing[@]}
          echo "count=$COUNT" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT

          if [[ $COUNT -gt 0 ]]; then
            printf '%s\n' "${missing[@]}" > /tmp/missing-tests.txt
            echo "has_missing=true" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
          else
            echo "has_missing=false" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
          fi

      - name: Check for existing open quality-sweep issue
        id: existing
        if: steps.sweep.outputs.has_missing == 'true'
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
        run: |
          NUM=$(gh issue list \
            --label "quality-sweep" \
            --state open \
            --json number \
            --jq '.[0].number // empty')
          echo "number=$NUM" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT

      - name: Create or update quality sweep issue
        if: steps.sweep.outputs.has_missing == 'true'
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
        run: |
          COUNT="${{ steps.sweep.outputs.count }}"
          DATE=$(date +%Y-%m-%d)

          # Format the missing files list as a checklist
          CHECKLIST=""
          while IFS= read -r file; do
            short="${file#overrides/}"
            CHECKLIST="${CHECKLIST}- [ ] \`${short}\`"$'\n'
          done < /tmp/missing-tests.txt

          BODY=$(cat <<EOF
          ## Weekly Quality Sweep — $DATE

          **$COUNT** component/hook file(s) are missing a paired test or story.

          ### Files without tests or stories

          $CHECKLIST

          ### How to fix

          - Components: add a \`.stories.tsx\` (required) and a \`.test.ts(x)\` if the component has logic worth testing — see AGENTS.md > Testing.
          - Hooks: add a paired \`.test.ts\`.

          Run \`/code-quality\` in a Claude Code session to get specific test case suggestions.

          ---
          *Updated automatically by the weekly-agents workflow.*
          *Close this issue once all items are checked off.*
          EOF
          )

          EXISTING="${{ steps.existing.outputs.number }}"
          if [[ -n "$EXISTING" ]]; then
            gh issue edit "$EXISTING" \
              --title "Quality sweep: $COUNT files missing tests/stories ($DATE)" \
              --body "$BODY"
            echo "Updated existing issue #$EXISTING"
          else
            gh issue create \
              --title "Quality sweep: $COUNT files missing tests/stories ($DATE)" \
              --label "quality-sweep,tech-debt" \
              --body "$BODY"
          fi

      - name: All tests/stories present
        if: steps.sweep.outputs.has_missing == 'false'
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
        run: |
          echo "✅ All components and hooks have paired tests or stories."

          # Close any open quality-sweep issue if everything is now covered
          EXISTING=$(gh issue list \
            --label "quality-sweep" \
            --state open \
            --json number \
            --jq '.[0].number // empty')
          if [[ -n "$EXISTING" ]]; then
            gh issue close "$EXISTING" \
              --comment "✅ All files now have test/story coverage. Closing automatically."
          fi

  contentful-drift-audit:
    name: Contentful drift audit
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Check for definition files without paired components
        id: audit
        run: |
          issues=()

          # Find all ContentfulDefinition.ts files under overrides/app/components/
          while IFS= read -r def_file; do
            dir=$(dirname "$def_file")
            base=$(basename "$def_file" ContentfulDefinition.ts)

            # Check for a paired component file
            found=false
            for ext in tsx ts; do
              [[ -f "${dir}/${base}.${ext}" ]] && found=true && break
              [[ -f "${dir}/index.${ext}" ]] && found=true && break
            done

            $found || issues+=("Orphaned definition (no paired component): $def_file")
          done < <(find overrides/app/components \
            -name "*ContentfulDefinition.ts" \
            ! -path "*/node_modules/*" 2>/dev/null | sort)

          COUNT=${#issues[@]}
          echo "count=$COUNT" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT

          if [[ $COUNT -gt 0 ]]; then
            printf '%s\n' "${issues[@]}" > /tmp/contentful-issues.txt
            echo "has_issues=true" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
          else
            echo "has_issues=false" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
          fi

      - name: Report Contentful audit results
        if: steps.audit.outputs.has_issues == 'true'
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
        run: |
          DATE=$(date +%Y-%m-%d)
          COUNT="${{ steps.audit.outputs.count }}"

          ITEMS=""
          while IFS= read -r issue; do
            ITEMS="${ITEMS}- [ ] ${issue}"$'\n'
          done < /tmp/contentful-issues.txt

          EXISTING=$(gh issue list \
            --label "contentful-drift" \
            --state open \
            --json number \

=== weekly-agents.yml ===
name: Weekly Agents

on:
  schedule:
    - cron: '0 1 * * 1'   # Every Monday at 1am UTC (after upstream-release-watch at midnight)
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  contents: read
  issues: write
  pull-requests: read

jobs:
  quality-sweep:
    name: Quality sweep — missing tests or stories
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Find components and hooks without paired tests/stories
        id: sweep
        run: |
          missing=()

          # Components under overrides/app/components/ — TypeScript only per AGENTS.md.
          # Per Zimmermann convention every UI component must have a paired .stories.tsx;
          # a .test.ts(x) is required for logic-heavy components but not for every leaf.
          # Flag any component file that lacks BOTH a story and a test.
          while IFS= read -r file; do
            base="${file%.*}"
            dir=$(dirname "$file")
            name=$(basename "$base")
            found=false
            # Check for paired test or story (same basename or co-located in the same folder)
            for t in "${base}.test.ts" "${base}.test.tsx" "${base}.stories.tsx" \
                     "${dir}/${name}.test.ts" "${dir}/${name}.test.tsx" "${dir}/${name}.stories.tsx" \
                     "${dir}/index.test.ts" "${dir}/index.test.tsx" "${dir}/index.stories.tsx"; do
              [[ -f "$t" ]] && found=true && break
            done
            $found || missing+=("$file")
          done < <(find overrides/app/components \
            \( -name "index.tsx" -o -name "index.ts" \) \
            ! -path "*/node_modules/*" 2>/dev/null | sort)

          # Hooks: look for use-*.ts (override convention keeps kebab-case) and useFoo.ts
          # (Zimmermann camelCase convention) without a paired test file.
          while IFS= read -r file; do
            base="${file%.*}"
            found=false
            for t in "${base}.test.ts" "${base}.test.tsx"; do
              [[ -f "$t" ]] && found=true && break
            done
            $found || missing+=("$file")
          done < <(find overrides/app/hooks \
            \( -name "use-*.ts" -o -name "use[A-Z]*.ts" \) \
            ! -path "*/node_modules/*" 2>/dev/null | sort)

          # Write results
          COUNT=${#missing[@]}
          echo "count=$COUNT" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT

          if [[ $COUNT -gt 0 ]]; then
            printf '%s\n' "${missing[@]}" > /tmp/missing-tests.txt
            echo "has_missing=true" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
          else
            echo "has_missing=false" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
          fi

      - name: Check for existing open quality-sweep issue
        id: existing
        if: steps.sweep.outputs.has_missing == 'true'
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
        run: |
          NUM=$(gh issue list \
            --label "quality-sweep" \
            --state open \
            --json number \
            --jq '.[0].number // empty')
          echo "number=$NUM" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT

      - name: Create or update quality sweep issue
        if: steps.sweep.outputs.has_missing == 'true'
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
        run: |
          COUNT="${{ steps.sweep.outputs.count }}"
          DATE=$(date +%Y-%m-%d)

          # Format the missing files list as a checklist
          CHECKLIST=""
          while IFS= read -r file; do
            short="${file#overrides/}"
            CHECKLIST="${CHECKLIST}- [ ] \`${short}\`"$'\n'
          done < /tmp/missing-tests.txt

          BODY=$(cat <<EOF
          ## Weekly Quality Sweep — $DATE

          **$COUNT** component/hook file(s) are missing a paired test or story.

          ### Files without tests or stories

          $CHECKLIST

          ### How to fix

          - Components: add a \`.stories.tsx\` (required) and a \`.test.ts(x)\` if the component has logic worth testing — see AGENTS.md > Testing.
          - Hooks: add a paired \`.test.ts\`.

          Run \`/code-quality\` in a Claude Code session to get specific test case suggestions.

          ---
          *Updated automatically by the weekly-agents workflow.*
          *Close this issue once all items are checked off.*
          EOF
          )

          EXISTING="${{ steps.existing.outputs.number }}"
          if [[ -n "$EXISTING" ]]; then
            gh issue edit "$EXISTING" \
              --title "Quality sweep: $COUNT files missing tests/stories ($DATE)" \
              --body "$BODY"
            echo "Updated existing issue #$EXISTING"
          else
            gh issue create \
              --title "Quality sweep: $COUNT files missing tests/stories ($DATE)" \
              --label "quality-sweep,tech-debt" \
              --body "$BODY"
          fi

      - name: All tests/stories present
        if: steps.sweep.outputs.has_missing == 'false'
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
        run: |
          echo "✅ All components and hooks have paired tests or stories."

          # Close any open quality-sweep issue if everything is now covered
          EXISTING=$(gh issue list \
            --label "quality-sweep" \
            --state open \
            --json number \
            --jq '.[0].number // empty')
          if [[ -n "$EXISTING" ]]; then
            gh issue close "$EXISTING" \
              --comment "✅ All files now have test/story coverage. Closing automatically."
          fi

  contentful-drift-audit:
    name: Contentful drift audit
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Check for definition files without paired components
        id: audit
        run: |

            found=false
            for ext in tsx ts; do

              [[ -f "${dir}/index.${ext}" ]] && found=true && break

            -name "*ContentfulDefinition.ts" \

        env:

        run: |

          ITEMS=""
          while IFS= read -r issue; do
            ITEMS="${ITEMS}- [ ] ${issue}"$'\n'
          done < /tmp/contentful-issues.txt

          EXISTING=$(gh issue list \
            --label "contentful-drift" \
            --state open \
            --json number \
            --jq '.[0].number // empty')

          BODY=$(cat <<EOF

          **$COUNT** structural issue(s) found in Contentful component definitions.

          ### Issues found

          $ITEMS

          ### Next steps

          Run \`/contentful-drift-check\` in a Claude Code session for a detailed
          prop-level comparison between component interfaces and their Contentful definitions.

          ---
          *Note: This automated check detects structural issues (orphaned files, missing pairs).*
          *Prop-level drift requires running \`/contentful-drift-check\` manually.*
          *Updated automatically by the weekly-agents workflow.*
          EOF
          )

          if [[ -n "$EXISTING" ]]; then
            gh issue edit "$EXISTING" \

              --body "$BODY"
          else

          fi

      - name: No Contentful drift issues

          if [[ -n "$EXISTING" ]]; then

=== .claude/hooks/ dir ===
.claude/hooks/tier2Warn.sh
.claude/hooks/registryUpdate.sh
.claude/hooks/contentfulDriftWarn.sh
.claude/hooks/testFileRemind.sh
.claude/hooks/session-reflect.sh
=== session-reflect.sh (if exists) ===
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Stop hook: ask Claude to reflect on the session and draft proposals
# for AGENTS.md, .docs/memory/*, and any other docs that may have drifted.
# Proposals are written to .docs/agents-proposals/ — NEVER edits docs directly.
set -euo pipefail

input=$(cat)

# Re-entry guard: if a Stop hook already ran this turn, do nothing.
active=$(echo "$input" | jq -r '.stop_hook_active // false')
[ "$active" = "true" ] && exit 0

branch=$(git branch --show-current 2>/dev/null || echo "no-branch")

# Skip only if nothing changed this session — otherwise always reflect,
# regardless of branch (develop/main/release included, just in case).
if [ -z "$(git status --porcelain 2>/dev/null)" ]; then
  exit 0
fi

ts=$(date +%Y%m%d-%H%M%S)
proposal_path=".docs/agents-proposals/${ts}-${branch//\//-}.md"

jq -n --arg path "$proposal_path" '{
  decision: "block",
  reason: ("Before ending this session, reflect on what changed and draft any documentation updates. " +
    "Write a SINGLE proposal file to " + $path + " (create the directory if needed). " +
    "Do NOT edit AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, .docs/memory/*, .docs/prd/*, or .claude/rules/* directly — those are Tier 1 / human-owned. " +
    "The proposal file should contain one section per doc you think needs updating, each with: " +
    "(1) the target file path, (2) a short rationale tied to something that actually happened this session, " +
    "(3) a concrete diff or before/after snippet. " +
    "Candidates to consider — only include the ones that genuinely changed:\n" +
    "  - AGENTS.md (rules, gotchas, unresolved deps)\n" +
    "  - .docs/architecture.md (stack/structural decisions, new integrations, key paths)\n" +
    "  - .docs/memory/projectState.md (phase, integration statuses, completed work)\n" +
    "  - .docs/memory/feedback.md (validated patterns, failed approaches, gotchas)\n" +

2	
3	*Draft for client sign-off. Last updated 2026-06-26. Scope: architecture — stack, customisation model, integrations, regional/multi-site, SSR/SEO, performance, accessibility, testing, CI/CD. Requirement IDs (e.g. DMU-030, REG-041) reference the **Zimmermann Functional Requirements** spreadsheet.*
4	
5	---
6	
7	## 1. Purpose & Scope
8	
9	This TSD describes the technical foundation for the Zimmermann production storefront at www.zimmermann.com — a luxury Australian fashion brand running on Salesforce Commerce Cloud (SFCC) PWA Kit.
10	
11	**In scope:**
12	- Stack and build pipeline
13	- The customisation model on top of `@salesforce/retail-react-app`
14	- Multi-site / multi-locale routing across 7 storefronts in 6 regions
15	- Integration map (SFCC, MuleSoft, Contentful, Global-e, Didomi, Adyen, Omneo, Narvar, GiveX, Google Places)
16	- SSR + SEO foundation (DMU-030, hreflang, sitemaps, structured data)
17	- Performance budgets, accessibility, consent gating, GDPR
18	- Testing strategy and CI/CD topology
19	- Open decisions requiring client input before build
20	
21	**Out of scope:** per-feature functional design; detailed per-vendor integration design
22	
23	---

25	## 2. Solution Overview
26	
27	A single PWA Kit codebase serves 7 logical SFCC sites, each with its own currency, tax model, locale set, delivery options, payment methods, and consent defaults. International checkout is owned by Global-e; domestic checkout is owned by SFCC. All order-creation, fulfilment write, and CRM sync traffic from SFCC routes through **MuleSoft** as the middleware boundary — SFCC does not call NewStore, AP21, Omneo, or Narvar directly. In addition, the PWA's MRT Node layer calls MuleSoft directly (via `/mobify/proxy/mulesoft/...`) for read operations: order history, order details, boutique stock checks (Find in Boutique, Collect in Boutique), GiveX balance check, and real-time stock availability. These reads bypass SFCC entirely.
28	
29	The PWA itself also talks to a handful of services without going through SFCC. Contentful and Didomi are browser-direct. Google Maps (Places API), GiveX balance check (proxied through MuleSoft — see §2 GiveX note), and select MuleSoft operations are called from the PWA's MRT Node layer via proxy, with API credentials held server-side as MRT environment variables.
